name: Four-file state layout under .harness
statement: Ledger state MUST live in exactly four fixed files with one role each: append-only data (ledger.jsonl), anchor (ledger.head.json), intent journal (ledger.pending.json) and lock (ledger.lock).
note: modify: keep the four-role split but place it in a G1-private directory outside the agent-writable workspace, keyed by repository identity.
threat: principle

name: Exact-field v2 record envelope
statement: Every ledger line MUST be a JSON object with exactly the nine envelope fields schema_version, ledger_id, seq, prev_record_hash, event_type, task_id, timestamp, payload, record_hash, each type-checked, else fail closed.
note: keep: a closed envelope makes every receipt mechanically checkable without trusting the writer's intent.
threat: Smuggled extra fields, missing fields or type-confused values silently changing a receipt's meaning.

name: Byte-canonical line encoding
statement: The stored bytes of every record, head and journal MUST equal canonical_json(value) plus one LF exactly (sorted keys, no whitespace, raw UTF-8), so each value has exactly one encoding.
note: modify: keep byte-canonicality but specify it as RFC 8785 JCS or an ASCII-key, integer-only subset, because Python key sort and float repr are not reproducible in a TS/Bun omp extension.
threat: Encoding malleability (whitespace, key order, unicode escapes, 1e0 vs 1.0, CRLF, missing final LF) hiding edits or giving one record several byte forms.

name: Strict JSON decoder rejects ambiguity
statement: Decoding MUST reject a UTF-8 BOM, invalid UTF-8, duplicate object keys, NaN/Infinity, a non-object top level and parser recursion overflow, all with one typed code.
note: modify: JS JSON.parse silently keeps the last duplicate key and loses big integers, so G1 needs a strict parser or pre-scan to keep this guarantee.
threat: Parser differentials (duplicate-key last-wins vs first-wins) letting two readers see different receipts; NaN/Infinity breaking comparisons.

name: Exact ranged integers only
statement: Integer fields MUST be exact integers (never bool, float or string) within +/-(2^63-1), and integer literals longer than 19 digits are rejected before conversion.
note: modify: keep the no-bool/no-float rule but cap at 2^53-1 (Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER) or parse as BigInt in TypeScript.
threat: Type confusion (True == 1, 1.0 == 1) forging sequence, offset or binding values; CPU exhaustion from huge integer literals.

name: Whitelisted JSON values with depth cap
statement: Every value read or written MUST be null, bool, int, finite float, surrogate-free string, list or string-keyed dict, nested at most 64 deep, with no cycles or shared sub-objects.
note: modify: keep the closed value model but drop floats entirely; G1 receipts need only integers, strings, booleans and hex digests.
threat: Unencodable values (lone surrogates) crashing hashing, non-string keys silently coerced, deep-nesting DoS, cyclic payloads.

name: 64 KiB record cap before parse/write
statement: A record line including its LF MUST NOT exceed 65,536 bytes; oversize lines are rejected before parsing on read and before the journal is written on append.
note: keep: bounded records keep verification cost predictable; store large evidence (stdout, manifests) out of line by digest.
threat: Memory/CPU exhaustion from huge lines; unbounded journals; oversize records half-written.

name: Exact derived head and journal size bounds
statement: Head and journal files MUST be size-checked against exact maxima derived from maximal-value templates (274 B head, 88,364 B journal) before they are read.
note: keep: deriving limits from the schema is exact and self-maintaining.
threat: Oversized or garbage control files causing memory blowup or slow parsing before validation runs.

name: Strict identifier and format validators
statement: Identifiers MUST use one exact lowercase spelling: canonical uuid4, 64-hex SHA-256, calendar-valid YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.mmmZ, task id [a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,63}, attempt id v-<32 hex>, git object id of 40-64 hex.
note: keep: single canonical spellings make plain string equality a sound binding check.
threat: Aliased identifiers (uppercase hex, braced uuids, impossible dates) defeating equality-based binding checks.

name: Domain-separated framed record hash
statement: record_hash MUST be SHA-256 over a fixed domain tag, then NUL-framed ledger_id, seq and prev hash, then the canonical JSON of the record without record_hash.
note: modify: keep framing and domain separation with a G1 tag, and consider an HMAC keyed outside the agent's reach to add authenticity.
threat: Cross-context digest confusion (a record hash reused as a manifest or line digest), framing ambiguity, undetected field edits.

name: Contiguous sequence hash chain from genesis
statement: Record n MUST have seq == n and prev_record_hash equal to record n-1's hash (64 zeros for n = 1); any gap, duplicate, reorder or relink fails closed.
note: keep: the chain is the core tamper-evidence primitive for harness-observed events.
threat: Insertion, deletion, duplication or reordering of receipts inside history.

name: Random per-ledger identity in every record
statement: Each ledger MUST carry a random uuid4 ledger_id fixed at genesis that appears in the head, every record, the journal and the hash framing, and must match everywhere.
note: keep: cheap anti-splice binding, but it is public, so it adds no authenticity.
threat: Splicing records or heads from another ledger (cross-repository replay of a valid completion).

name: Head anchor binds count, tail hash, length
statement: A separate head file MUST record last_seq, last_record_hash and last_record_end_offset, and verification fails unless file size, record count, tail hash and parsed length all equal it.
note: modify: keep the anchor but also hold its (seq, hash) in extension memory and a G1-private store so a consistent ledger+head rollback is caught.
threat: Silent tail truncation (deleting an invalidation or failed receipt), unanchored appended lines (echo >> ledger), prefix replacement, head-only rollback.

name: Head schema with genesis consistency
statement: The head MUST be canonical, size-bounded and exact-field, with last_seq 0 iff the hash is 64 zeros and the offset is 0, and a nonzero seq implying a nonzero hash and offset.
note: keep: a small, fully specified control record.
threat: Malformed or forged heads claiming emptiness for a non-empty ledger or the reverse.

name: O(1) first-line and tail check on append
statement: Before appending, the writer MUST confirm file size equals the anchor, line 1 is a valid genesis-linked v2 record, and the tail record is valid, canonical and equal to the head hash.
note: keep: O(1) appends suit per-tool-call receipts, provided a full verify runs at every trust decision because middle corruption is invisible to append.
threat: Extending a ledger whose tail or anchor has been tampered with or torn.

name: Write-ahead intent journal
statement: Before touching the ledger, the writer MUST durably write a journal holding old head, new head, intended seq and hash, and the exact line bytes as base64 plus their SHA-256.
note: keep: it makes every post-anchor byte explainable, which lets G1 treat unexplained bytes as tampering.
threat: A crash leaving bytes beyond the anchor that cannot be told apart from tampering.

name: Strict durable commit order
statement: An append MUST run journal durable, then O_APPEND write plus ledger fsync, then atomic head replace plus directory fsync, then journal unlink plus directory fsync, so the anchor never points past durable data.
note: keep: standard WAL ordering; Bun/Node fsyncSync and renameSync give the same guarantees on Linux.
threat: An anchor referencing data lost on power failure; torn appends.

name: Recovery infers phase from durable state
statement: Recovery MUST classify a journaled append only by exact comparison of current head and ledger bytes with the journal (aborted, committed, finalized); every other state is blocked.
note: keep: state-derived recovery is simpler and more robust than recording phases.
threat: Guessing the recovery direction from partial evidence and committing a forged or partial record.

name: Exact-match recovery, never truncate or rebuild
statement: Recovery MUST NOT truncate, rewrite or reconstruct the ledger; torn records, mismatched bytes or an unknown head block with ledger_recovery_blocked, and the full chain is re-validated before the journal is resolved.
note: keep: fail closed over repair; truncating a torn tail that is a byte-exact prefix of the journaled line is a provably safe experiment.
threat: Recovery used as a laundering path to rewrite history; data loss from automatic repair.

name: Pending journal blocks reads and appends
statement: While a journal exists, every read and append MUST fail with ledger_pending_recovery until an explicit recover() resolves it.
note: modify: because recovery is exact-match only, the G1 extension can run it automatically at session start instead of waiting for an operator.
threat: Consumers trusting a ledger that is mid-transaction and ambiguous.

name: Journal self-consistency validation
statement: A journal MUST be exact-field, canonical and size-bounded, internally consistent (ids, seq+1, hashes, offsets), carry strictly canonical base64 whose decoded line matches its digest and links to the old head, and hold a current-schema event.
note: keep: the journal is an injection surface and needs validation as strict as the ledger's.
threat: A crafted journal used to inject a record (including a retired event) through recover().

name: Post-durable failures typed as incomplete
statement: Once the journal is durable, any typed failure MUST surface as ledger_transaction_incomplete, and post-commit success is reported only when the journal is verifiably gone.
note: modify: keep the typing but surface cleanup warnings to the operator, which T1 silently drops.
threat: A caller believing an append failed cleanly (and retrying) or succeeded while state is ambiguous.

name: Named crash-injection points
statement: The append path SHOULD expose named fault points so every crash boundary can be exercised deterministically.
note: keep: a cheap seam that turns crash-consistency claims into reproducible evidence.
threat: principle

name: Atomic replace with inode verification
statement: Control files MUST be replaced by writing an O_EXCL temp file in the same directory, fsyncing it, renaming it, confirming the target now has the temp's inode, and fsyncing the directory.
note: keep: portable to Bun/Node (openSync 'wx', fsyncSync, renameSync, fstatSync with bigint ino).
threat: Torn head or journal writes; a concurrent swap of the target between rename and use.

name: Directory fsync after namespace changes
statement: After a create, rename or unlink in the ledger directory, the directory itself MUST be fsynced.
note: keep: required for real durability on Linux; macOS needs F_FULLFSYNC for an equivalent guarantee.
threat: Renames or unlinks lost on power failure, reviving stale heads or journals.

name: Short writes retried, I/O failures typed
statement: Writes MUST loop until every byte is written (zero progress is an error), and write and fsync failures MUST map to typed codes.
note: keep: trivial and necessary.
threat: Silent partial writes; untyped crashes that leave operators guessing.

name: No-follow single-link regular-file opens
statement: Every ledger, head, journal and lock open MUST refuse symlinks, hardlinked (nlink != 1) or non-regular files and detect path/inode swaps around the open; without O_NOFOLLOW the ledger refuses to operate.
note: modify: keep the nofollow, nlink and inode checks (Node exposes O_NOFOLLOW and fstat ino/nlink) but re-verify the directory inode after each operation, since Node has no openat.
threat: Symlink redirection to files outside the repo, hardlink aliasing so edits elsewhere change the ledger, a planted FIFO hanging opens, swap races.

name: Private modes enforced on write paths
statement: Ledger files MUST be mode 0600 and the ledger directory 0700, enforced on every write-path open.
note: modify: also verify mode and st_uid on read; against a same-user agent modes add nothing, so pair them with state stored outside the workspace.
threat: Other local users reading or modifying receipts.

name: Zero-write read paths
statement: read(), verify() and status() MUST NOT create, chmod or modify any file, including the lock file and the directory.
note: keep: in an evidence-only harness, observation must never perturb the observed state.
threat: Observers mutating evidence, e.g. creating files that change later pristine-state proofs.

name: Exclusive flock serializes all mutations
statement: Every mutation (append, genesis, recover, and caller read-validate-append sequences) MUST hold an exclusive flock on a never-unlinked lock file for the whole operation, fsyncs included.
note: modify: Bun/Node core has no flock, so use an in-process async mutex (single G1 writer) plus an O_EXCL lockfile or FFI flock across omp instances, with a timeout.
threat: Concurrent writers interleaving lines or racing sequence numbers.

name: Shared-lock reads, guarded lockless fallback
statement: Readers MUST take a shared flock when the lock file exists; if it does not, they read unlocked and fail with ledger_race if the lock appeared meanwhile.
note: modify: with a single in-process writer G1 can serialize reads behind the writer's mutex; keep the 'lock appeared' post-check for out-of-process readers.
threat: Reading a half-applied append; read paths creating lock files.

name: Check-then-append in one critical section
statement: Lifecycle decisions (status, completion, contract update) MUST read, validate and append under the same exclusive lock so no event can intervene.
note: modify: keep the single critical section but have the ledger cross-check supplied receipts against the head (count and tail hash) instead of trusting the caller.
threat: TOCTOU: a verification start or invalidation landing between completion evaluation and the complete append.

name: Writer allowlist of seven current events
statement: Only the seven current events may be appended, checked before the lock is taken and again inside it.
note: keep: a closed writer vocabulary; G1's events would be harness observations such as command_run, file_hashed, tool_call_recorded.
threat: Writing retired or invented event types that consumers might misinterpret.

name: Legacy events readable-inert, unknown rejected
statement: Six retired event types MUST stay readable with unvalidated payloads (apart from reserved keys) and never be written or recovered; any other event type fails read with ledger_event_unknown.
note: drop: a fresh G1 ledger has no history; keep only the unknown-event rejection.
threat: Retired semantics re-entering the live ledger; unknown future events silently accepted.

name: Payload cannot shadow envelope fields
statement: Payload keys MUST NOT reuse envelope or decoded alias names, and callers MUST NOT supply ledger-minted fields, so flattened receipts cannot be spoofed.
note: keep: required whenever envelope and payload are merged; never flattening is simpler still.
threat: A payload carrying its own seq, record_hash or event that overrides the real values in the flattened view.

name: Current events bind task, contract, receipt id
statement: Every current-event record MUST target a valid task_id and carry a ledger-minted uuid4 receipt_id and a 64-hex contract_hash.
note: modify: keep the task+contract binding but drop receipt_id, which nothing consumes because seq and record_hash already identify a receipt.
threat: Receipts not attributable to a task contract.

name: Exact per-event payload field sets
statement: Each current event's payload keys MUST lie between its required and allowed sets, with optional groups present all-or-none.
note: keep: closed per-event schemas, generated in G1 from one declarative table.
threat: Partial bindings (a seq without its hash) or stray fields altering meaning.

name: Contract registration and update payloads
statement: contract_registered MAY carry bootstrap=true with a nonempty allowed_paths list (both or neither); contract_update_accepted MUST carry a valid old hash different from the new one and a nonempty reason.
note: modify: also enforce at append that old_contract_hash equals the task's currently registered contract; T1 checks only shape.
threat: No-op or malformed contract updates; partial bootstrap scope declarations.

name: Status enum and completion binding shape
statement: task_status_changed status MUST be pending, active, complete or blocked, and the verification_receipt_seq/hash pair is allowed only for complete, with 1 <= seq < the record's own seq.
note: keep: backward-only references keep the chain acyclic and checkable in one pass.
threat: Forward or self references in completion bindings; bindings attached to non-complete states.

name: Bounded single-line invalidation reason
statement: task_invalidated MUST carry a nonempty reason of at most 2048 UTF-8 bytes with no NUL, CR or LF.
note: keep: bound every free-text receipt field this way; T1 does not do so for contract-update reasons.
threat: Log or terminal injection via multi-line reasons; oversized free text.

name: verification_started binds attempt and command
statement: verification_started MUST carry attempt_id v-<32 hex>, a 64-hex public_command_digest and a nonempty workspace; a legacy {command, workspace} shape is also accepted.
note: modify: keep attempt and digest binding, drop the legacy shape, and require every result to pair with a harness-recorded start.
threat: Unattributable verification attempts; command substitution between start and result.

name: verification_succeeded binds evidence snapshot
statement: verification_succeeded MUST have exit_code 0 and bind attempt_id, command digest, manifest path, source digest, git tree id, artifact hashes and timestamp, with optional manifest_content_hash and a stdout/stderr digest pair.
note: modify: make every digest mandatory, drop the legacy and oracle shapes, and compute all digests inside the harness process only.
threat: Success receipts that do not pin what was verified: which tree, which artifacts, which output.

name: verification_failed requires typed failure
statement: verification_failed MUST carry attempt_id, command digest, ranged exit_code, boolean timed_out, nullable manifest and a nonempty failure code.
note: keep: negative evidence must be as well-typed as positive evidence.
threat: Failures recorded without a cause, making invalidation and staleness reasoning impossible.

name: Artifact binding schema
statement: artifact_hashes MUST be a nonempty list of exact {path, type, size, sha256} entries with type file or directory, and directories carry a nonempty entries list of {path, size, sha256}.
note: modify: also require safe relative paths and sorted unique entries, and allow empty directories.
threat: Completion evidence that does not bind artifact content.

name: Completion requires explicit receipt binding
statement: A new task_status_changed to complete MUST include both verification_receipt_seq (int >= 1) and a 64-hex verification_receipt_hash, plus a valid contract hash and task id.
note: keep: the central evidence-only rule, under which 'done' must cite a harness-produced receipt by seq and hash.
threat: Completion claimed without pointing at concrete verification evidence.

name: Binding must hit same-task same-contract success
statement: The bound receipt MUST exist at that seq with that record hash, be verification_succeeded with exit_code 0, and match the completion's task id and contract hash.
note: keep: and re-check the binding on every full verify in G1, not only at append.
threat: Borrowing another task's success, an older contract's success or a failed receipt to claim completion.

name: Later task events make binding stale
statement: A completion binding MUST be refused if any current-schema event for the same task appears after the bound receipt.
note: keep: 'latest evidence wins' is the freshness rule an evidence-only harness needs; derive the frontier set from the event table rather than duplicating it.
threat: Completing on old evidence after a newer verification start or failure, an invalidation, a contract change or a status change.

name: Completed tasks are terminal
statement: Once a task has a complete transition, the ledger MUST refuse non-complete status changes and contract updates (task_reopen_refused) and new verification starts (verification_refused_complete_task).
note: modify: enforce terminality for every event type through an O(1) per-task state index instead of full scans.
threat: Reopening or re-verifying a finished task to change its meaning after the fact.

name: Validate everything before first durable write
statement: All checks (event allowlist, reserved fields, ids, binding, terminal state, record self-validation, size) MUST finish before the journal is written, so a rejected append changes no bytes.
note: keep: zero-write rejection keeps the ledger a pure record of accepted harness observations.
threat: Rejected requests leaving partial artifacts that later look like evidence or block recovery.

name: Writer round-trips through reader validator
statement: The writer MUST validate the record it built with the same validator and canonical-bytes check readers use before persisting it.
note: keep: one validator for both directions removes a whole class of self-inflicted corruption.
threat: Writer/reader skew producing records that later make the whole ledger unreadable.

name: Genesis only from proven-pristine state
statement: With ledger and head both absent, genesis is legitimate only if the plan has zero tasks and no contract markers and .harness holds only allowlisted entries (plan.md, empty lock, evidence/real-codex-smoke, empty private/runtime); otherwise fail with ledger_state_missing and never repair.
note: modify: keep 'missing state is never pristine unless proven', but prove it from G1's own external state registry instead of scanning T1's plan and Codex-specific directories.
threat: Deleting both files to silently restart history and launder failed or invalidated work.

name: Genesis only via explicit first-task begin
statement: Only the explicit first-task path may create genesis, with allow_genesis decided under the exclusive lock; ordinary appends to an uninitialized ledger fail with ledger_uninitialized.
note: modify: keep explicit genesis but journal it so ledger and head appear atomically, closing T1's crash window.
threat: Accidental or attacker-triggered re-initialisation by any writer.

name: One-sided loss typed, never repaired
statement: If exactly one of ledger or head is missing, every surface MUST report ledger_file_missing or ledger_head_missing, and no operation may recreate the missing counterpart.
note: keep: deletion must be as detectable as modification.
threat: Deleting the head to escape anchor checks, or deleting the ledger to have it rebuilt.

name: Schema version gate without migration
statement: A ledger whose first record is not schema v2 MUST be reported ledger_schema_unsupported on read and append and never rewritten or migrated.
note: keep: version the format from day one and treat any migration as a new ledger, never an in-place rewrite.
threat: Silent migrations that rewrite, and could launder, history.

name: Every read re-verifies the whole chain
statement: Every read or verify MUST re-validate the entire chain against the head from the bytes on disk, trusting nothing cached from earlier calls.
note: keep: re-verify at each trust decision (for example before accepting 'done') and cache only within one locked operation.
threat: Stale caches hiding tampering that happened between calls.

name: status() never raises, classifies state
statement: status() MUST return uninitialized, blocked with a failure_code, append_recovery_required, or the ready verify summary, converting every HarnessError into blocked.
note: keep: one typed state feeds the omp status line and session_start injection; also catch OSError, which T1 lets escape.
threat: Diagnostic surfaces crashing with tracebacks instead of reporting a typed fail-closed state.

name: Stable typed failure codes
statement: Every ledger failure MUST raise HarnessError with a stable machine code specific to file kind and failure (e.g. ledger_tail_truncated, ledger_unanchored_tail, ledger_head_symlink, ledger_pending_corrupt), shared by all surfaces.
note: keep: machine codes let G1 gate on exact failures without parsing prose.
threat: Untyped tracebacks that an agent can misread or argue past; inconsistent diagnoses across surfaces.

name: Flattened decoded view with alias fields
statement: Readers receive each record as one flat dict of envelope fields, payload fields and aliases (event, prior_ledger_seq, prior_ledger_hash, receipt_hash).
note: drop: aliases duplicate envelope fields; expose envelope and payload separately with one name per concept.
threat: principle

name: Linear verify, constant-work ordinary append
statement: Full verification MUST be one streaming O(n) pass, and ordinary appends (registration, invalidation, verification results) MUST do O(1) existing-record work; lifecycle appends (status, completion, contract update, verification start) may read O(n).
note: modify: keep the complexity contract but measure it with real call counters; T1 reports hardcoded constants.
threat: Verification cost growing until it is skipped in practice; lock hold times growing with history.

name: Same-user rewrite out of scope
statement: The chain plus head is tamper-evident only against partial edits; anyone able to write both files (same OS user or root) can rewrite history or roll back to an older pair, and it will verify.
note: modify: this is the decisive gap for G1 because the LLM runs as the same user; add a MAC keyed outside agent reach or an external witness, and keep the head copy outside agent-reachable paths, with omp tool_call blocking only as defense in depth.
threat: The agent (same user) forging a full ledger, or copying back an older ledger+head pair to erase an invalidation and revive a completion.

name: Ledger checks shape, not truth
statement: Append validates payload structure and lifecycle ordering but not the truth of digests, exit codes or attempt pairing; truth depends entirely on which process writes.
note: modify: in G1 only the extension process appends, the agent never gets a write path, and every result must pair with a harness-recorded start (same attempt, command digest, contract).
threat: Any caller with API or CLI access, including an agent, minting plausible success receipts.

name: Canonical plan file; stateless reconstruction
statement: All task contracts must live in one canonical file (.harness/plan.md), and every invocation must rebuild task state from canonical files only, never from session memory.
note: modify: keep one canonical contract store but hold it outside the agent's write reach (or treat any agent edit to it as untrusted input).
threat: Context reset or agent memory loss; divergent task definitions across sessions.

name: Root selection: flag, env, upward search
statement: The harness root is --root if given, else HARNESS_ROOT, else the nearest ancestor containing .harness/plan.md; otherwise root_not_found.
note: modify: pin the root from the omp session workspace; an env var the agent can set must not redirect the harness.
threat: Operating on the wrong repository's state.

name: Strict plan header; empty plan valid
statement: A plan that is missing, a symlink, unreadable, non-UTF-8, zero-byte, or lacks a '# [Name ]Harness Plan' first line is invalid (fail closed), while a valid header with no tasks is a legitimate zero-task state.
note: keep: fail-closed parsing that distinguishes corruption from 'no durable work'.
threat: Truncated/swapped plan silently read as 'no tasks'; symlink redirection of the canonical plan.

name: Task identity fields grammar
statement: Each task starts at '## Task `id`' with a unique id matching [a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,63} and has exactly one non-empty 'Objective:' line and exactly one 'Status:' line in {pending, active, complete, blocked}.
note: keep: strict id grammar matters because ids become filesystem paths.
threat: Ambiguous task identity, path injection through ids used in evidence paths, out-of-vocabulary status claims.

name: Required contract sections, no duplicates
statement: Every task must have Scope, Acceptance Criteria, Public Verify, Artifacts and When To Stop sections, each exactly once; extra ### sections are tolerated and not hashed.
note: keep: required fields; but prefer a structured format over markdown headings.
threat: Contracts lacking a verify command or artifact list; shadowing via duplicate sections.

name: Section value extraction rules
statement: Scope and Artifacts are the non-empty '- ' bullets (outer backticks trimmed); Public Verify and When To Stop are all non-blank lines joined by spaces with one surrounding backtick pair stripped; empty values are invalid.
note: modify: replace markdown heuristics with a typed contract schema (JSON/TOML) so hashing is unambiguous.
threat: Empty/whitespace verify commands or artifact lists entering a contract.

name: Acceptance criteria are strict checkboxes
statement: Every non-blank line under Acceptance Criteria must be '- [ ] text' or '- [x|X] text', and at least one criterion is required.
note: keep: strict criteria list; the checkbox state itself is a claim (see LIFE-18).
threat: Free-form or hidden criteria escaping the completion check.

name: Contract hash over immutable fields
statement: contract_hash is sha256 of canonical JSON of task_id, objective, scope, criterion texts, public_verify, artifacts and when_to_stop, and must exclude status and check marks.
note: keep: the anchor every receipt and transition binds to.
threat: Silent edits to goals, criteria, verify command or artifacts after evidence was produced.

name: First-sight contract registration anchor
statement: A non-terminal task's contract must be anchored in the ledger (contract_registered) before verification or any lifecycle mutation uses it.
note: modify: register only at explicit task creation; implicit enrollment makes display commands write state.
threat: Verifying or completing against an unanchored, still-editable contract.

name: Contract drift is refused
statement: If a non-terminal task's current hash differs from its latest anchor without an accepted update, verification and every plan mutation must fail with contract_drift; terminal tasks are skipped so their drift is reported, not blocking.
note: keep: core anti-goalpost-moving rule.
threat: Agent weakens criteria, verify command or artifacts and then verifies/completes.

name: Explicit accepted contract update with reason
statement: A changed contract becomes authoritative only through an explicit accept command with a non-blank reason, recorded as contract_update_accepted{old_contract_hash, contract_hash, reason} with old != new.
note: modify: acceptance must come from the human channel, not an agent-invokable command; the agent's reason is a claim, not evidence.
threat: Silent drift; reusing evidence produced under a superseded contract.

name: Enrolled tasks cannot vanish from plan
statement: Every task id ever registered in the ledger must remain in the plan; otherwise bootstrap is refused and the report cannot be complete.
note: keep: append-only task registry must dominate the editable plan view.
threat: Deleting an unfinished task from the plan to reach vacuous completion.

name: At most one active task
statement: At most one task may be active: more than one is a typed ambiguity, and activating another task while one is active is refused.
note: keep: one focus task per session simplifies evidence attribution.
threat: Conflicting continuations; racing activations.

name: Status vocabulary and transition routing
statement: pending/active/blocked may change freely (subject to single-active), 'complete' is reachable only through the completion gate, and nothing leaves complete.
note: modify: add an explicit state machine (e.g., only active -> complete).
threat: Agent declaring completion by editing status; reopening finished work.

name: Terminal if plan OR ledger says complete
statement: A task is terminal if the plan says complete or the ledger holds any complete transition for it; terminal tasks refuse status change, criterion marking and contract acceptance (task_reopen_refused).
note: keep: fail-closed union; new work requires a new task.
threat: Reopening or amending completed work by editing the plan back to active.

name: Ledger-level terminal enforcement
statement: The ledger itself must refuse non-complete status changes, contract updates and verification starts for a task with a complete transition, independent of plan content.
note: keep: enforce invariants at the single writer, not only at the CLI.
threat: Bypassing CLI checks via direct API/tampered plan; overwriting a completed task's evidence.

name: Plan-first status writes with ledger reconcile
statement: Non-complete status changes write the plan then append task_status_changed; a retry whose plan already matches but whose ledger frontier differs appends once (status_reconciled), and an exact repeat is zero-write.
note: modify: write the authoritative log first and derive the plan view from it; avoid frontier heuristics.
threat: Crash between plan write and ledger append leaving plan/ledger divergent; duplicate transitions on retry.

name: Criterion marking flips checkboxes in place
statement: --mark N / --mark-all flip '- [ ]' to '- [x]' for 1-based criteria via an atomic plan rewrite; out-of-range numbers fail (invalid_criterion), repeats are zero-write, and no ledger event is recorded.
note: modify: checkmarks are agent self-attestation; bind each criterion to a harness-run check or record marks as claims only.
threat: Lost updates between concurrent marks; marking criteria of completed tasks.

name: All criteria checked before completion
statement: Completion (current and historical) requires a non-empty criteria list with every criterion checked.
note: modify: necessary but not sufficient, since marks are agent-written.
threat: Completing with acknowledged-unfinished acceptance items.

name: Bootstrap input validation
statement: Task bootstrap requires a grammar-valid id, single-line bounded texts (4096 B; verify 8192 B), relative non-traversing scope/artifact paths, at least one scope/criterion/artifact, and no duplicate scopes or criteria.
note: keep: validate all agent-supplied contract text before it touches canonical state.
threat: Newline injection into the markdown contract; absolute or '..' paths escaping the repository.

name: Artifacts must lie inside allowed scope
statement: Every declared artifact path must equal or be beneath one of the task's allowed scope paths.
note: keep: cheap consistency check; reject '.' as a scope.
threat: Declaring evidence artifacts outside the task's mutation boundary.

name: Bootstrap preconditions re-checked under lock
statement: A task may be bootstrapped only when plan and ledger agree, no task is active, and the id is unused, all evaluated inside the exclusive lock.
note: keep: concurrent bootstraps must have exactly one winner and a zero-write loser.
threat: Racing bootstraps creating two active tasks or duplicate ids.

name: Atomic generated bootstrap with rollback
statement: Bootstrap must write a machine-generated contract only after the full candidate plan re-parses with exactly one active task, then register it, restoring the original plan if registration fails.
note: modify: log-first (or journaled) creation so process death cannot leave an unregistered task; generate from structured data.
threat: Plan containing a task the ledger never registered, or a corrupt plan, after a failed bootstrap.

name: Ledger genesis only by first bootstrap
statement: A new ledger may be created only by the first task bootstrap from a provably pristine state; any other missing-ledger state fails closed.
note: keep: history deletion must be detectable, never a fresh start.
threat: Deleting the ledger to erase history and restart clean.

name: Allowed paths recorded, never enforced
statement: Scope/allowed paths are hashed into the contract and stored in the bootstrap receipt, but nothing checks repository mutations against them.
note: modify: G1 can enforce scope from recorded omp tool calls/diffs before allowing completion.
threat: limitation: agent edits outside its declared scope go undetected.

name: Explicit idempotent task invalidation
statement: Any task's current contract can be explicitly invalidated with a non-blank single-line reason of at most 2048 bytes, recorded exactly once per (task, contract_hash).
note: keep: an explicit kill switch for evidence later found wrong.
threat: Duplicate or racy invalidations; multi-line injected reasons.

name: Invalidation permanent and retroactive
statement: An invalidation of a contract hash must defeat completion for that contract forever, including an already-committed completion; recovery requires a new contract.
note: keep: retroactive invalidation is the only safe response to evidence later found wrong.
threat: Continuing to trust a completion later shown to be wrong.

name: Completion only through explicit gate
statement: A task becomes complete only via 'plan --task X --status complete', which evaluates current evidence and commits a receipt-bound transition before updating the plan.
note: keep: the single choke point; in G1 it should be triggered/checked by the harness, not merely invoked by the agent.
threat: Agent claiming completion in text or by editing the plan without harness-validated evidence.

name: Plan completion claim is not authority
statement: A plan 'Status: complete' without a matching ledger complete transition must never count as completion.
note: keep: status text is a claim; only harness-written transitions count.
threat: Agent edits the plan status to complete.

name: Latest verification attempt must succeed
statement: In current mode the newest verification event (started, succeeded or failed) for the task must be verification_succeeded.
note: keep: latest-attempt-wins prevents cherry-picking an old pass over a newer failure.
threat: Cherry-picking an older success after a later failure; completing during an in-flight re-verification.

name: Receipt bound to contract, exit, command
statement: The selected receipt must carry the current contract_hash, exit_code 0 and public_command_digest equal to sha256 of the plan's Public Verify text.
note: keep: G1 should additionally record the exact argv it executed.
threat: Evidence from a weaker or different command, or from a superseded contract.

name: Task-local manifest path binding
statement: The receipt's manifest must be exactly .harness/evidence/<task_id>/manifest.json.
note: keep: evidence location must be derived by the harness, not chosen by the receipt.
threat: Reusing another task's manifest or receipt.

name: Authoritative receipt field completeness
statement: Non-legacy success receipts must contain all 15 binding fields (task, attempt, contract, manifest, manifest hash, command digest, exit, source, tree, artifacts, verification time, schema, ledger id, prev/record hash).
note: keep: make the receipt schema itself require every binding field.
threat: Partially bound receipts skipping a check by omission.

name: Manifest content hash binding
statement: The manifest file's current SHA-256 must equal the receipt's manifest_content_hash.
note: keep: binds the manifest to the exact bytes the harness hashed at verification time.
threat: Rewriting the manifest after verification (exit, tree, timestamp forgery).

name: Receipt-manifest cross-binding
statement: Receipt attempt_id, verification_timestamp, source_digest, repository_tree_hash and artifact_hashes must equal the manifest's attempt_id, timestamp, source_digest, git_tree_hash and artifacts.
note: keep: cheap redundancy that also catches receipt/manifest pairing mistakes.
threat: Pairing a receipt with a manifest from another attempt or snapshot.

name: 60-second receipt append freshness
statement: The success receipt's ledger append time must be no earlier than, and at most 60 s after, the recorded verification time.
note: modify: G1 emits both events itself; use a configurable bound measured from harness-observed command exit with monotonic time.
threat: Hand-appending a success receipt long after the fact for an old manifest (replay/deferred forging).

name: Current snapshot equals verified snapshot
statement: At completion the repository source digest and Git tree hash must equal those in the success receipt and declared artifacts must re-hash identically.
note: keep: strongest evidence check; recompute in the harness process, never accept agent-reported hashes.
threat: Editing code after a passing verification, then completing.

name: Command output digest binding
statement: For schema-3 manifests the receipt's stdout/stderr SHA-256 must match the manifest and the 0600 output files must still hash to those digests.
note: keep: command output is harness-observed evidence and must stay immutable after capture.
threat: Tampering with recorded command output after verification.

name: Manifest semantic validation delegated
statement: The manifest must be a secure 0600 regular file with exact fields, supported schema, exit 0, no timeout, root workspace '.', and the current task's id, contract hash and command digest.
note: keep: the manifest must be re-validated on every read, never trusted from a prior pass.
threat: Malformed or forged manifest accepted as evidence.

name: Receipt chain position re-check
statement: The selected receipt must sit at its seq in the validated chain with ledger schema v2, the correct predecessor hash and the ledger's id.
note: drop: duplicate of full-chain validation on read; keep chain checks in one place.
threat: Receipt spliced from another ledger or position.

name: Fail-closed completion state loading
statement: Any ledger read error or current-snapshot error must make evaluation invalid with that error's code, and state computed for a different root is rejected.
note: keep: any uncertainty about evaluation inputs must yield 'not complete'.
threat: Evaluating against a corrupt/pending ledger or the wrong repository.

name: Completion transition must bind receipt
statement: Every new complete transition must name verification_receipt_seq and verification_receipt_hash of a successful (exit 0) receipt for the same task and contract.
note: keep: completion is a pointer to harness-recorded evidence, never a free-standing flag.
threat: Unbound or forged completion transitions; binding to a failed receipt.

name: Later same-task event stales binding
statement: A completion binding must be refused if any lifecycle event for the same task (contract registration/update, invalidation, status change, verification start/success/failure) follows the bound receipt; other tasks' events do not stale it.
note: keep: closes the evaluate-then-commit race at the single writer.
threat: Completing on a receipt superseded by a newer attempt, invalidation, contract or status change that raced with evaluation.

name: Two-phase completion re-checked under lock
statement: Evaluation runs outside the lock; the commit happens in a fresh lock window that re-reads ledger and plan and re-checks committed binding, plan status and an unchanged contract hash before appending.
note: modify: also re-validate the filesystem snapshot and criteria under the commit lock (T1 leaves a TOCTOU gap).
threat: Races between concurrent completers, verifiers, invalidators and contract editors.

name: Committed completion validated before reuse
statement: An existing complete transition is honored only if it is the task's latest status event, matches the current contract, and binds a successful same-task/same-contract receipt equal to any requested binding.
note: keep: recovery must re-prove the binding instead of trusting a prior transition.
threat: Recovering or re-reporting completion for a drifted contract or substituted receipt.

name: Ledger-first commit, idempotent recovery
statement: The ledger transition must be committed before the plan is updated, and any rerun of the same complete request converges to exactly one transition, reporting completion_recovered or completion_already_committed.
note: keep: authoritative record first, derived views reconciled idempotently.
threat: Crashes at any point duplicating transitions or leaving plan and ledger permanently divergent.

name: Legacy completion compare-and-commit
statement: Reconciling an unbound legacy completion requires a passing historical evaluation and an unchanged ledger (same length and tail hash) between snapshot and commit.
note: drop: no legacy ledgers in G1 (the whole-ledger CAS pattern is reusable).
threat: Ledger mutation during unlocked legacy validation.

name: Historical evaluation of completed tasks
statement: A completed task is judged historically: its latest complete transition for the current contract must explicitly bind a successful same-task receipt, with evidence intact but no current source/tree/artifact match required.
note: keep: separates 'was proven at completion' from 'passes now'.
threat: Conflating 'was valid when completed' with 'passes now'; substituting a later receipt.

name: Legacy-prefix binding with disclosed weakness
statement: For legacy unbound transitions the receipt is the latest qualifying success strictly before the transition, and the verdict must disclose weaker evidence (legacy-manifest-unbound) and a manifest-rewrite tri-state (True/False/None).
note: drop: no legacy data; keep only the 'disclose evidence strength' field idea.
threat: A post-completion success retroactively justifying completion; weak legacy evidence presented as strong.

name: Reports are read-only, never re-snapshot
statement: Reporting must write nothing and never compute current source/tree digests (no Git objects), relying only on recorded state.
note: keep: observation surfaces must not perturb the evidence they report.
threat: Read paths mutating state or the Git object store; trusting cached reports.

name: Historical vs current semantics explicit
statement: Reports must label completed tasks as historical snapshots (not 'passes now') and the active task as a recorded-event projection that always needs explicit completion.
note: keep: stops readers treating historical snapshots as current proof.
threat: Readers over-interpreting a report as current verification.

name: Active-task verification projection
statement: The active task's state is projected only from ledger events after its current contract anchor (contract-unregistered, invalidated, missing, started, succeeded, failed, stale-contract) with a derived next_action.
note: modify: keep the projection but derive it with the same invalidation/drift rules as the gate.
threat: Pre-anchor results leaking into guidance; re-verifying just to answer 'where am I'.

name: Single global integrity-regression issue
statement: Plan/ledger disagreement (missing/mismatched contract anchor for a non-active task, a ledger-complete task failing historical evaluation, or plan status differing from the latest ledger status) must raise one global issue that blocks overall completeness.
note: keep: tamper detection on the agent-writable view.
threat: Post-hoc plan tampering (unchecking criteria, editing objective, flipping status) going unnoticed.

name: Overall completeness aggregation
statement: The repository is complete only if every task report is complete, no issues exist and the ledger is readable; --require-complete maps incompleteness to exit 1.
note: modify: do not treat zero tasks as complete (vacuous truth).
threat: Partial or corrupted state reported as done.

name: Typed verdicts and fail-closed exits
statement: Evaluations return a typed verdict (valid, reason_code, receipt seq/hash, scope, binding, evidence mode) and CLI failures surface as ERROR[code] exit 2; unexpected exceptions fail closed as internal_error (2), interrupts exit 130, negative report/ledger states exit 1.
note: keep: a harness that cannot decide must say no with a machine-readable reason.
threat: Ambiguous outcomes being treated as success by an orchestrator.

name: Validate before write; refusals zero-write
statement: All request validation (terminality, single-active, criterion range, committed completion) must happen before the first durable write so refusals leave .harness byte-identical.
note: keep: rejected requests must leave no partial state.
threat: Partial state from rejected commands.

name: Advisory exclusive lock serializes mutations
statement: Every plan/ledger mutation and its preceding re-read must happen inside one exclusive lock on .harness/ledger.lock.
note: modify: an advisory lock does not stop the agent's direct edits; G1 must own the store (single writer process).
threat: Lost updates between concurrent harness processes (marks, statuses, bootstraps, invalidations).

name: Atomic durable plan rewrites
statement: Every plan mutation must be a whole-file replace via temp file, fsync, rename and directory fsync.
note: keep: crash-safe whole-file replacement for any derived view.
threat: Torn or partial plan after a crash mid-write.

name: Verification pinned to root workspace
statement: Authoritative verification must run in the repository root; --workspace must resolve in-root without symlinks and equal the root.
note: keep: evidence must come from the same tree that is being completed.
threat: Verifying a scratch copy that differs from the code being completed.

name: Minimal command surface and writer set
statement: The lifecycle CLI exposes only doctor, plan, task begin|invalidate, verify, report, ledger status|verify|recover and hook, and production code writes only seven core event types.
note: keep: small closed event vocabulary; the 'hook' entry is Codex-specific and replaced by the omp extension.
threat: Hidden side channels or retired writers mutating lifecycle state.

name: Harness-executed verification is sole evidence
statement: Success evidence MUST come only from a verification command the harness itself spawned, observed and recorded; agent self-report or predicted success never counts.
note: keep: this is G1's core premise; run verifiers from the omp extension process, never through an agent tool call.
threat: Agent claims tests pass without running them, or reports a fabricated exit status.

name: Verification runs only in root workspace
statement: Authoritative verification MUST execute with cwd equal to the resolved repository root, and evidence MUST record workspace '.'.
note: keep: pin cwd to the session root the extension owns; drop the vestigial --workspace option.
threat: Verifying a scratch worktree or subdirectory and presenting it as root-repository evidence.

name: Absolute-path bash runner with captured output
statement: The verifier MUST be launched through a fixed absolute interpreter path with controlled cwd and environment, capturing stdout and stderr in full.
note: modify: keep the absolute interpreter, but capture bytes (text=True crashes on non-UTF-8 output) and spawn in a new process group.
threat: PATH-shadowed shell or inherited cwd/env altering what actually runs.

name: Timeout yields exit 124 and flag
statement: A verifier exceeding its time budget MUST be killed and recorded as timed_out with exit 124, never as a pass.
note: modify: keep semantics but kill the whole process group/cgroup and make the budget harness-configured, not agent-supplied.
threat: Hung or deliberately stalled verifier, or a partial run treated as success.

name: Pass means exit zero, not timed out
statement: A run passes only if the observed exit code is exactly 0 and it did not time out; harness-internal failures map to exit 70, and the result is passed only when a success receipt was appended.
note: keep: a binary exit-0 predicate is simple and observer-checkable.
threat: Partial success, misread exit codes, or a pass without a durable receipt.

name: Completed tasks refuse re-verification
statement: Verification MUST be refused for a task whose plan status is complete or whose ledger holds a complete transition, so historical evidence is never overwritten.
note: keep: terminal tasks immutable; the ledger-side check is the real guard since plan status is agent-editable.
threat: Overwriting or re-binding evidence of an already-completed task.

name: Contract registered before verification
statement: Verification MUST run against a ledger-registered contract hash; an unaccepted contract change aborts before any receipt.
note: modify: in G1 the contract (command, artifacts) should be fixed by the user or harness, not accepted by the agent.
threat: Silently verifying an edited contract (weaker command or artifacts).

name: Command identity bound by SHA-256 digest
statement: Every receipt and manifest MUST carry the SHA-256 of the exact executed command, and completion MUST require it to equal the digest of the plan's Public Verify.
note: keep, but refuse the --command override at run time instead of recording a success for a non-plan command.
threat: Running an easier command and passing it off as the planned verifier.

name: Allowlist-only child environment
statement: The verifier MUST receive a freshly built allowlist environment, never the parent environment.
note: keep: allowlist beats denylist; build it in the extension, not from omp's own environment.
threat: Credential leakage into verifier output and env injection (LD_PRELOAD, BASH_ENV, PYTHONPATH, GIT_DIR).

name: Private per-attempt HOME and TMPDIR
statement: Each verification attempt MUST get its own owner-only HOME and TMPDIR shared with no other attempt or the user's real home.
note: modify: keep per-attempt sandbox dirs outside the workspace and fix the boundary-less ancestor chmod, which only works where the user owns every ancestor (e.g. proot).
threat: Verifier reading real dotfiles or credential caches via HOME; cross-attempt temp contamination.

name: PATH entries inside repository denied
statement: PATH entries resolving inside the repository MUST be removed from the verifier's PATH.
note: modify: resolve relative entries against the child cwd, apply the same filter to harness git calls, prefer absolute tool paths.
threat: Repo-planted binaries (fake pytest/python) shadowing system tools to fake a pass.

name: Runtime cleanup with surfaced warning
statement: The per-attempt runtime directory MUST be removed after every run, and a cleanup failure MUST be surfaced rather than hidden.
note: keep.
threat: Leftover verifier state (tokens, caches) leaking into later attempts or evidence.

name: Secret env values harvested by name
statement: Values of parent env vars whose names look secret (length >= 4) MUST be redacted wherever they appear in evidence.
note: keep; also redact encoded forms and short values, and never fall back to the full process env on an empty mapping.
threat: A verifier or command line echoing a real credential into persisted evidence.

name: Pattern-based secret redaction
statement: Known token shapes MUST be redacted from command text and outputs before persistence.
note: modify: extend to JSON-quoted keys, PEM blocks, JWTs, xox*, AIza and Basic auth, all currently missed.
threat: Literal secrets printed by tools landing in evidence files.

name: Redact before any persistence
statement: Unredacted command text and output MUST never be written to disk or returned; only redacted forms persist.
note: keep; note the output digests attest the redacted bytes, not raw output.
threat: Secrets persisting in evidence files that are later shared or committed.

name: Ledger stores digests and codes only
statement: Append-only receipts MUST carry digests, paths and failure codes, never raw command text or output.
note: keep.
threat: Secrets becoming permanent in an unredactable append-only log.

name: Owner-only symlink-free harness directories
statement: Evidence and private runtime directories MUST be created component-by-component below a boundary, rejecting symlinks and forcing mode 0700.
note: modify: same-uid modes do not separate harness from agent; store evidence in an extension-owned dir outside the agent-writable tree.
threat: A symlinked .harness/evidence redirecting writes outside the repo; other local users reading evidence.

name: Private evidence file descriptor checks
statement: Evidence files MUST be written atomically at 0600 and, when read, MUST be a regular, single-link, exact-0600 file checked on the open descriptor.
note: keep.
threat: Hardlink, symlink, FIFO or permissive-mode substitution of evidence files.

name: Atomic fsynced file replacement
statement: Harness files MUST be replaced atomically with data and directory fsync so readers never see partial content.
note: keep.
threat: Torn or partially written manifests and outputs after a crash.

name: Single-slot task-local evidence path
statement: A task's evidence lives at the fixed path .harness/evidence/<task_id>/ and a success receipt MUST reference exactly that manifest.
note: modify: use per-attempt content-addressed evidence so earlier attempts are never overwritten.
threat: Reusing another task's manifest or receipt (cross-task replay).

name: Runtime evidence paths are git-ignored
statement: Ledger, head, pending, lock, evidence/ and private/ paths MUST be git-ignored while the canonical plan MUST NOT be.
note: modify: keep G1 evidence outside the repo entirely, which makes this contract unnecessary.
threat: Evidence or private runtime files being committed, or the plan accidentally untracked.

name: Manifest schema v3 field set
statement: A manifest MUST record schema_version 3, task id, contract hash, attempt id, redacted command, command digest, exit code, timestamp, git tree hash, source digest, workspace, timed_out, artifacts and output paths with digests.
note: modify: keep the field set, add a pre-run snapshot and runner identity, and validate against the schema at run time.
threat: Under-specified evidence that cannot be re-validated later.

name: Legacy v2 and oracle fields tolerated
statement: Schema-2 manifests (no output digests) and inert legacy oracle fields are accepted but labelled as weaker evidence.
note: drop: G1 starts clean; legacy acceptance only widens the attack surface.
threat: principle (backward compatibility with older receipts)

name: Output digests bind stdout and stderr
statement: The SHA-256 of persisted stdout and stderr MUST be stored in both the manifest and the success receipt and recomputed on validation.
note: keep.
threat: Post-hoc editing of captured output to hide failures.

name: Strict exact-key manifest validation
statement: Manifests MUST have exactly the expected keys and types, with regex-checked ids and hashes and well-formed artifact entries.
note: keep.
threat: Malformed or padded manifests slipping through lenient parsing.

name: Manifest timestamp zoned and not future
statement: A manifest timestamp MUST be ISO-8601 with an explicit timezone and not later than now.
note: keep, though the harness clock in the receipt is the stronger source than a file field.
threat: Pre-dated or future-dated evidence used to win ordering checks.

name: Manifest bound to task and contract
statement: When validated for a task, the manifest task id and contract hash MUST equal the task's current values.
note: keep, and also require manifest artifact paths to equal the contract's artifact list.
threat: Replaying a manifest from another task or an older contract.

name: Secure manifest loading rules
statement: A manifest MUST be loaded only if it is a non-symlink, nonempty, mode-0600 regular file inside the evidence root that parses as a UTF-8 JSON object.
note: keep, but check nlink and mode on the same fd that is read.
threat: Symlinked, escaping or forged manifest files, or parser crashes on hostile input.

name: Manifest alone is never authority
statement: A manifest file MUST never prove success by itself; only a harness-appended success receipt whose manifest_content_hash matches can.
note: keep: in G1 the receipt store must be unreachable to the agent for this to hold.
threat: Editing a failed manifest to exit_code 0 or swapping in a forged manifest.

name: Relative traversal-free artifact paths
statement: Artifact and evidence paths MUST be non-empty, relative, drive-less and free of '..' components.
note: keep, but reject '.', which is currently accepted and hashes the whole workspace.
threat: Path traversal to hash or reference files outside the workspace.

name: Fd-anchored no-follow artifact hashing
statement: Artifacts MUST be opened component-by-component relative to directory fds with O_NOFOLLOW and hashed from that same descriptor, failing closed when O_NOFOLLOW is unavailable.
note: keep: Node lacks openat, so implement via a small native or Python helper.
threat: Symlink escapes and lookup-to-open swap races (TOCTOU).

name: Artifacts must be nonempty
statement: Zero-byte files and directories containing no regular files MUST be rejected as artifacts.
note: keep (cheap), but nonempty is a weak content check.
threat: Satisfying artifact requirements with placeholder empty files.

name: Canonical directory artifact digest
statement: A directory artifact's hash MUST be a canonical digest over its sorted regular-file entries, rejecting symlinks and special files.
note: keep, with depth and fd limits (deep trees raise RecursionError).
threat: Ambiguous or order-dependent directory hashes; links smuggling external content.

name: Artifacts rehashed at validation time
statement: Current-scope validation MUST recompute every artifact hash and require exact equality with the recorded entry.
note: keep.
threat: Replacing an artifact after verification.

name: Artifacts inside declared scope at bootstrap
statement: Every declared artifact MUST lie under one of the task's allowed scope paths.
note: modify: enforce at verification time too and forbid harness-owned paths.
threat: Declaring out-of-scope or harness-internal files as task artifacts.

name: Source digest over entry identity
statement: The source snapshot MUST hash every non-directory entry's path, type and content (symlinks by target bytes) and fail on special files.
note: keep, but handle non-UTF-8 names, vanished files and unreadable directories explicitly.
threat: Undetected source changes between verification and completion.

name: Host-stable digest normalization
statement: Snapshot identity MUST ignore mtime, ownership and non-executable mode bits, recording only whether any execute bit is set.
note: keep.
threat: Spurious invalidation from touch, chmod or copying across hosts.

name: Digest exclusion set for runtime state
statement: Snapshots MUST exclude the harness's own runtime state and VCS metadata so harness writes never perturb them.
note: modify: exclude only harness-owned paths; cache dirs such as __pycache__ can carry executable bytecode.
threat: Self-invalidation from harness writes (evidence, ledger, caches).

name: Git tree hash via temporary index
statement: The repository snapshot MUST be a real Git tree object built from a throwaway index, never touching the user's index, and must work without HEAD.
note: experiment: written objects allow re-materializing the snapshot for reproduction, but use a harness-owned GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY and hardened git config.
threat: Snapshot gaps for untracked files; user index corruption.

name: Deterministic Git subprocess environment
statement: Harness Git calls MUST run with a minimal environment that disables global/system config and prompts and drops inherited repository overrides.
note: modify: also neutralize repo-local config (core.fsmonitor, filters, hooksPath) and call git by absolute path.
threat: Env-redirected repository or index, or interactive hangs during snapshotting.

name: Dual snapshot recorded and compared
statement: Evidence MUST record both a content digest and a Git tree hash, and current-scope completion MUST require both to match the present repository.
note: keep: the two digests cover each other's gaps (gitignored files versus excluded cache dirs).
threat: Code changes after a passing run being credited to the old pass.

name: Post-run snapshot stability re-check
statement: After writing the manifest, the harness MUST recompute source, tree and artifact hashes and fail the run if any changed.
note: modify: add a pre-run snapshot and require pre == post (or record both); both T1 snapshots are post-run.
threat: Background processes mutating files while evidence is recorded.

name: Read-only surfaces never snapshot or write
statement: Diagnostic and projection surfaces MUST NOT compute snapshots, write files or add Git objects; they report recorded state only.
note: keep.
threat: Observation perturbing evidence (object writes, bytecode), or diagnostics posing as current verification.

name: Write-ahead verification_started receipt
statement: A verification_started receipt (attempt id, contract hash, command digest, workspace) MUST be appended before the command runs.
note: keep, and require the terminal receipt to reference the started attempt_id.
threat: Crashed or killed runs disappearing without trace.

name: Success receipt binds full evidence tuple
statement: A verification_succeeded receipt MUST bind task, contract, attempt, manifest path and content hash, command digest, exit 0, source digest, tree hash, artifact hashes, verification timestamp and output digests.
note: keep; in G1 sign or MAC receipts with a key the agent cannot read.
threat: Partial receipts that can be paired with substituted evidence.

name: Failure receipts classify cause
statement: Every non-passing run MUST append verification_failed with exit code, timeout flag, manifest reference and a failure code.
note: keep, but catch all exceptions; non-HarnessError exceptions currently skip the receipt.
threat: Failures being silently dropped so an older success looks current.

name: Random attempt id links manifest and receipt
statement: Each run MUST get an unpredictable attempt id carried by the started receipt, manifest and terminal receipt, and completion MUST require manifest and receipt ids to match.
note: keep.
threat: Pairing a receipt with a manifest from a different run.

name: Success receipt freshness window
statement: The success receipt MUST be appended no earlier than, and within 60 s of, the verification timestamp, which must equal the manifest timestamp.
note: modify: measure from the end of snapshotting or scale the window; slow hosts can exceed 60 s.
threat: Late-appended or replayed success receipts.

name: Bounded 512-byte SessionStart projection
statement: Session start MUST inject at most 512 bytes of recorded task state: task id, status, first unchecked criterion, recorded verification state and a status command.
note: modify: port to omp's session-start hook, truncate by bytes, and label verification state as recorded, not current.
threat: Context bloat, and the model losing task continuity after compaction or resume.

name: Fail-open SessionStart hook output
statement: Projection failures MUST never block the session: errors become a typed systemMessage with continue=true, and unknown events pass through.
note: keep for projection only; G1 enforcement gates must fail closed instead.
threat: A harness bug or hostile state locking the user out of the agent.

name: Hook root resolution rejects symlinks
statement: The hook root MUST be the symlink-free Git top-level of the event cwd and equal the wrapper's own root, with a real .harness dir and regular plan.md; HARNESS_ROOT is ignored.
note: modify: take the root from omp session config; any symlinked ancestor (e.g. Android /sdcard) currently fails.
threat: Projecting another repository's state or following a symlinked root into attacker-controlled state.

name: Plan/ledger task mismatch is surfaced
statement: If the ledger registers task ids absent from the plan, projection MUST fail and doctor MUST report plan_ledger_task_mismatch rather than reconstruct.
note: keep.
threat: Agent deleting a task from the plan to hide its failed history.

name: Generated hook manifest with drift check
statement: Host hook configuration MUST be generated from code and checked for drift rather than hand-edited.
note: drop the Codex file; keep the idea of code-generated extension registration with a drift check.
threat: Silent hook config edits adding events or changing the command.

name: Thin symlink-guarded hook wrapper
statement: The hook entry point MUST be a thin wrapper that refuses symlinked locations and passes its own derived root explicitly to the handler.
note: modify: G1 hook code must live outside the agent-writable workspace (T1 imports repo src at run time).
threat: Hook path redirection to foreign code.

name: Harness entry points never write bytecode
statement: Harness processes and verifier children MUST NOT write bytecode or caches into the repository.
note: keep the principle: harness observation must not mutate the observed state.
threat: Observation perturbing source or tree digests (__pycache__ entering trees).

name: Doctor labels lifecycle-only facts
statement: Diagnostics MUST state explicitly that they reflect recorded lifecycle facts and performed no authoritative current check.
note: keep the labeling pattern; fix the crash on ambiguous active tasks.
threat: Users or agents mistaking a health check for verification.

name: Optional Codex hook trust probe
statement: Hook liveness MAY be checked only on request; a hook counts as active only if exactly SessionStart is discovered, all project hooks are trusted or managed and enabled, and the manifest has no drift.
note: drop: replace with an omp extension self-registration check.
threat: Believing continuity hooks run when the host marked them untrusted or modified.

name: Root discovery by plan marker
statement: The harness root is --root if given, else HARNESS_ROOT (which must contain .harness/plan.md), else the nearest ancestor of cwd containing .harness/plan.md.
note: modify: fix the root in extension config and never read it from agent-controllable env vars.
threat: Operating on the wrong repository.

name: Contained in-root path resolution
statement: Referenced evidence paths MUST validate as relative, contain no symlinked component, resolve inside the root and exist.
note: keep, preferring the fd-based walk to avoid path-based TOCTOU.
threat: Manifest output paths pointing outside the repo or through links.

name: Typed fail-closed error codes
statement: Every harness failure MUST carry a stable machine code, and unexpected exceptions MUST fail closed without leaking tracebacks.
note: keep.
threat: Ambiguous failures treated as success, or internals leaking to the agent.

name: Canonical JSON and UTC timestamps
statement: All hashed structures MUST use canonical JSON (sorted keys, compact separators, no NaN), and timestamps MUST be UTC millisecond ISO-8601 with Z.
note: keep.
threat: Non-deterministic hashes across runs or hosts.

name: Verify skill advisory rules
statement: Agent-facing verify guidance forbids self-report evidence and lists the rejection conditions, but enforcement lives in code.
note: modify: G1 never relies on agent compliance; keep only as prompt text mirroring enforced checks.
threat: principle (agent guidance)

name: Report skill factual taxonomy
statement: Reports MUST separate passed, failed and unverified facts, cite receipts and paths, avoid confidence language, and never present historical completion as current verification.
note: keep as the output contract for G1's own generated reports.
threat: Confidence language or stale results masquerading as evidence.

name: Harness self-integrity and dependency pins
statement: The harness's own code, hook directory, ledger event set and dependency list MUST be pinned so unreviewed changes are detected.
note: modify: check the extension's own hash at load time from outside agent-writable paths, not in a test the agent can edit.
threat: Agent weakening the harness itself, e.g. by editing validation code.

name: Reconstruct continuity from durable state only
statement: A fresh agent must reconstruct valid continuation from the repository and canonical harness state alone; any continuation-critical fact held elsewhere is a defect.
note: keep: G1 must rebuild every decision from its own observed ledger, never from omp session state.
threat: principle

name: Ephemeral context is never authority
statement: Conversation, memory, summaries, transcripts, handoffs, sessions and compaction output are disposable inputs and must never serve as authority.
note: keep: treat omp transcripts and compaction summaries as untrusted model-authored input.
threat: principle

name: Each turn is a bounded fail-closed slice
statement: Every disposable turn performs a bounded slice of work and either durably progresses or pauses fail-closed; multi-turn work continues only through durable state.
note: keep: G1 should close every omp turn with a harness-computed durable-delta verdict.
threat: principle

name: Task completion never implies Goal completion
statement: Completing an atomic task proves only that task's contract and never implies completion of the overall Goal.
note: keep: stops an agent from parlaying one green task into a 'done' claim.
threat: principle

name: Hard gates before any authority
statement: A candidate becomes authority only after hard invariants, deterministic task verification, frozen anchors, history preservation and context independence all pass.
note: keep: in G1 only harness-executed gates can promote a change.
threat: principle

name: Model reports and opinions are not authority
statement: Preferences, model reports, a bare process exit and audit opinions are never authority; findings count only after reproduction and acceptance.
note: keep: this is G1's founding rule; extend it to all LLM text.
threat: principle

name: Reject dominated higher-complexity candidates
statement: Reject any candidate dominated by a known capability-equivalent lower-complexity candidate, and freeze only after a delete-first test finds no equivalent reduction.
note: keep: every G1 mechanism should be justified by a reproduced threat or deleted.
threat: principle

name: Preserve native agent capabilities
statement: The harness must not override the host agent's reasoning, tools, permissions, sandboxing, approvals, retries, subagents, models, providers or transport.
note: modify: G1 may observe and record every omp tool call but should gate only completion claims, not ordinary tools.
threat: principle

name: Goal spec is inert; progress derived
statement: The normative Goal spec stores no progress and adds no runtime or canonical surface; satisfaction is derived on demand from source, contracts, ledger and current receipts.
note: keep: no mutable progress file an agent could edit to fake advancement.
threat: principle

name: Lessons persist only as verified artifacts
statement: Meta-improvements persist only as verified code, tests, specs or deterministic procedures with anchors intact; lessons-memory, self-approval and weaker verifiers never count as gains.
note: keep: encode G1 lessons as tests/checks, never as prompt notes or memory.
threat: principle

name: Accepted steps require strict gain
statement: Each accepted step preserves invariants and verified capability and strictly reduces the unsatisfied goal set, improves verified capability, or reduces complexity at equal capability.
note: experiment: needs a progress predicate G1 can compute itself instead of audit judgement.
threat: principle

name: Finite objective terminality, no scores
statement: The Goal is a finite set of terminal properties satisfied exactly when none is unsatisfied; percentages, intelligence scalars and subjective scores are never authority.
note: keep: an LLM-produced score must never decide done-ness.
threat: principle

name: Goal completion bound to current receipt
statement: Goal completion requires current deterministic Goal verification and an explicit completion bound to that successful receipt; model declarations, stale verification and unbound reports are rejected.
note: keep: done-ness is a fresh harness re-verification, never a stored flag.
threat: principle

name: No-active boundary registers one smallest task
statement: At a no-active boundary with an unsatisfied property, one fresh native turn records gap/justification fields and registers exactly one smallest justified task by fixed priority (integrity > continuity > capability > native > minimality > convenience); with nothing unsatisfied it creates no task and runs only final verification.
note: modify: keep one-task-at-a-time, but G1 can only validate the selection's structure, not the model's justification.
threat: principle

name: Forbidden selection anti-patterns
statement: Selection must never yield a giant complete-everything task, simultaneous active tasks, a hidden mutable queue, conversation-carried selection, supervisor reasoning or model routing.
note: keep: G1 orchestration must stay mechanical and non-planning.
threat: principle

name: Terminal evidence deterministic and reproducible
statement: Each terminal property stays false until its evidence (commands, exits, hashes, receipts, tests, inventories) is reproducible from durable state; vague terms such as 'good enough' are rejected.
note: keep: every G1 acceptance criterion must name a command, hash or receipt.
threat: principle

name: Every P0-P2 finding maps to receipt
statement: Audit resolution requires every P0/P1/P2 finding to map to a remediation receipt or an explicit exclusion, with environment, revisions, commands, exits and hashes recorded.
note: keep: G1 findings close only by harness-verified receipts, never by agent assertion.
threat: principle

name: Optional layers removable without damage
statement: Optional execution layers must be deletable without canonical migration while leaving the core and the native agent operational.
note: keep: uninstalling G1 must leave omp fully functional.
threat: principle

name: Restart recovery proven by hash equality
statement: Crash/restart recovery is accepted only when real kill/restart tests reproduce identical plan/ledger/head/source/tree/artifact hashes and pass ledger verification.
note: keep: inject real process kills at every G1 write boundary.
threat: principle

name: Sterile isolation for end-to-end evidence
statement: End-to-end continuity claims require isolated runs with empty user/runtime directories that exclude ephemeral authority and bind a verification receipt.
note: keep: G1's own E2E proofs need empty HOME/config to rule out hidden state.
threat: principle

name: Unproven failure types stay unclaimed
statement: Only boundary and failure types backed by a source matrix and tests are supported; unproven approval/transient types remain unclaimed and are never blindly retried or inferred.
note: keep: no blind retries on unclassified omp/provider errors.
threat: principle

name: Deferred scope declared and pinned
statement: Later-goal exclusions are listed explicitly and the checker pins the exact exclusion set so scope cannot silently grow or shrink.
note: keep: G1 should state what it does not verify.
threat: principle

name: Bounded on-demand spec reading
