statement: With an active task, read only the instruction file, the task contract and canonical state; read the Goal spec only at a no-active boundary or when the contract targets a terminal property.
note: modify: limit G1 context injection, noting G1 cannot verify what the model actually read.
threat: principle

name: No completion claim without current evidence
statement: Never claim a task complete without current evidence; reports must separate passed, failed and unverified facts, cite paths/receipts and avoid confidence language.
note: keep: in G1 the claim gate is mechanical and chat claims are ignored.
threat: principle

name: Opt-in enrollment, narrow harness scope
statement: The harness is used only for durable continuity and verification; work not enrolled via task begin remains valid native work with no harness continuity claim.
note: modify: G1 observes all turns but issues verification claims only for enrolled tasks.
threat: principle

name: No host-specific paths in canonical rules
statement: Optional external copies are never required for correctness, and canonical instructions/specs must not assume host paths, models, providers or hosts.
note: keep: G1 rules must run identically on any host.
threat: principle

name: Always-read instruction budget
statement: The always-loaded agent instruction file is capped at 2048 bytes to bound per-turn context and interpretation cost.
note: keep: cap G1's injected instructions per turn.
threat: principle

name: Stdlib-only with zero runtime dependencies
statement: Production code depends only on the language standard library plus Git, and the dependency list is pinned empty by test.
note: modify: keep the zero-dependency discipline in G1's own runtime language.
threat: principle

name: Exactly one active task
statement: At most one task is active; more than one is a typed current_task_ambiguous error, and pending/blocked tasks stay parked and unprojected.
note: keep: one active claim surface keeps attribution unambiguous.
threat: principle

name: Explicit scoped idempotent invalidation
statement: Retraction is explicit: one reason-bearing invalidation record per task, appended without running commands or rewriting evidence, idempotent and task-scoped.
note: keep: G1 needs an append-only retraction instead of edits.
threat: principle

name: Weaker evidence labelled, never upgraded
statement: Evidence lacking a binding is labelled as such (legacy-output-unbound, legacy-prefix, null tri-state) and never presented as bound or as current-repository verification.
note: keep: every G1 verdict should carry its binding strength.
threat: principle

name: Hooks are read-only bounded projections
statement: Host hooks only project bounded (512-byte) derived state, write nothing, fail open, and never intercept ordinary tool calls.
note: modify: G1 hooks may append to G1's own observation log but must not gate tools or mutate task state.
threat: principle

name: Host trust observed, never inferred
statement: Hook activation is reported from the host's own trust state (installed, trusted and active are distinct); automation never touches user trust and is labelled transport-only.
note: modify: prove G1 is actually loaded in omp from observed events, never from config presence.
threat: principle

name: Generated config is drift-checked
statement: Host configuration is generated from code and verified byte-equal by a check mode; hand edits are drift failures.
note: keep: generate G1's omp extension config and diff it every run.
threat: principle

name: Runtime state local; contract tracked
statement: Ledger, head, pending journal, locks, evidence and private runtime are git-ignored local state, while the canonical plan must stay tracked.
note: modify: keep G1 evidence out of agent-committed paths; cross-host moves must carry it explicitly.
threat: principle

name: Spec checked by structure and contradiction corpus
statement: The normative spec is validated by a deterministic checker: 12 obligations each with MUST and one REJECT counterexample, numbered terminals, one spec file, semantic signatures and a forbidden-contradiction corpus.
note: modify: reuse the negative/positive corpus pattern but treat it as a bounded oracle (THR-33).
threat: principle

name: Frozen anchor tripwires
statement: Tests pin exact digests of protected assets (core tree, adapter, host config), the event-type set, the empty dependency list and the single lock so any change must be explicit.
note: modify: anchor G1's verifier, but keep pins outside the agent-writable tree (see findings).
threat: principle

name: Independent reproduce-first re-audit
statement: Every task is re-audited by a non-implementer from a fresh session that treats the report as claims, reproduces each claim in isolated copies with empty HOME, and leaves the original untouched.
note: keep: G1 audits run in separate sessions with no shared context with the implementer.
threat: principle

name: Evidence classes with attestation ceiling
statement: Classify evidence as user-observed, host-observed, repository-bound, runtime-reproducible or not reconstructible, rank code and canonical state above reports, and never claim beyond the class.
note: keep: G1 records should carry an evidence-class field.
threat: principle

name: Report frozen before verification
statement: The task report is frozen before Public Verify and hashed as an artifact into the success receipt; explicit completion must post-date it and bind that receipt.
note: keep: an agent-written summary is just another hashed artifact, not a claim channel.
threat: principle

name: Failed attempts preserved as negative evidence
statement: Failed verification attempts stay immutable in the ledger as negative evidence; remediation proceeds by a new attempt, never by rewriting history.
note: keep.
threat: principle

name: Worker writes harness canonical state
statement: An agent/delegate with write access can tamper with harness-owned state (oracle, evidence, ledger) undetected when that state is inside its writable area or outside the integrity snapshot, or when isolation is a trusted boolean rather than proof.
note: keep: omp's agent can write anything its user can, so G1's evidence store must be outside its reach or hash-anchored externally.
threat: Delegate wrote ../../private/oracle.json and still returned status verified (P1); write_isolation=True flag trusted without proof (P3).

name: Completion trusted self-reported exit code
statement: A completion gate that trusts a manifest's self-reported exit_code lets a one-integer edit turn a failed verification into completion.
note: keep: G1 computes success only from the exit status it observed itself.
threat: Editing exit_code 1 to 0 passed plan --status complete, report --require-complete and the Stop gate (P1).

name: Evidence fields recorded but never bound
statement: Evidence fields that are recorded but never recomputed or hash-bound (tree hash, timestamp, stdout/stderr content) accept forged values.
note: keep: every evidence field must be recomputed by G1 or bound by a hash G1 computed.
threat: Fake git_tree_hash 'deadbeef', a 1999 timestamp and edited command.stdout were all accepted (P2/P3).

name: Secrets and private oracles leak into evidence
statement: Verification commands inheriting the full environment and world-readable evidence files leak secrets and private oracle commands/outputs into shareable evidence.
note: keep: G1 command capture must scrub env and restrict file modes.
threat: Oracle command and stdout appeared in a 0644 manifest; an echoed env secret landed in command.stdout (P2/P3).

name: Untyped exceptions escape the gates
statement: Tamper, lock, decode or permission failures that surface as raw exceptions instead of typed fail-closed codes break uniform handling and can hide every task's result.
note: keep: G1 verdicts form a closed typed alphabet; anything else maps to a typed fail-closed error.
threat: Uncaught HarnessError/PermissionError/RecursionError/ValueError turned the whole report into internal_error or a traceback (P2-P4).

name: Bypass-validated activation claims
statement: Protection validated only through bypass paths (trust-bypass smoke, disabled production hooks) gets claimed as active protection while the real path never ran.
note: keep: G1 must prove its activation from observed omp events and label test-only paths as such.
threat: Hooks silently inactive until trusted (P1); fixed PreToolUse never ran in production yet 'production failure fixed' was claimed (P2).

name: Trust hash excludes executed code
statement: Host trust that hashes only the hook handler definition lets changes to transitively imported harness code alter hook behavior without re-approval.
note: modify: G1 should hash its own loaded code and stamp that digest on every verdict.
threat: Codex trust covers the command/wrapper, not src/codex_harness imports, so source edits silently change trusted hook behavior.

name: Symlink, hardlink and TOCTOU file swaps
statement: Path checks separated from use, or missing symlink/hardlink/inode checks, let an attacker redirect canonical writes or make the harness hash a different file.
note: keep: open agent-controlled files no-follow and hash via the opened descriptor.
threat: ledger.jsonl symlink wrote outside the repo; a symlink swap between check and hash; lock inode replacement; manifest hardlink accepted (P3/P4).

name: History rollback or erasure goes undetected
statement: A self-validating hash chain without an external anchor or loss detection accepts a truncated prefix or a silently re-created empty ledger, reviving invalidated completions or erasing history.
note: modify: keep the anchor, but place it where the agent cannot write (T1's head is same-user writable).
threat: Deleting the invalidation line revived completion; deleting ledger+head silently re-genesised and erased invalidations (P2).

name: Superlinear ledger cost blocks availability
statement: Re-validating the whole hash chain on every append makes append O(n^2) and sessions O(n^3), turning normal growth into a denial of service.
note: keep: benchmark G1's evidence log at 10k+ records.
threat: Single append took 687 ms at 500 records and 10k records exceeded 5 minutes (P2; severity first understated as P3).

name: Surfaces disagree on the same state
statement: When different surfaces (stop gate, report, plan, hooks) evaluate different task subsets or logic, one surface passes what another blocks.
note: keep: one verdict function, many projections.
threat: Stop checked only tasks[0] and returned continue:true while report blocked another task's invalidation (P2).

name: Non-canonical encodings cause parser divergence
statement: Accepting duplicate keys, NaN/Infinity, bool-as-int, alternate spellings or unbounded sizes lets two parsers read the same bytes differently and lets oversized records strand recovery.
note: keep: hash exact canonical bytes and reject anything a second parser could read differently.
threat: A duplicate-key line read as a forged payload by first-wins parsers; NaN appended; a 3.2 MB payload left a permanently unrecoverable pending journal (P3).

name: Lock liveness and identity hazards
statement: Blocking locks without timeout, lock files replaceable by inode swap, and lock-free status reads cause indefinite hangs, lost mutual exclusion or false alarms.
note: modify: use bounded lock waits and verify lock identity after acquisition.
threat: A SIGSTOPped holder hangs every surface; rm+touch of ledger.lock let two writers append seq 2 (P3).

name: Environment override redirects canonical writes
statement: Root discovery that prefers an environment variable over the event's working directory or explicit root lets a write land in a different repository.
note: keep: derive the workspace root from observed facts, never from agent-settable env.
threat: HARNESS_ROOT=A with cwd B appended hook events into A; smoke children inherited HARNESS_ROOT (P3).

name: Residue and leaked resources pollute state
statement: Leftover worktrees, temp files, caches, bytecode and stray copies accumulate and leak into digests or repo-wide scans, changing what gets verified.
note: keep: snapshot the workspace before/after G1 actions and fail on unexplained residue.
threat: Orphan worktrees; .tmp files after crashes; .pyc from hooks; .ruff_cache from Public Verify; an in-repo sdcard/ draft copy entered source_digest; fixture trees broke the single-spec scan (P2-P4).

name: Tool-gating hook blocks its own lifecycle
statement: A pre-tool gating hook with a shell classifier denies legitimate verification and lifecycle commands, blocks subagents and reimplements native approvals.
note: keep: G1 observes tool calls instead of vetoing them; vetoes self-DoS the harness.
threat: With an active task, pytest, ruff, verify and complete were denied (19/31); Agent/spawn_agent always denied (P1/P2).

name: Non-authoritative events enter canonical history
statement: Telemetry, denial, advisory-hook or retired events written to (or replayed into) the canonical ledger get misread as invalidations and pollute authority.
note: keep: separate G1's tool-call observation log from its verdict ledger; only verdict events change authority.
threat: A denied, never-run command logged as pretool_blocked invalidated a valid verification (P1); ledger recover committed a retired codex_takeover (P4).

name: Historical validity tied to current source
statement: Requiring every past completion to match the current source makes any unrelated edit invalidate all history and forces endless re-verification.
note: keep: distinguish 'verified at receipt' from 'valid now'.
threat: Adding one unrelated file flipped four completed tasks to SOURCE_CHANGED; 9 of 16 verifications were re-verifications.

name: Turn-end gate forces unwanted continuation
statement: A stop/turn-end hook that blocks while criteria are incomplete forces extra model continuations, nags parked tasks and breaks intentional pause or context-clear boundaries.
note: keep: G1 never forces an omp turn to continue; it only refuses completion claims.
threat: A trusted Stop hook forced a continuation at a clear gate (STOP_HOOK_ROTATION_CONFLICT) and failed the E2E; Stop appended unbounded records (P3).

name: Empty versus corrupt state confusion
statement: Treating an empty plan as invalid breaks fresh bootstrap, while treating a corrupt or zero-byte plan as 'no tasks' yields vacuous success.
note: keep: 'nothing to check' must never be reported as 'checked and passed'.
threat: A placeholder task blocked every Stop in fresh repos (P2); a truncated plan read as 'no T1 tasks' passed Stop and report (P3).

name: Unbound or legacy completion paths
statement: Completion transitions without explicit receipt binding (latest-success fallback, raw API append, migration import) let unrelated or later receipts satisfy completion or silently downgrade strict tasks.
note: keep: every completion names the exact receipt it rests on.
threat: A later bogus success changed history; Ledger.append wrote an unbound complete; ledger migrate manufactured a legacy completion (P3).

name: Later attempts overwrite earlier evidence
statement: Single-path evidence lets a new verify attempt overwrite earlier outputs, destroying a completed task's historical proof or a failed attempt's diagnostics.
note: modify: make G1 evidence per-attempt and append-only so nothing is overwritten.
threat: Re-verifying a completed task made report --require-complete fail repo-wide with MANIFEST_CHANGED (P2); failed-attempt stdout lost (P3).

name: Check-then-act races outside the lock
statement: Guards evaluated before acquiring the mutation lock can be passed by two racing processes, letting a loser overwrite evidence or duplicate records.
note: keep: every G1 decision re-reads state under the same lock it writes under.
threat: A verify started inside complete's evaluate-to-append window overwrote the manifest (2/6 runs, P2); concurrent invalidations appended twice (P4).

name: Terminal state bypassed by edits
statement: Completed tasks can be silently reopened or rewritten when status changes or contract amendments are not terminal-checked on every mutation path.
note: keep: closed tasks are immutable; new work needs a new task.
threat: plan --status active then verify replaced evidence and re-bound completion; --accept-contract-change on a completed task destroyed history (P3).

name: False conflated with cannot tell
statement: Reporting false for a check that could not run (missing hash, unreadable file) makes 'undetectable' indistinguishable from 'verified unchanged'.
note: keep: every G1 check result is pass/fail/unknown, never boolean.
threat: mvp's receipt lacked manifest_content_hash, so a rewritten manifest showed rewritten=false (P3).

name: Dual-write crash window strands state
statement: A crash between two non-atomic writes (ledger append then plan replace) can leave a state that newly added guards refuse forever.
note: keep: inject kills between every pair of writes and require convergence.
threat: A kill after the complete append left ledger complete/plan active, refused by completion_binding_stale with no exit but contract amendment (P2 regression).

name: Lost updates reported as success
statement: Read-modify-replace file updates without a lock or compare-and-swap silently drop concurrent writers' changes while every caller reports success.
note: keep: one lock covers every co-dependent write.
threat: Two concurrent activations both returned rc 0; the plan kept one while the ledger recorded both (P3).

name: Read-only surfaces that actually write
statement: Status, report, hook or audit commands assumed read-only can still write (git objects, index.lock, bytecode, caches, smoke evidence), mutating what later checks see.
note: keep: verify read-only claims with before/after filesystem snapshots, including .git.
threat: An active Stop wrote loose git objects; resume --dry-run created objects; hooks wrote .pyc; a read-only git status created index.lock (P3/P4).

name: Verifier weakened during reduction
statement: Deleting or loosening tests/checks while simplifying removes security coverage, and reports may still claim that coverage passes.
note: keep: pin G1's test inventory and fail when a check disappears.
threat: Five security-boundary tests vanished while the report said they 'continue to pass' (P3).

name: Tests depend on live mutable state
statement: Tests that read live harness state (e.g., counting completed tasks) go red once the task under test completes, making every later Public Verify fail.
note: keep: G1 acceptance tests must be hermetic or pinned to frozen IDs.
threat: The suite was 280/281 after the task's own completion; the implementer's '281 passed' held only pre-completion (P3).

name: Caller overrides contract-declared evidence
statement: Letting the verifier's caller substitute evidence targets (e.g., --artifact) lets completion succeed on artifacts the contract never declared.
note: keep: the agent never chooses which evidence G1 checks.
threat: verify --artifact other.txt then complete succeeded for a task declaring artifact.txt (P3, pre-existing).

name: Unbounded scope accepted as bounded
statement: Path validators that normalize '.' to an empty path accept the entire repository as a 'bounded' task scope.
note: keep: canonicalize, then reject root-equivalent or escaping scopes.
threat: A selected task with Allowed path '.' claimed the whole repo and could declare protected files as artifacts (P2).

name: Text-pattern oracles defeated by paraphrase
statement: Keyword/regex checkers over prose (giant-task detection, spec contradiction corpus) are bounded oracles that paraphrased or gutted-but-consistent text passes.
note: drop: never rely on text matching of model output for safety; gate on executed evidence.
threat: 'Deliver the whole local release candidate end to end' passed the giant-task filter (P3); gutted obligation bodies pass the spec checker (P2-info).

name: Claiming another process's operation
statement: Attributing any observed new state change to 'my' invocation lets a run claim a registration caused by a peer or external writer.
note: modify: attribute effects via G1's own recorded tool-call IDs, not a model-echoed nonce.
threat: Two concurrent selectors both reported selected/task-beta though one child failed (P3); the nonce is correlation, not authentication (argv-visible).

name: Goal completion by self-declared coverage
statement: A final task whose contract merely declares it checked every terminal property can yield goal_complete if its Public Verify is weak.
note: modify: G1 maps each terminal property to a check it runs itself.
threat: A weak-but-textually-final completed task would report goal_complete (P3).

name: Digest blind to mode and file type
statement: A source digest that omits executable bits or type tags misses meaningful changes (chmod +x, file/symlink swaps, symlink-to-dir) and misclassifies them as no progress.
note: keep: G1's workspace fingerprint includes type and exec bit and fails on special files.
threat: chmod 0644 to 0755 and same-content file/symlink swaps were classified no_durable_progress (P2/P3).

name: Out-of-band tampering reported as clean
statement: Direct edits to completed or parked task records (criteria, objective, status resurrection) leave report/doctor clean when integrity checks skip non-current tasks or short-circuit on the active branch.
note: keep: cross-check every task record against its ledger anchors each turn.
threat: Flipping a completed criterion [x] to [ ] and editing Status: complete to active stayed silent (P2/P3).

name: No-op turn counted as progress
statement: A turn that exits 0 without any durable change, if reported as ordinary 'active', lets a loop spin forever.
note: keep: progress is a harness-measured durable delta, never the agent saying it progressed.
threat: A no-op fake codex was reported active (exit 10) indefinitely.

name: Loops that never converge
statement: Execution loops oscillate between equivalent states (A to B to A, verify-only history churn) or run unbounded unless state is fingerprinted and turns/episodes are hard-capped.
note: keep: fingerprint semantic state, not history, and hard-cap turns.
threat: A-B-A cycles and verify-only appends that never finish the task.

name: Child process hangs without deadline
statement: Without a wall-clock deadline per child invocation, one hung or partially-writing child blocks the controller forever; turn counts bound count, not duration.
note: keep: every process G1 launches gets a hard deadline.
threat: Sleeping selector/active children and a grandchild holding stdout hung the supervisor (P2).

name: Unbounded child output capture
statement: Capturing a child's whole stdout before size validation lets a flooding child exhaust controller memory.
note: keep: cap every captured stream G1 reads.
threat: An infinite producer drove supervisor RSS to 3.2 GiB in 6 s (P2).

name: Descendants escape and keep mutating
statement: Children and grandchildren outside a managed process group, or orphaned by a hard-killed parent, keep running and mutating state, and a restarted controller can overlap them.
note: modify: prefer cgroups/PID namespaces where available; POSIX groups cannot catch setsid escapes.
threat: Supervisor SIGKILL left its adapter alive and a replacement started a second adapter (P2); setsid/double-fork descendants survive (P3/P4 residual).

name: Stale terminal outcome accepted
statement: Accepting a child's terminal outcome (complete/blocked) without post-cleanup revalidation lets descendant writes after the decision make it stale.
note: keep: re-verify after all child processes are reaped, never at the moment of the claim.
threat: A grandchild's write landed after the direct child emitted complete, and the supervisor emitted task_complete anyway (P3).

name: Single-flight keyed to wrong identity
statement: A mutual-exclusion lock keyed to a script inode instead of the protected resource lets copies bypass it and serializes unrelated repositories.
note: keep: key locks to the workspace identity.
threat: A byte-identical copy at another inode ran concurrently in the same repo (P4).

name: Protocol validator fidelity errors
statement: Inter-process protocol validators can be too strict (rejecting reachable legitimate outcomes) or too loose (accepting unpinned informational fields).
note: keep: derive the accepted alphabet from the producer's reachable states and test against the real producer.
threat: turn_budget_exhausted after a final no_durable_progress turn was misreported as protocol_error (P2); resealed evidence with altered informational fields verified (P4).

name: Done versus next-task ambiguity
statement: A stateless turn boundary cannot distinguish 'goal achieved' from 'next task not yet registered', so a loop stops after one task or needs a giant task or hidden memory.
note: modify: G1 needs an explicit terminal spec so 'no work' is never mistaken for 'done'.
threat: The supervisor stopped after task A with no path to a second task.

name: Spec bloat with dead constructs
statement: Normative specs accumulate dead symbols, removable formulas and duplicated statements that cost interpretation without adding rejection power.
note: keep: keep G1's rule spec minimal and mutation-tested.
threat: Four dead symbols, two removable formula blocks and prose/formula duplication (P2); 9 axioms reducible to 5 (P3).

name: Checker overfit to current prose
statement: A checker of hard-coded strings rejects meaning-preserving smaller rewrites, blocking legitimate simplification.
note: keep: pair every negative corpus with a positive equivalence corpus.
threat: About 115 hard-coded strings rejected glyph variants and paraphrases of required sentences (P2).

name: Host-specific instruction leaks into repo
statement: Host-specific standing instructions (a fixed /sdcard draft copy) in always-read instructions get applied wrongly and leak residue into the verified tree.
note: keep: lint G1's injected instructions for host paths, not just the spec.
threat: A relative-path copy created sdcard/abc/t1/draft/... inside the repo, which entered source_digest and the verified tree (P3/P4).

name: Scope creep into unneeded subsystems
statement: Agents add subsystems without proven need (tool classifier, routing/delegation, resume loops, migration, private oracle, context rollover), expanding attack surface and leaking authority.
note: keep: require a reproduced need before G1 grows a component.
threat: Route/delegate was always imported and the sole writer of invalidation events; rollover was proposed without an observed need.

name: Derived artifacts mistaken for authority
statement: Caches, backups and reports that look canonical can be consumed as authority or go stale silently.
note: keep: G1 recomputes views; it never trusts a cached verdict.
threat: A write-only cache with zero readers and a backup that could be mistaken for truth.

name: Fake or redirected provider passes as real
statement: Environment overrides (base URL, fake-boundary flags, PATH shadowing) can swap the real agent/provider for a mock while evidence still looks like a real run.
note: keep: record binary hash and effective env for every agent process G1 observes.
threat: Mock transport or a shadowed codex binary producing E2E evidence.

name: Frozen evidence tampered and resealed
statement: Self-describing evidence documents can be edited and resealed unless a canonical self-hash, an external receipt and a broad tamper matrix pin every gated field.
note: keep: seal G1 evidence with an external anchor; a self-hash alone is resealable.
threat: Resealed variants changing informational fields or adding a fake process record still verified (P4).

name: Hidden context smuggled as continuity
statement: Continuity that silently relies on hidden conversation, memory or session state passes ordinary tests yet violates reconstruction-only continuity.
note: experiment: adopt the marker/nonce test to prove G1 continuity is reconstruction-only.
threat: An agent recovering a value only present in prior conversation context.

name: Model prose drives control decisions
statement: Controllers that parse model text or unstable output to decide outcomes can be steered by the model.
note: keep: G1 branches only on harness-observed facts, never on LLM text.
threat: A model printing 'goal complete' or crafted text to steer the loop.

name: Implementer reports overclaim or understate
statement: Implementation reports overstate results (fixed in production, no new P1, tests pass, check counts) or understate severity and omit residual attack paths.
note: keep: treat every agent report as a list of claims to re-execute.
threat: 'Production failure fixed' and 'no new P0/P1' were false; F11 severity understated; tail truncation omitted from residuals; smoke checks miscounted.

name: Premature completion claims
statement: Agents claim completion before verification exists or present historical completion as current verification.
note: keep: a 'done' message without a G1-observed receipt is logged as a false claim.
threat: A report asserts done while no verification_succeeded receipt exists.

name: Remediations introduce regressions
statement: A fix for one finding can create new failure modes (stuck states, weakened legacy checks) unless the whole boundary is re-audited, including crash windows.
note: keep: re-run the full adversarial matrix after every fix.
threat: The G1 race fix created the H1 permanent stuck state; core isolation dropped manifest checks a prior audit relied on.

name: Self-approval and non-independent audit
statement: An implementer approving its own work, or an audit drawing on auxiliary models/subagents, cannot count as verification.
note: keep: the agent under test never grades itself.
threat: An implementer signing off its own claims.

name: Fresh ephemeral one-shot agent turn
statement: Each agent turn must be a new, ephemeral, non-resumed agent process whose only authority is the repository plus canonical harness state.
note: modify: one `omp -p --mode json` process per turn with no session continuation; the harness composes the prompt from repo state.
threat: Hidden conversational or session continuity steering work or acting as completion authority.

name: Fail-closed canonical integrity preflight
statement: Before and after every turn the harness must re-derive state and abort unless the ledger is ready with no pending recovery, plan and ledger agree, issues are empty, task ids are unique, at most one task is active, and every task contract is anchored to its latest registration receipt.
note: keep: G1 recomputes state itself before and after trusting any turn.
threat: Acting on corrupted, ambiguous or silently edited plan/ledger state.

name: Durable-delta progress snapshot
statement: A turn counts as progress only when a harness-computed snapshot (source digest, task contract/status/criteria/verification fields, ledger seq and tail hash) differs before vs after the turn.
note: keep: progress is a harness-observed diff, never an agent statement.
threat: Agent claiming progress without durable change; idle turns burning budget.

name: Observed state outranks agent exit code
statement: Turn outcome is classified from re-observed canonical state; the agent exit code may only turn a still-active task into agent_failed and never creates or cancels a terminal state.
note: keep: core evidence-only rule.
threat: Trusting agent self-report (exit 0 = done) or losing a real completion because the agent crashed afterwards.

name: Completion only when receipt-bound
statement: A task may be reported complete only if its projection is complete with valid history, an explicit completion binding, an integer authoritative receipt seq, and no current task.
note: keep: completion must point at a harness-recorded verification receipt.
threat: Plan text edited to 'Status: complete' without a verification receipt.

name: Task identity fixed across a turn
statement: The task observed after a turn and reported by every child must equal the task that was active (or selected) before it; identity drift is a protocol or canonical error.
note: keep.
threat: Agent swapping or re-registering tasks to escape a failing one.

name: Single typed result line per runner
statement: Each runner prints exactly one compact sorted-key JSON line with a closed key set and a typed outcome whose exit code is a fixed function of the outcome; agent output goes to stderr and unexpected exceptions become typed internal errors, never tracebacks.
note: keep: with omp --mode json, keep harness verdicts on a channel separate from agent events.
threat: Agent output spoofing harness results; ambiguous or secret-leaking failure output.

name: Precondition-gated zero-write launch
statement: An adapter must not launch the agent or mint a nonce unless its precondition holds (active task for execution; no active task and a valid goal for selection; agent binary present); otherwise it returns a typed not-applicable/unavailable result without writes.
note: keep.
threat: Wasted or unattributable agent runs; double selection after a crash.

name: Selection turn may only register
statement: Task selection is a separate agent turn that may only register a task: source digest, git tree, non-canonical residue and protected files (goal, AGENTS, active adapter) must be byte-identical across it.
note: keep: enforce with omp tool_call filtering plus before/after hashing.
threat: Selector implementing work, planting files or hidden hand-off notes during 'selection'.

name: Per-invocation nonce binds the registration
statement: Each selection run mints a 128-bit random operation id, injects it into the prompt, and attributes a registration only if the new contract contains exactly one line `SELECTION_OPERATION_ID = <id>`.
note: keep: inject via before_agent_start; generalize to bind any agent-produced artifact to the run that produced it.
threat: Pre-staged, replayed, concurrent or externally written registrations being credited to this turn.

name: Closed delta grammar for selection
statement: A selection turn's canonical delta must be either nothing or exactly one new task: prior tasks unchanged, plan append-only, ledger +1 contract_registered with matching id/hash/allowed paths, and the new task sole-active and unprogressed; anything else is protocol_error.
note: keep.
threat: History rewrite, multi-task registration, pre-progressed or pre-verified tasks.

name: Deterministic contract lint at selection
statement: A selected contract must carry six non-vague justification fields, a terminal-property effect, a specific objective, <=8 non-root allowed paths, risk and out-of-scope lines, 6-40 criteria, 1-8 in-scope artifacts, a deterministic verify command and stop conditions, and must not add supervisors, routers or queues.
note: modify: keep the structural bounds; regex vagueness checks are gameable hygiene, not evidence.
threat: Vague, unbounded or self-expanding tasks; smuggled task queues.

name: Normalized fingerprint blocks duplicate selection
statement: A new task whose normalized identity fingerprint (goal ids plus NFKC-casefolded gap/effect fields, excluding the nonce and WHY_THIS_TASK_NOW) equals any existing task's is rejected.
note: modify: exact-normalized match is evaded by rewording; add outcome- or artifact-overlap-based dedupe.
threat: Selection oscillation: re-selecting a blocked or finished task forever.

name: Goal completion derived, never declared
statement: Goal completion is accepted only from a completed final-verification task covering every terminal property whose current verification receipt seq/hash match its latest completion transition; registering nothing is never goal completion.
note: keep: never trust omp goal-mode 'done'; derive goal completion from harness receipts.
threat: Agent declaring the goal done, or idling at a no-active boundary.

name: Exactly one authoritative goal document
statement: Exactly one regular non-symlink master goal file may exist in the repository (outside .git), and it must pass the goal linter before selection or loop observation.
note: keep.
threat: Shadow or duplicate goal documents steering selection; symlinked goal.

name: Bounded turn, episode and time budgets
statement: Work is bounded at every layer: at most 8 active turns per task episode, 32 episodes per loop, and finite nested wall-clock limits (6 h per child, 60 h per episode) whose inner budgets fit inside the outer ones.
note: keep.
threat: Unbounded loops, runaway cost, hung turns.

name: Consecutive no-progress stagnation stop
statement: Two consecutive turns without durable progress stop the episode as stalled_no_progress; a progressing turn resets the counter.
note: keep.
threat: Spinning turns that never change durable state.

name: Effective-state oscillation detection
statement: Revisiting any previously seen effective-state fingerprint within an episode stops it as stalled_oscillation; the fingerprint covers task fields and source digest but excludes ledger seq/hash so repeated verification churn is not progress.
note: keep.
threat: A->B->A oscillation; re-running verification to look busy.

name: Supervisor re-derives progress itself
statement: After each child turn the supervisor recomputes effective state; a child claiming no progress while state changed is a protocol error, and a child claiming progress with unchanged state is caught as oscillation.
note: keep: every layer re-observes instead of trusting the layer below.
threat: Buggy or tampered adapter misreporting progress.

name: Strict child result validation
statement: A child's stdout is accepted only if it is <=1024 bytes of UTF-8, exactly one non-empty JSON line without duplicate keys or non-finite numbers, with the exact key set, a known outcome whose mapped exit code equals the real exit code, and typed bounded fields consistent with the outcome.
note: keep.
threat: Forged, truncated, smuggled or inconsistent child results.

name: Bounded nonblocking capture with deadline
statement: Child output must be read nonblocking with a hard byte cap (detecting cap+1) under a monotonic deadline; overflow or timeout aborts and the child's process group is killed.
note: keep: apply to omp --mode json streams too (per-line and total bounds).
threat: Infinite output, memory exhaustion, hangs on pipes held by descendants.

name: No automatic retry of failed turns
statement: Any typed failure (agent_failed, protocol_error, canonical_error, unavailable, interrupted) stops the episode and loop immediately; no runner retries a model turn or a launch.
note: keep.
threat: Retry-until-pass masking failures; best-of-N cherry-picking.

name: Process-group cleanup on every exit path
statement: Every child runs in its own session/process group and is TERM'd, given a grace period, KILL'd and waited before its result is accepted, on success, error, timeout and SIGTERM alike.
note: keep: G1 must own the whole omp process tree, including bash-tool children.
threat: Leftover descendants mutating state after a verdict; orphaned agents.

name: Single-flight supervisor lock
statement: Only one supervisor episode may run at a time; contention returns supervisor_busy without side effects and the kernel releases the lock if the holder dies.
note: modify: lock the repository/state directory (as RUN-27 does), not the script inode.
threat: Concurrent episodes racing on one repository.

name: Probe kernel supervision primitives before relying
statement: The loop driver must enable and read back PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER, probe PR_SET_PDEATHSIG (set/verify/restore), confirm /proc lists itself, and give each child PDEATHSIG=SIGTERM with a parent-changed race check, failing closed if any primitive is missing.
note: keep: Linux-only primitives, but probe-before-rely is a portable principle.
threat: Assuming orphan cleanup works on a kernel or emulator where it silently does not; driver death orphaning an episode.

name: Reconcile adopted descendants to zero
statement: After each episode every descendant (including orphans adopted by the subreaper) must be found via a /proc ppid walk, TERM'd then KILL'd by group or pid, and reaped until none remain; no episode may start while any descendant exists.
note: keep.
threat: Detached grandchildren overlapping the next episode or mutating state after completion.

name: Repository guard lock with race check
statement: The driver holds a nonblocking exclusive flock on the repository's state directory, opened O_NOFOLLOW|O_DIRECTORY and verified by dev/inode equality before and after open.
note: keep.
threat: Two loops on one repository; symlink or rename swap of the state directory.

name: Re-verify terminal claims at the boundary
statement: A child's task_complete or goal_complete is only a hint: after all descendants are reaped the driver independently re-evaluates current receipt-bound completion (projection, current verification, latest transition seq/hash) and rejects stale or unbound claims.
note: keep: the central evidence-only check; run it on omp session_stop.
threat: Stale terminal (a descendant changes an artifact after verification); forged child output.

name: Double-read stable observation for verdicts
statement: A completion verdict requires two consecutive observations to agree on root, ledger seq/tail, source digest, active task and plan tasks, and a repeated completion evaluation to return the same receipt.
note: keep.
threat: TOCTOU with a concurrent or lingering writer during the verdict.

name: Observable state outranks transport errors
statement: After a child timeout or protocol error the driver re-observes canonical state and reports canonical_error if the repository is no longer observable, instead of the transport failure.
note: keep.
threat: A crashing turn leaving corrupted state that is reported only as a timeout.

name: Stateless loop; repository is sole continuity
statement: Runner layers keep only process-local counters and persist no loop, pid or queue state; every episode and turn reconstructs from the repository and canonical ledger.
note: keep.
threat: Hidden runner state becoming a second, unverified authority.

name: Strict layering of the runner stack
statement: The driver launches only the supervisor, the supervisor launches only the two adapters, only adapters launch the agent, and each layer is removable without canonical migration.
note: keep, but hash-pin the launched scripts (see findings).
threat: Policy leaking across layers; untestable monoliths.

name: Sterile per-run agent home
statement: A real-agent proof runs with fresh empty 0700 HOME/agent-home/TMP/XDG directories, an allowlisted environment without global git config, and only the approved auth plus a generated sanitized config admitted.
note: modify: same pattern for omp's config/session/cache directories per run.
threat: Prior sessions, memories, caches or user config leaking context into a 'fresh' run.

name: Reject provider redirection and continuity env
statement: Real-provider runs must refuse provider-redirect or fake-boundary variables and session/thread continuity variables, both inherited and in the constructed child environment.
note: modify: map to omp provider/base-URL and session variables.
threat: Silently testing against a fake or proxy provider, or resuming a prior session.

name: Pinned agent executable identity
statement: The agent binary must resolve to exactly one regular executable whose path, size and sha256 are recorded and version-checked, PATH-shadow checked at launch, and re-verified live by the offline verifier.
note: modify: pin the omp binary/bundle hash.
threat: Binary substitution or PATH shadowing by a wrapper.

name: Out-of-band /proc process trace
statement: Fresh-context claims are proven by the harness sampling /proc for descendants keyed by (pid, start_ticks): exe equals the pinned binary, argv is exec/--ephemeral/--cd fixture without resume/fork/session args, role comes from the ancestor script, and every process exited and was reaped.
note: modify: combine /proc sampling with omp RPC/session events; sampling can miss short-lived processes.
threat: Agent or adapter claiming freshness while reusing a session or long-lived process.

name: Control repository unchanged by fixture run
statement: A proof run in a fixture must leave the control repository's canonical files, protected hashes, source digest and git tree byte-identical, checked live and re-checked by the verifier.
note: keep.
threat: A proof run contaminating the real repository.

name: Pinned protected-file hash inventory
statement: Harness control files are pinned by an approved sha256 inventory (plus an out-of-scope source digest) checked at preflight and by the offline verifier; any drift aborts.
note: keep, and extend it to the production loop's launched scripts.
threat: Agent or operator silently modifying harness code used by the proof.

name: Self-hash sealed evidence
statement: Evidence carries self_hash = sha256 of its canonical JSON with self_hash set to a zero sentinel; verifiers recompute it, and the written file is re-read and re-verified.
note: modify: a self-hash is not authenticity; anchor it in a harness-held key or ledger receipt.
threat: Accidental corruption or partial writes of evidence.

name: Strict exact-key JSON parsing
statement: Evidence, specs and traces are parsed rejecting duplicate keys and NaN/Infinity, then validated with exact key sets at every nesting level.
note: keep.
threat: Parser-differential and schema-smuggling attacks on evidence.

name: Offline re-derivation verifier
statement: Evidence must verify offline with no provider by recomputing everything from embedded raw material: ledger hash chain, artifact bytes, manifest digests, receipt bindings, dependency values and trajectory frontiers.
note: keep.
threat: Evidence checkable only by re-trusting the original run or its operator.

name: One-shot attempt with typed failure evidence
statement: A real-provider proof gets exactly one attempt: pre-existing evidence blocks a rerun, a started attempt that fails writes sealed failure evidence to the same path, and failure evidence can never verify as success.
note: keep.
threat: Best-of-N reruns cherry-picking a lucky success; failures disappearing.

name: No secrets in evidence; credentials unrecorded
statement: Evidence and reports are rejected if they contain token/key/authorization-shaped strings, and credentials are recorded only by class, size and mode, never by content or digest.
note: keep (regex scanning is heuristic in both directions).
threat: Credential leakage through evidence artifacts.

name: Explicit non-claims in evidence
statement: Evidence must carry an exact, verifier-checked list of what is not proven (e.g. provider model identity configured-only, sampled /proc, unlink-not-overwrite, hook trust bypass used).
note: keep.
threat: Overclaiming: evidence read as proving more than was observed.

name: Model text is never evidence
statement: Evidence and reports may not contain prompts, transcripts, response text, session/thread ids, raw model output or chain-of-thought; only harness-observed facts are recorded.
note: keep: core paranoid rule.
threat: Agent prose being laundered into authoritative evidence.

name: Disposable genesis fixture for proofs
statement: Behavioral proofs run in a disposable fixture built outside the control repo from approved bytes, with a zero-task genesis ledger, empty git history and an asserted initial observation.
note: keep.
threat: Proofs contaminated by prior history, or polluting the real repository.

name: Cross-task dependency recovered from receipts
statement: A later task must recover earlier-task facts (artifact hash, verification receipt seq/hash, completion hash) from canonical ledger evidence and be registered after that completion; the verifier recomputes the binding and order.
note: keep.
threat: Hand-off via prompt or session instead of durable evidence; out-of-order tasks.

name: Context-identity chain per durable step
statement: Each durable step records the pinned-binary process identity (pid, start_ticks, exe sha256) that produced it, the previous step hash, a chain commitment, verified-dead predecessors and a pre-frontier; one context may produce at most one step.
note: experiment: useful for proving per-turn freshness on omp.
threat: One long context faking several 'fresh' contexts; step reordering.

name: In-band claims cross-checked by observer
statement: An in-band step is accepted only if the out-of-band tracer independently observed the same live process identity, all predecessors were reaped with clean boundary scans, and no two active contexts overlapped.
note: modify: keep observer output in harness-private storage, not the agent workspace.
threat: Agent fabricating a context identity; overlapping contexts sharing memory.

name: Frontier hash adjacency chain
statement: Each active context records pre/post frontiers (ledger seq/tail, plan sha, source digest, tree hash); consecutive contexts must be adjacent and an offline replay of step manifests must reproduce every frontier.
note: keep: a per-turn frontier chain is a cheap G1 trajectory proof.
threat: Hidden work between contexts; spliced or reordered trajectories.

name: Git-free tree hash re-derivation
statement: Verifiers recompute git blob/tree ids and the source digest from a file manifest without invoking git, and require the loose-object set and .git admin hash to match exactly (no packs).
note: modify: worth it only if G1 must verify without trusting git.
threat: Hidden commits/objects as hand-off channels; trusting a possibly tampered git binary.

name: Boundary scan for hidden channels
statement: At every context boundary the fixture's source paths, .harness paths, git admin hash, git object set and ignored caches must exactly match the expected stage, else CONTEXT_RESIDUE_PRESENT.
note: keep.
threat: Notes, caches or git objects carrying context to the next fresh turn.

name: Disposable runtime root per invocation
statement: Every agent invocation gets a brand-new opaque runtime root (home, agent home, tmp, xdg, sqlite, rollout) created in an empty parent, never reusing a prior root id or inode, and deleted before the next invocation starts.
note: modify: point omp's config/session/cache directories at a per-turn temp root.
threat: Agent-internal databases or rollouts carrying context between 'fresh' turns.

name: PATH-interposed launcher wrapper
statement: The harness places its own launcher first on PATH under the agent's name so unchanged adapters' invocations are forced through exact argv validation (`exec --ephemeral --cd <fixture> <prompt>`, no continuation args) and isolation.
note: modify: on omp prefer SDK/RPC launch control over a PATH shim.
threat: Adapters or agents invoking the agent outside the isolation boundary.

name: Guarded auth-file copy
statement: Only the approved auth file is copied: read O_NOFOLLOW, owner-only 0600, single link, bounded size, allowed JSON keys only (no context-bearing keys), written O_EXCL 0600 into the runtime; its source identity (dev, inode, size, mtime, sha256) must be unchanged at genesis and after the run.
note: modify: same rules for omp's auth/token store.
threat: Credential tampering, token refresh written back to the real source, context smuggled through auth.

name: Fresh pinned sanitized agent config
statement: Agent configuration is generated fresh per run from a pinned template (model, reasoning effort, tier, approval never, hooks/plugins/apps/multi-agent off) with its template hash recorded; no user config is inherited.
note: modify: generate omp settings per run and pin model roles explicitly.
threat: User config enabling plugins, hooks or providers that alter behavior or leak context.

name: Syscall-entry write-boundary tracer
statement: The whole agent process tree is ptraced and every mutation-capable syscall is classified at entry by resolved target (runtime/fixture/device/nonpersistent/external); external targets or bypass syscalls (mount, ptrace, bpf, setns, untraced clone, ...) kill the tree before the syscall runs.
note: experiment: only on a real kernel; prefer landlock/bubblewrap/seccomp-notify enforcement over a Python ptrace observer.
threat: Agent writing outside its sandbox (real home, other repos) or escaping observation.

name: Fd hygiene and io_uring denial
statement: Before exec the traced child starts a new session, sets PDEATHSIG=SIGKILL, closes all inherited fds >=3, sets NO_NEW_PRIVS and installs a seccomp filter returning ENOSYS for io_uring_setup so every write stays ptrace-observable.
note: keep if any syscall-level containment is attempted.
threat: Inherited writable fds or io_uring submissions bypassing entry-time observation.

name: Emulated-ptrace syscall decoder fallback
statement: When PTRACE_GET_SYSCALL_INFO is unsupported (nested PRoot), syscall stops are decoded from aarch64 registers via GETREGSET with per-tracee entry/exit phase tracking, and the decoder used is recorded in evidence.
note: drop: nested PRoot ptrace cannot prove termination/reap (EXITKILL unimplemented); run on a real kernel or make no containment claim.
threat: Misdecoded syscalls under PRoot's partial ptrace emulation.

name: Exactly one pinned agent process
statement: Each invocation must observe exactly one process image of the pinned agent binary in the traced tree; zero or several is PROCESS_IDENTITY_AMBIGUOUS.
note: modify: admit known self re-exec (tool helpers) or the rule self-defeats; currently untested.
threat: A wrapper or substitute executing instead of, or alongside, the pinned agent.

name: Hash-chained lifecycle trace on fixed schedule
statement: Invocation lifecycles are appended as genesis/process/cleanup triplets to an owner-only, fsynced, hash-chained trace (seq, previous hash, run id) checked against a fixed role schedule derived from the parent adapter; partial, resealed, out-of-order, extra or wrong-role invocations fail, and an incomplete predecessor blocks successors.
note: keep, with the trace outside agent write reach (a plain hash chain is re-sealable by any writer).
threat: Replayed or forged lifecycle records; surplus provider invocations.

name: No live references before deleting a root
statement: Before deleting a runtime root the harness must find zero mounts, cwd/root/fd/mmap references and AF_UNIX sockets into it across same-UID processes, and no symlink or hardlink crossing out of it.
note: keep.
threat: Live processes retaining authority over 'deleted' state; links smuggling state out.

name: Continuity-bearing runtime artifacts forbidden
statement: Agent-generated artifacts that can carry context across invocations (sessions, threads, histories, memories, rollouts, sqlite stores, installation ids, mutated config, unknown files) must stay confined to the per-invocation root and be destroyed or rejected; unclassified means forbidden, and only byte-pinned markers may be admitted.
note: modify: enumerate omp's own session/memory stores and isolate them per turn.
threat: Agent runtime databases or memories acting as a hidden continuity channel.

name: TOCTOU-safe exact file reads
statement: Security-relevant files are read via lstat, O_NOFOLLOW open and fstat equality (dev, inode, mode, uid, gid, nlink, size), requiring a single link, the expected owner/mode and a size bound.
note: keep.
threat: Symlink/hardlink swaps and concurrent replacement of files being verified.

name: Hash-pinned import of reused verifier code
statement: Verifier code reused from an earlier runner is imported only if the file's sha256 equals a pinned constant and the expected attribute surface exists.
note: keep.
threat: Silently changed shared verifier logic weakening later proofs.

name: No stale loop processes at preflight
statement: A run may not start while any goal-loop, supervisor, adapter, launcher or ephemeral agent process matching the exact argv shape is alive.
note: keep.
threat: Leftover processes from an earlier run writing into the new run.

name: Provider-free scripted mock model
statement: Agent-runtime integration is tested against a loopback mock Responses server that issues scripted tool calls and records the tool outputs it receives, so command execution is observed at the transport instead of being narrated by a model.
note: modify: register a mock provider for an omp model role and assert on recorded tool_call events.
threat: Tests depending on a live provider, or trusting model narration of tool results.

name: Real home and harness state unchanged
statement: An agent run must use an isolated temporary agent home and prove that the real home's stable config/auth files and the harness's canonical state bytes are hash-identical before and after.
note: modify: snapshot omp's real config dir; note the snapshot skips volatile session/log/sqlite stores.
threat: Agent runs mutating the operator's real configuration or the canonical ledger.

name: Strip root-redirect env and workspace PATH
statement: Child agent environments drop repository/git redirection variables (HARNESS_ROOT, GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE, GIT_INDEX_FILE) and PATH entries inside the workspace, and replace HOME/TMPDIR.
note: keep.
threat: Redirecting the harness at another repository or shadowing tools with workspace binaries.

name: Single allowlisted chat, silent drop
statement: The remote gateway acts only on updates whose chat id equals the single configured id and silently ignores every other chat.
note: modify: also allowlist the sender user id (a group chat id admits every member).
threat: Unauthorized Telegram users triggering agent jobs; oracle responses to probers.

name: Bot token never leaves the gateway
statement: The bot token must never appear in repr, errors, child environments, results or chat: errors are redacted with exception chains suppressed, the child env drops TG_* and any value containing the token or chat id, results are redacted, and raw agent diagnostics are withheld.
note: keep.
threat: Credential leakage via tracebacks, logs, the agent environment or chat messages.

name: Remote jobs refuse full-access sandbox
statement: Remotely triggered agent runs may only use read-only (default) or workspace-write sandboxing; danger-full-access is a configuration error.
note: keep: map to omp tool permissions/approval policy.
threat: A remote message granting unrestricted host access.

name: Bounded validated attachments
statement: Attachments must match strict file-id/path/media-type patterns (no traversal), agree on declared, getFile and downloaded sizes under a 20 MB cap, be materialized 0600 in a job-private temp dir with a sha256, never be auto-extracted, and be deleted after the job.
note: keep if G1 exposes a remote channel.
threat: Path traversal, oversized or size-shifting downloads, archive bombs.

name: Durable ack before side effect
statement: The next update offset is durably persisted (temp file, fsync, atomic replace, directory fsync; 0600 file in an owner-only directory outside the repo) before an update is dispatched, so a crash never replays a job.
note: keep: at-most-once for any externally triggered job.
threat: Duplicate job execution after a crash or restart; offset tampering through the repo.

name: One cancellable job at a time
statement: The gateway runs at most one agent job, launched without a shell in its own process group with the prompt on stdin and a wall-clock timeout; cancel or timeout terminates the whole group TERM then KILL.
note: keep.
threat: Job pile-up, shell injection via argv, orphaned agents after cancel.

name: Content-free progress reporting
statement: Remote progress is derived only from event types and counts in the agent's JSONL stream, never from event content, with per-line and total log size bounds.
note: modify: map from omp --mode json event types.
threat: Leaking code, secrets or model reasoning to a remote channel.

name: Same-model retry; no silent model switch
statement: Provider capacity errors may be retried only with the same model, with bounded exponential backoff inside the job deadline; exhaustion is reported explicitly and the model is never substituted.
note: keep: pin omp model roles and record the model actually used.
threat: Silent downgrade to a different model invalidating evidence assumptions.

name: Gateway preflight and fail-closed config
statement: Before polling, the gateway validates token shape, a real git repository root, absolute non-symlink state/temp paths outside the repo, bounded numeric knobs, the agent binary on PATH, a bot identity and the absence of a webhook.
note: keep: harness state must live outside the agent-writable workspace.
threat: Misconfiguration placing harness state inside the agent workspace, or competing update consumers.

name: Harness-run checks gate Stop, but opt-in
statement: At Stop the harness runs the accepted contract's machine checks itself and, if any fails, may refuse the stop (agy: continue) at most MaxStopBlocks=2 times per user prompt, but in the default 'recommend' rollout this block never fires because s5.stop_unmet can only block after advice for it was delivered, and that advice is only ever produced by the block itself.
proof_purpose: The harness's own checks fail on the current tree, so allowing the stop would be a false completion.
note: G1's Stop hook always runs its own verification (no opt-in), writes a receipt, and returns continue with the receipt digest and failing criteria while the control vector shows displacement; it counts its own continues in the ledger (cap well under agy's 10) instead of relying on host flags.

name: Discard check results if identity changed mid-run
statement: A harness-run checkpoint result is applied only if the contract revision, task id and intent revision are unchanged and no observation was lost between the start and end of the run; otherwise every result is marked not passed and skipped.
proof_purpose: The verification receipt describes the same contract, intent revision and tree that existed when it started and when it ended.
note: G1 records contract hash and tree hash before and after its verification run and writes the receipt only if both are equal; any skipped, side-effecting or interrupted criterion makes completion fail closed.
novelty: duplicate-of:T1 completion gate binding current source and tree (TOCTOU variant)

name: Grader outside agent tree, digest-pinned
statement: In the benchmark harness a trial counts as verified only when a grader copied outside the agent-writable repo exits 0, and the task tree and the grader copy hash identically before the agent ran, before grading and after grading.
proof_purpose: The acceptance oracle G1 ran is byte-identical to the contracted oracle and was outside the agent's write reach for the whole run.
note: G1 stores acceptance checks under a G1-owned directory outside the workspace, pins their tree digest in the contract hash, re-digests before and after each Stop verification, and voids the receipt on any mismatch or link.
novelty: duplicate-of:T1 self-run verification in a scrubbed environment (adds an oracle kept outside the agent-writable tree with pre/post oracle digests)

name: Graders must observe expected behavior, not exit 0
statement: Benchmark graders run the candidate in a subprocess and compare exact expected outputs, and the suite proves that an emptied test file or a 'raise SystemExit(0)' submission fails.
proof_purpose: A criterion passed because the expected behavior was observed, not because a process exited 0.
note: Contract lint: every acceptance criterion's check must assert concrete expected output; G1's contract test suite includes an exit(0) stub and an emptied-test mutant that must both fail, otherwise the contract is rejected (zero row in the coverage matrix).

name: Seal pins evaluator, config and price versions
statement: Every session seal records the evaluator version, the hash of the effective merged config and the price-table version next to the chain head, and verification fails on any version mismatch or when a reopened observation makes the stored analysis stale.
proof_purpose: The completion receipt was produced by G1 version V under the exact merged hook policy H, and nothing was observed after it.
note: Add G1's evaluator version and the SHA-256 of the effective merged policy (global plus workspace hooks.json plus G1 config) to every receipt; any later event for the task or a version/policy mismatch at re-check voids the receipt.
novelty: duplicate-of:T1 completion gate binding receipt seq and hash (adds evaluator/policy version binding)

name: Imported evidence never becomes authority
statement: A handoff bundle is strictly decoded and treated as history: a past pass becomes reusable only if the receiver independently accepted the same contract, recomputes matching local input/environment keys, already holds an identical evidence record in its own ledger, and has no observation gap.
proof_purpose: A fresh agent inherits only facts present in G1's own ledger whose keys still match the current tree and contract.
note: At SessionStart G1 rehydrates only from its ledger; transcripts, memories and agent-written handoff files are data, and an old receipt is trusted only after G1 recomputes its key against the current tree and contract.

name: Strict contract schema with one check per criterion
statement: A contract with any unknown key is invalid as a whole, every done item has exactly one of a machine check (expect exit0) or a manual condition, ids are unique, and globs, budgets and v2 reuse settings are validated.
proof_purpose: The contract parsed exactly and every acceptance criterion maps to at least one deterministic check.
note: Strict decode of G1 contracts; build the criteria x checks coverage matrix at load and reject the contract if any row is zero (manual-only criteria count as zero).
novelty: duplicate-of:T1 immutable task contracts with contract hash

name: Checks hash keys reuse; authority hash keys acceptance
statement: The contract has two digests: checks_hash over machine checks keys result reuse, while authority_hash over the canonical JSON of the whole contract decides whether an acceptance is valid, so editing any field (goal, scope, budget, forbid, temporal requirement) makes the acceptance stale and a redirect revokes it before any edit.
proof_purpose: This pass ran under exactly contract authority A, and no completion binds to a superseded contract.
note: Receipt keys include the full contract hash; a superseded contract hash is recorded in the ledger at the moment the goal changes, before any agent edit.
novelty: duplicate-of:T1 immutable task contracts with contract hash

name: HMAC-signed acceptance with a home-directory key
statement: Contract acceptance records are MACed with HMAC-SHA256 under a random 32-byte key in the user's home, so agent-written or copied state files are treated as stale, but the key is readable by the agent's own OS user and only accepted states are checked.
proof_purpose: none: a MAC under a key the agent's OS user can read is not tamper-evident against the agent.

name: User-origin contiguous intent revisions, explicit redirects
statement: A task's goal revisions are contiguous, require user-origin provenance assigned by the ingress adapter (never tool output or imported text), are idempotent on exact replay and conflict on overwrite, and only fixed prefixes ('Change goal:', '목표 변경:', '/samcheonpo:edit') redirect the goal.
proof_purpose: Goal revision n descends from a user-role transcript record at (conversation, step), and no tool output ever amended the goal.
note: G1 derives user origin only from host-structured USER_INPUT transcript records; an explicit marker appends revision n+1, which supersedes older evidence and requires a new contract hash.
novelty: duplicate-of:T1 immutable task contracts with contract hash

name: Protected-path deny with canonical paths
statement: With an accepted contract, any write or edit whose canonical project-relative path matches a protected glob, falls outside the root, or touches tests when the contract forbids test changes is denied before it runs at every rollout stage.
proof_purpose: No agent tool call modified G1's protected set (both hooks.json files, G1 state, contract, pinned oracle files) through a write tool.
note: G1's fail-closed PreToolUse denies write/edit tools whose symlink-resolved canonical target is in the protected set or outside the workspace, denies run_command calls whose text names a protected path, and re-hashes the protected set at Stop to catch any other write.

name: Test-weakening heuristics versus oracle-file pinning
statement: Patches to pre-existing tests that remove tests or assertions, add skips or identity assertions, swap real targets for mocks, change test infrastructure, or source patches that add error-hiding constructs are flagged by regex counts, and some are denied before they land, but shell writes bypass all of it.
proof_purpose: Replaced in G1 by an exact fact: every contract-pinned oracle file (tests, test configs, conftest, fixtures) is byte-identical to its contracted digest.
note: The contract lists oracle files (seeded from the name catalog plus explicit declarations) with SHA-256 digests; write tools to them are denied in PreToolUse and any digest change voids completion at Stop; the regexes survive only as measured warnings.

name: Irreversible actions require a fresh passing receipt
statement: A release, publish or tag-push command is gated on a passing check after the last code change and after any observed CI failure, and on a rate limit of 2 releases per hour, with command classification done by regex.
proof_purpose: No irreversible action left the machine without a passing G1 receipt bound to the current tree hash.
note: G1 PreToolUse denies run_command calls the adapter classifies as publish/release/tag-push unless the latest G1 receipt passed and matches the current tree hash; classification stays in the agy adapter.

name: Past the ceiling only reads are allowed
statement: Once active time or fresh tokens exceed a configured or contracted ceiling, every call that is not read-only is denied before it runs, and only an explicit user extension lifts it.
proof_purpose: No mutation happened after the contract's declared budget was exhausted.
note: If a contract declares a hard limit (for example a maximum number of G1 Stop continuations or verifications), G1 enforces it as a deterministic deny of mutating tools; there is no in-session extension, only a new contract hash.
novelty: duplicate-of:T1 bounded loops (read-only degradation is new)

name: Observation gaps poison completion
statement: Any event the harness failed to process (queue overflow, worker panic, storage error) increments a sticky, monotone, persisted gap counter, and while it is non-zero no intervention is emitted, no checks run, criteria count as unmet and no receipt is issued.
proof_purpose: G1 observed every tool step of the task: stepIdx is contiguous, every PreToolUse has a PostToolUse or a transcript result, and every hook run journaled start and finish.
note: G1 keeps a monotone per-task gap counter fed by stepIdx contiguity, Pre/Post pairing and transcript parse failures; any gap makes completion fail closed, while PreToolUse guardrail denies stay active regardless.

name: Unknown is a third state, never pass
statement: Every measured or verified field is tri-state: missing usage, prices, quota or checks stay unknown instead of becoming zero or pass, deferred judgments carry a named reason, and tool calls without a result are recorded as not executed.
proof_purpose: A completion predicate is evaluated only over known facts; unknown never satisfies it.
note: G1's ledger stores every criterion result and every tool call as tri-state (pass/fail/unknown; executed/denied/unknown) with a reason code; the completion gate treats unknown as fail and the control layer treats it as non-progress.

name: Evidence-basis table decides who may deny
statement: Rules are classed by evidence: user-set limits (protected path, budget, ceiling) always block, rules backed by observable facts may escalate without a contract, rules judging scope, completion or ratios need an accepted contract, and estimated or model-judged rules never block.
proof_purpose: Every deny G1 issues is traceable to a mechanism whose evidence class is a G1-produced deterministic fact.
note: G1 keeps a static table mapping each mechanism to its evidence class (G1-run check, exact hash, host payload, heuristic); PreToolUse denies and Stop continuations may use only the first two classes, enforced by a unit test over the table.

name: Rule authority bound to an evaluation digest
statement: A heuristic rule can only block in 'validated' mode when the operator declared, in the user config, a 32-byte SHA-256 digest of the evaluation report justifying it; nothing is pre-approved and the project config can only drop such digests.
proof_purpose: A rule's or injected variant's promotion is bound to the exact measurement artifact that justified it.
note: Any G1 rule or injection variant promoted from experiment to default must reference the SHA-256 of an A/B result file in G1 state; G1 verifies the file exists, hashes equal, and its recorded interval clears the threshold before loading the rule.

name: Regex rule data with pinned test vectors
statement: Every regex list the harness loads (verify commands, failed-test patterns, forced-continue prompts) ships with must-match and must-not-match cases, and a list that fails its own cases is not loaded.
proof_purpose: Each text matcher G1 uses (transcript exit-code parser, request extraction, adapter tool classification) passes its pinned vectors at load time.
note: Every regex in G1's agy adapter is stored with positive and negative fixtures from captured agy 1.1.27 transcripts; a failing vector makes PreToolUse deny and injection hooks emit nothing.

name: Layered config where the workspace can only weaken
statement: Project settings merge on top of user settings under a lattice that lets the repository only lower blocking (mode down to shadow, block cap down to 0) and only turn off egress, judges and experiments, which means an agent-writable file can disarm interventions for the next session.
proof_purpose: The effective policy is no weaker than the global root-of-trust policy.
note: G1 merges ~/.gemini/config/hooks.json (root of trust) with .agents/hooks.json so the workspace can only add denies and tighten limits, uses strict decoding, and hashes the merged policy into receipts; since both layers run and a deny from either wins, G1 also verifies at SessionStart that its global group is byte-identical to the installed record.

name: Evidence key where empty means unknown
statement: Check evidence is keyed by task, revision, check id, command hash, input hash, environment hash, runner version and the accepted contract's authority hash; any empty component makes the key invalid rather than a wildcard, and a past pass is only a candidate until a freshly recomputed key matches.
proof_purpose: This pass was observed for exactly this contract, revision, command, input bytes, scrubbed environment and runner.
note: G1's receipt key is a full SHA-256 over contract hash, criterion id, command, tree id, input digests, scrubbed-environment digest and runner version; an empty component means not reusable, and the default at completion is always to re-run.
novelty: duplicate-of:T1 completion gate binding receipt hash, source, tree and output digests (adds env digest, runner version and empty-is-unknown)

name: Pass needs exit 0, full output, unchanged tree
statement: A harness check passes only with exit 0, no timeout, combined output under the 1 MiB capture cap, and an unchanged workspace tree fingerprint across the run; a changed tree marks the check as a side effect that can never pass.
proof_purpose: The receipt verdict was computed from complete output within the time limit, and the verification did not mutate the tree it certifies.
note: G1 receipts carry exit code, timeout flag, output byte count, truncation flag and before/after tree ids inside the receipt digest; truncated, timed-out or tree-changing runs are FAIL, and dropping a criterion requires a new contract hash, never an automatic skip.

name: Checks run in a detached worktree snapshot
statement: Worktree-isolated checks run in a detached git worktree built from 'git stash create' (or HEAD) plus copied untracked, non-ignored files, so they see current edits without touching the project.
proof_purpose: Verification ran against an immutable snapshot whose commit or tree id equals the certified state.
note: G1 verifies in a detached worktree of a snapshot commit (write-tree plus commit-tree), runs git with hardened options (no fsmonitor, filters or system config), uses a scrubbed environment, and records the snapshot id in the receipt.

name: Process-group kill with bounded pipe wait
statement: Checks run in their own process group (a Job Object attached while suspended on Windows), the whole group is SIGKILLed on timeout, and a 2-second WaitDelay keeps orphans that hold the output pipe from hanging the check.
proof_purpose: No verification process outlives its receipt, and a stuck descendant cannot push the Stop hook past agy's timeout.
note: Keep T1's process-tree reaping and add a WaitDelay-style bound on pipe draining so the Stop hook always finishes inside agy's timeout.

name: Session identity bound to agent and workspace
statement: Session ids must be path-safe and bound to one agent and one project, late hooks cannot resurrect an ended session, and the same id from another agent or project is rejected.
proof_purpose: Event E belongs to conversation C bound to workspace W.
note: G1 validates conversationId as a safe path component before using it, binds it to workspacePaths[0] at first sight, and refuses (deny for PreToolUse, ignore elsewhere) events whose workspace differs.

name: Deterministic, replayable detector state
statement: All S1-S8 detectors are a pure fold over the ordered event sequence with time only from event timestamps, restarts replay stored facts idempotently without issuing new verdicts, and incremental totals are property-tested to equal a full rescan.
proof_purpose: Control state is a pure, idempotent function of the G1 fact log, so any fresh hook process or agent recomputes the same Stop-continuation decision.
note: G1 computes its control vector (pass/fail vector, displacement, revisits) as a pure fold over ledger facts keyed by (conversationId, stepIdx, phase) on every hook invocation, with a property test that incremental and full recomputation agree.

name: Progress means the failing set strictly shrinks
statement: Progress is a pass, or a strict-subset shrink of failing tests or error fingerprints on a comparable harness-run check (same check, command hash and environment hash); repeated non-shrinking failures across changed inputs are a stall, and failure keys that keep changing without shrinking are whack-a-mole.
proof_purpose: Per-turn displacement: the Hamming distance of G1's acceptance vector decreased, or the failing set is a strict subset of the previous one.
note: G1's Stop controller compares the current pass/fail vector of its own checks with the previous receipt; it continues only while the failing set strictly shrinks within k continuations, and stops on zero displacement or a revisit.
novelty: duplicate-of:T1 stagnation and oscillation detection (adds the strict-subset definition and comparability key)
