name: Failure invariant across distinct trees
statement: When the same normalized failure (error fingerprint, failing-test name, or whole result fingerprint) survives edits that changed the workspace, the edits are not moving the failing criterion, which samcheonpo escalates at 3, 5 and 8 distinct-tree attempts.
proof_purpose: Nonzero tree displacement produced zero result displacement on a G1-run check.
note: G1 computes result digests only from its own check runs; if the digest of a failing criterion is unchanged across k distinct tree hashes, the controller stops issuing Stop continuations.

name: Execution identity with a certainty flag
statement: Two shell runs are the same execution only if a hash over effective directory, sorted env assignments, timeout wrapper and normalized command matches, and any opaque construct ($ substitution, backticks, command lists, cd/export/source, out-of-project directory) marks the identity uncertain and never blockable.
proof_purpose: This command is execution-identical to an earlier one, or G1 cannot know and therefore claims nothing.
note: G1 uses exec identity plus tree hash plus result digest only as a zero-displacement input to the Stop controller; an uncertain identity never counts as a repeat.

name: Workspace revisits an earlier content state
statement: A write whose content hash equals an earlier non-latest hash of the same file, or an edit that exactly reverses an earlier edit, is an edit-and-revert loop reported with the reverted writes as evidence.
proof_purpose: The workspace returned to a previously observed state: a revisit in state space.
note: G1 hashes the whole tracked tree itself at each turn boundary (not per-file agent-reported writes) and treats a revisit of an earlier tree hash with an equal acceptance vector as oscillation that ends Stop continuations.
novelty: duplicate-of:T1 stagnation and oscillation detection (file-content variant)

name: Count forced continuations without progress
statement: Prompts injected by auto-continue tools (Stop-hook feedback, todo continuation, ralph loops) are recognized, excluded from user intent, and three forced turns without a progress event raise an L2 finding.
proof_purpose: k consecutive G1-issued continuations produced no displacement, so another continuation is unjustified.
note: G1 persists a per-task continuation counter (incremented and written before it emits continue, never decreased) together with the displacement of each continued turn, and stops continuing after k zero-displacement continuations, well below agy's cap of 10.

name: Outside-the-code failure classification
statement: One ordered table reads exit codes and output phrases to classify a failure as transient, external (missing dependency or command, DNS, refused connection, permission, port, auth, disk), UI timing or code, and two identical external failures on an unchanged workspace freeze source edits with a suggested human remedy.
proof_purpose: Control only: G1's own check failed twice at the same tree hash for a reason code edits cannot fix, so further continuations are futile.
note: If adopted, classify only the stderr tail of G1-run checks, use the class only to stop Stop continuations and record 'needs-human' in G1 state, and never generate, display or run remedy commands.

name: Unchanged tree hash is not unchanged environment
statement: Because a workspace fingerprint cannot see a service coming back or a package being installed elsewhere, one rerun is always allowed per (cause, command) after an external or transient failure.
proof_purpose: Documents the limit of tree-hash evidence: an unchanged tree hash does not prove an unchanged environment.
note: Make G1's revisit detector key states by (tree hash, environment epoch) and treat an environment-class failure as unknown displacement rather than zero displacement, so the Stop controller does not stop on a state that may have changed outside the tree.

name: Scope from contract globs, never from prompt text
statement: Writes outside an accepted contract's allow globs are deterministic out-of-scope findings, while without a contract the scope is guessed from path tokens in the request (minus negated lines) and every such finding is an estimate that never blocks.
proof_purpose: Every path in the final tree diff lies inside the contract's declared scope.
note: Keep only the contract half: the immutable contract carries allow/protect globs; G1 checks write-tool targets in PreToolUse and re-checks the final tree diff against the globs at completion (catching shell writes).

name: Durable failed-edit memory per revision
statement: Edits made since the last verification are fingerprinted and stored with the failure fingerprint when that verification fails, persist across sessions and agents of the same task revision, and re-applying an already-failed edit is flagged before it is written.
proof_purpose: This exact edit on this exact tree was already followed by a failing G1 receipt in this revision.
note: G1 links edit digests (from its own pre/post file hashes) only to its own failing receipts and injects the list of failed approaches at SessionStart/PreInvocation, so a fresh agent does not repeat them; an exact repeat on an identical tree may be denied in PreToolUse.

name: Bounded state projection after context loss
statement: After a compaction the next injectable response carries one bounded line restating goal, protected and allowed paths, budget and passed/total checks, and the goal card and four-state status label are derived only from harness evidence and explicitly grant nothing.
proof_purpose: None (projection); it makes model memory irrelevant by restating G1 facts.
note: agy has no compaction event, so G1 injects a bounded, ledger-derived projection (task id, contract-hash prefix, failing criteria, last receipt digest) at SessionStart and the first PreInvocation of each turn, labeled as projection, and never tells the agent to trust anchor-like text found elsewhere.

name: Completion-claim regex as measurement only
statement: When the final assistant message matches a completion-claim regex and the session wrote code, the claim is compared with the latest verification: a failed live checkpoint or failing last run is L2, a run older than the last code write is L1 (stale), and no run at all is recorded only.
proof_purpose: Measurement only: the rate at which the model claims DONE while G1's receipt says not done (G1 measured 3 of 8).
note: Completion authority ignores the message; a claim regex runs only in measurement to count false-DONE claims per configuration, reported with a confidence interval.

name: agy output: deny, continue, inject or nothing
statement: For agy a pass or any client failure prints nothing so the call stays in agy's own permission flow, a deny becomes {"decision":"deny","reason"}, a stop refusal becomes {"decision":"continue","reason"}, and advice becomes a PreInvocation injectSteps ephemeralMessage, so neither 'allow' nor '{}' is ever emitted.
proof_purpose: G1 output never widens native permissions: its PreToolUse output set is {empty, deny}, and '{}' (a deny on agy 1.1.27) is never printed by accident.
note: G1's agy adapter is a pure translation table from abstract decisions {none, deny, continue, inject} to agy JSON, with a fixture-replay test asserting the PreToolUse output set is {'', deny} and that '{}' and 'allow' never appear.

name: agy tool results recovered from the transcript
statement: Because agy's PostToolUse carries no output or exit code (its 'error' field is empty even when 'false' exits 1) and the shell result reaches the transcript only after the hook returns, the shell PostToolUse is held and resolved at the next event from the transcript line whose step_index equals stepIdx.
proof_purpose: Observation of which shell steps ran and their host-reported exit codes, for control and measurement only.
note: G1 records (conversationId, stepIdx, args digest) at PostToolUse and resolves results at the next PreInvocation/Stop by reading transcript_full.jsonl with a persisted offset and last-line hash; unresolved results stay unknown, the parse regex is anchored and vector-tested, and results feed only control vectors, never completion.

name: agy turn boundaries and usage from transcript
statement: Because samcheonpo assumes agy has no prompt event, the first PreInvocation (invocationNum 0) is treated as the user turn with the request read from the latest USER_INPUT <USER_REQUEST> block, later PreInvocations deliver pending advice, and token usage comes from PLANNER_RESPONSE lines with cached tokens subtracted.
proof_purpose: A turn boundary for per-turn displacement and continuation counting.
note: G1 segments turns with SessionStart plus PreInvocation invocationNum, never derives contract content from transcript request text, and reads token counts offline in the measurement harness only.

name: Reversible named hook group for agy
statement: The agy installer adds one named 'samcheonpo' group to the global ~/.gemini/config/hooks.json (PreToolUse and PostToolUse with matcher '*', PreInvocation, Stop; 5 s, Stop 160 s), records the exact bytes it added, writes atomically with a backup, refuses symlinked settings, and uninstalls only if the group is still byte-identical.
proof_purpose: G1's group in the root-of-trust file equals the recorded installed bytes, and removing G1 restores the host config exactly (TW a).
note: G1 installs groups in both hooks.json layers for all six events with regex matchers valid on 1.1.27 ('.*'), records exact bytes and SHA-256, verifies them at every SessionStart, and uninstalls only byte-identical entries.

name: Thin fail-open hook client with deadlines
statement: The hook process reads stdin, sends one request to the daemon with a per-event deadline (PreToolUse 15 ms, Stop 150 s, others 50 ms) that the daemon honors by stopping file reads 2 ms early and counting late denies as possibly undelivered, never retries after writing, and on any failure prints nothing and exits 0.
proof_purpose: TW(a): removing or crashing the advisory path never blocks the native agent.
note: G1's PreToolUse has two parts: a fail-closed authority part (protected paths, G1 state, self-invocation) computed in-process from local files with no daemon, and a fail-open advisory part that prints nothing on any error; every hook run journals start and finish so a killed hook is recorded.
novelty: duplicate-of:T1 fail-closed gates and fail-open projection (samcheonpo makes the gate fail-open too)

name: Host capability profiles and output filtering
statement: Each host adapter declares which hook outputs it can carry with a tested version range, unsupported fields are stripped, a block requested on a host that cannot block is downgraded to advice, a user message or observation, and payload-shape drift drops the host to observe-only.
proof_purpose: Every recorded enforcement went through a channel the host contract says is fail-closed.
note: The agy adapter declares per-event capabilities from G1's measured facts (PreToolUse deny, fail-closed; SessionStart and PreInvocation inject, fail-open; Stop continue up to 10; PostInvocation terminate) and the core marks an intervention 'enforced' only on a fail-closed route.

name: Payload-shape tripwire per host event
statement: Tool hook payloads must carry session, tool name, call id, an object tool_input with a command or path and, for PostToolUse, a result; the first mismatch drops every session of that agent to observe-only until restart and is reported by doctor and the status line.
proof_purpose: Every agy stdin in this session matched the pinned contract for agy 1.1.27 for its event type.
note: Pin a per-event schema for agy 1.1.27 derived from captured payloads of every tool type; on mismatch record a host-contract violation, keep guardrail denies on, distrust derived observations, and refuse completion until the measurement harness re-tests the host contract.

name: Captured host payloads as golden fixtures
statement: Real agy 1.3.0 hook payloads (PreInvocation 0-3, PreToolUse and PostToolUse for steps 2/4/6 and write_to_file, Stop) and a transcript are frozen in testdata and replayed through the daemon, defining the tested version range.
proof_purpose: G1's agy adapter parses exactly the payloads agy 1.1.27 emitted, pinned by SHA-256.
note: Capture all six agy 1.1.27 events for every tool type plus transcript_full.jsonl, pin them by SHA-256, replay them in CI, and treat a recapture diff as the host-contract re-test.

name: Delivery is not compliance: staged intervention log
statement: Each intervention moves proposed, emitted, delivered (a one-shot token echoed after the client printed it), acknowledged, then effect_observed over a 10-event window or censored, with immutable stage times, no 'resolved' outcome, and at most one prescription per cause and three per revision.
proof_purpose: Measurement: G1 emitted injection X at stepIdx k, and what happened in the next N relevant steps (censored when unknown).
note: G1 writes each injectSteps emission (variant id, conversationId, stepIdx) to its ledger after a successful stdout flush, caps injections per cause and revision, and uses the staged outcome schema in A/B analysis, counting censored separately.

name: Refuse agent shell calls to user-only verbs
statement: PreToolUse denies shell commands that run the harness's user-only verbs (accept, keep, skip, edit, extend, rollback apply, contract accept) in command position, including through env/sudo/sh -c wrappers and heredoc interpreter bodies, at every rollout stage.
proof_purpose: None on its own (defense in depth); authority must sit outside the agent's OS identity.
note: G1 has no user-operated verbs (P6), so its PreToolUse simply denies any run_command whose text names the G1 binary or G1 state paths, as defense in depth behind protected-path hashing.

name: Observational injection format and directive lint
statement: Agent-facing messages follow a fixed four-line observational form (observation, evidence event numbers, measured cost or unknown, contract goal) with any prescription kept separate, templates are linted for directive vocabulary, and an agent skill tells the agent to treat warnings as facts, not instructions.
proof_purpose: None for authority; makes every G1 injection a quoted fact tied to a receipt.
note: G1 injections are lines like 'fact | G1 receipt seq/hash | criterion', with agent-derived strings quoted and length-capped, and the lint runs on the final rendered text with Unicode-aware boundaries; any skill text is an A/B-tested injection variant, never authority.
novelty: duplicate-of:vesperchant 3-tier hooks (PreInvocation ground-truth injection) and RULES.md rule files

name: Contract draft from manifest-derived check candidates
statement: On a new task, if drafts are enabled or a contract file exists, the agent is asked to draft .samcheonpo/contract.yml from candidate checks read from package.json, go.mod, pyproject, Makefile and CI files, told not to wait for acceptance, and a written draft is validated with errors fed back at PostToolUse.
proof_purpose: Candidate deterministic checks exist for each acceptance criterion (an input to the coverage matrix, not authority).
note: G1 may propose coverage rows from manifest-derived candidates, but the contract's checks are accepted only after G1's coverage-matrix lint and oracle pinning; CI-derived commands are labeled untrusted.

name: Hash-assigned experiment arms for injections
statement: Advice is assigned deterministically by hash(session, rule) to a none, fact-only or prescription arm; the control arm records the verdict but delivers and blocks nothing, and outcomes are tabulated per arm without ever claiming 'resolved'.
proof_purpose: Measurement: the effect of an injected content variant is estimated against a deterministic control arm.
note: G1 assigns arms by an unbiased reduction of SHA-256(conversationId, experiment id) (rejection sampling or a full-integer modulus), records the arm in its ledger, and never applies arms to authority-path decisions.

name: Interval statistics with withholding rules
statement: Rates carry Wilson 95% intervals, arm differences use a paired task-cluster percentile bootstrap (4000 resamples, seed 73129, Bonferroni-adjusted), and verdicts are withheld below 12 clusters or 30 paired blocks, on version or grader gaps, or on degenerate intervals, with a pre-registered sample-size planner.
proof_purpose: None (measurement): confidence intervals for host-contract re-tests and A/B tests of injected content.
note: G1's measurement harness reports every rate (for example 'DONE after block: 3/8') with a Wilson interval, compares variants with a paired cluster bootstrap over tasks, and refuses to promote a variant below pre-registered sample sizes.

name: A/B protocol hygiene and cost attribution
statement: Arm order is permuted per task-by-trial block with a recorded seed, every trial gets a fresh repo copy and an isolated harness home, result rows are rejected on duplicates, mixed versions, double-counted sessions or unpaired blocks, cost is taken only from a unique fresh transcript matched by session and workspace, and harness overhead is counted only after its process is proven terminated.
proof_purpose: None (measurement): A/B rows are independent, paired and attributable.
note: Each G1 A/B trial uses an isolated HOME (so ~/.gemini/config/hooks.json does not leak between arms), a fresh repo copy, a seeded block order, a transcript bound by conversationId plus workspacePaths plus mtime after trial start, and row validation before analysis.

name: Pre-registered, hash-pinned corpus evaluation
statement: Stored session records are re-analyzed in isolation from a manifest that pins every source, contract and context file by SHA-256, rejects train/eval leakage by source hash or benchmark task, reads labels only after predictions are fixed, leaves unlabeled runs unscored, and reports precision, recall and FPR with Wilson intervals and effectiveness_validated=false.
proof_purpose: None (measurement): rule and injection effects measured on a frozen, leakage-free corpus.
note: G1 keeps a pinned corpus of captured agy transcripts for regression and A/B scoring of control rules, with labels read only after predictions.

name: Scenario DSL with fires and not-fires expectations
statement: Forty YAML scenarios script prompts, shell runs with exit codes and output, writes, edits and final messages, render them to a synthetic transcript, and assert which rules must fire, must not fire, and a maximum level, identically across two runs.
proof_purpose: None (regression): each control rule fires on its positive scenarios and stays silent on honest negatives.
note: G1 adds an agy-format scenario DSL (hook payloads plus transcript lines) to regression-test its Stop controller, revisit detection and false-DONE counting, including honest-failure negatives.

name: Implementation-agnostic conformance suite
statement: A stdlib-only runner invokes any implementation as a command, independently recomputes the hash chain, checks head, row count, token totals, must-fire and must-not-fire rules, contract state, progress grade and cross-agent verdict equality, and a v2 suite requires exact golden seals while 8 tampering mutations must exit non-zero.
proof_purpose: G1's receipt and ledger format is reproducible by an independent recomputation, and forged, stale or tool-origin evidence cannot produce a receipt.
note: G1 ships golden agy cases and an independent verifier for its ledger and receipts, plus a mutation suite (tampered goal, tool-origin intent, revision gap, false pass, unknown field) that must all be rejected; run it on every agy upgrade.
novelty: duplicate-of:T1 receipt-binding completion gate (adds an independent verifier and a mutation suite)

name: Offline replay, gap sampling and human labels
statement: Past transcripts are re-run through the same engine in audit mode and bucketed into progress, exploration, waste and other with 'would have intervened N times', spans the rules missed are sampled for human labels, labels are scored by majority consensus with Cohen's kappa, and real failure spans can be rebuilt into replay tasks when restorable by hash.
proof_purpose: None (developer-side measurement).
note: If used, replay captured agy transcripts offline to tune Stop-continuation thresholds; keep labels out of every runtime path.

name: Hook latency benchmark with server cross-check
statement: An isolated benchmark sends a cold first prompt then n warm PreToolUse calls, cross-checks the daemon's received-call counts so fast fail-open replies never count as passes, reports p50/p95/p99/max, and a light hook binary without CLI, SQLite or SDK imports cuts p95 from 21.2 ms to 8.7 ms on one host.
proof_purpose: Measurement: G1 hook latency distributions on this host fit agy's timeouts with margin, since a G1 PreToolUse timeout blocks the call.
note: G1's host-contract re-test ensemble invokes each hook via 'sh -c' from the hooks.json directory, reports p95 with an interval against agy's timeout, and fails the re-test if fail-closed hooks approach it.

name: Pre-run denies that police wasted runs
statement: Several PreToolUse denies stop wasteful but harmless runs: an identical failing verification on an unchanged workspace, a rejected unknown command rerun, a return to an already-failed token structure, a full suite after a small change, an unprobed long run, a rerun of a check with valid evidence, and source edits during an external-cause freeze.
proof_purpose: none
novelty: duplicate-of:T1 stagnation and oscillation detection (as deny gates)

name: Effort, time and cost advisories
statement: A family of advice-only detectors polices effort: read-only streaks (20 reads or 10 minutes), verify-to-produce ratio (4:1 in 20 events), test bloat (60+ lines and 3x code), verify after docs-only changes, repeated reviews, serial triage (10 cycles), flaky UI races, post-completion sleeps, session length tiers (2 h/10M and 4 h/30M tokens), idle spend, spend velocity, and an external iron-laws audit after every write.
proof_purpose: none

name: Advice-then-block ladder with human release
statement: Signals carry hand-set confidences (below 0.5 never delivered), one primary per event with a 5-event cooldown, and a heuristic rule turns from advice into a deny only after acknowledged advice for the same (revision, rule, kind, target), under a 3-block cap, unless the user released it; user false-positive marks also raise thresholds by 50% per 3 marks up to 2x.
proof_purpose: none

name: Optional LLM drift judge
statement: Every 15 tool events, with an accepted contract and no gap, an optional model (Anthropic haiku by default, or an OpenAI-compatible or loopback endpoint) labels recent activity on_track, side_quest or drift, and two drift labels raise an L2 advisory, with cost reserved before each call.
proof_purpose: none
novelty: duplicate-of:vesperchant 3-tier hooks (Stop audit with a fast judge model)

name: Text heuristics for shell, scripts and contracts
statement: Shell commands are classified (verify, produce, explore, mutating, unknown) by stage-splitting and regex/word lists, heredoc and embedded Python/Node bodies are parsed for writes and executions, masked exit codes are inferred from output, and natural-language 'forbid' entries become rules by substring ('test', '테스트', 'dependenc').
proof_purpose: none; G1 detects mutation by tree hash instead of parsing commands

name: Per-session hash chain and seal
statement: Each completed analysis is serialized into canonical redacted rows (paths and test names hashed), chained with SHA-256(prev||0x00||row), and summarized by a seal, but rows are deleted and re-inserted per analysis, the head lives in the same database, and there is no anchor or pending journal.
proof_purpose: none beyond T1
novelty: duplicate-of:T1 hash-chained append-only ledger with head anchor, pending journal and crash recovery

name: Resident per-user daemon behind a socket
statement: A long-lived per-user daemon (spawned by the first hook, flock-guarded, idle exit) holds all session state and serves hooks over a 0600 unix socket that accepts any same-UID peer, with an optional shared budget across linked parent/child sessions.
proof_purpose: none

name: Ownership-proven rollback and passing-point snapshots
statement: A file is agent-owned only if its post-write hash equals the content implied by the write tool input applied to the pre-write content and nobody changed it since; owned files are snapshotted at each passing check and can be restored through a preview whose plan id must still match at apply time.
proof_purpose: Bytes of the agent-owned files at the moment receipt R passed (loss-of-work prevention).
note: If adopted, store receipt-bound trees as git objects under a G1-owned ref outside the agent's reach, verify hashes on read, and derive ownership from G1's own pre/post hashes rather than tool-argument replay.

name: Typed probability-only decision API
statement: A decision is one state text plus named typed questions, and the model may only return a probability distribution over options the caller supplied, never free text.
proof_purpose: none (a closed output space limits what a judge can say but proves nothing)
note: If G1 ever consults a model judge in the measurement layer, restrict it to closed typed questions with fixed option keys so its output cannot carry instructions, and log answers only as measurement rows.

name: Small local judge as hook-time veto
statement: Running the only phone-plausible size, Kev-0.8B, inside PreToolUse or Stop to flag risky commands or false completions is not supported by the repository's own evidence.
proof_purpose: none
note: n/a: keep every PreToolUse and Stop decision deterministic; see KEV-03 for the only plausible (offline) variant.
novelty: duplicate-of:vesperchant 3-tier hooks (Stop audit with a fast judge model)

name: Offline veto-only triage classifier for audits
statement: A Kev model fine-tuned on G1's own receipt-derived labels could, off the hook path, rank archived sessions for extra deterministic re-audits without ever certifying or suppressing anything.
proof_purpose: none; at most it orders an offline re-audit queue
note: Derive labels only from G1 receipts (DONE claimed with vs without a receipt, including withheld-evidence twins), train off-device, confirm on a locked holdout, and use the score solely to order an offline deterministic re-audit queue; it never grants, denies or suppresses.

name: Paired cluster bootstrap with full recomputation
statement: Every comparison is a candidate-minus-reference delta on the same items, with a 95% percentile interval from resampling whole record groups within each source and recomputing nonlinear statistics in every draw.
proof_purpose: that the difference between two injected-rule variants, or two agy versions, on the same task fixtures has a 95% interval excluding zero
note: Run each fixture under both arms, store per-fixture outcome vectors, and compute the paired delta CI by resampling fixtures (all repeats of a fixture move together); write the CI into the measurement receipt, never into the authority path.

name: Pre-registered CI-bound rule with tri-state verdict
statement: A study's panels, primary criteria (lower bound above zero), guard criteria (non-inferiority margins on upper bounds) and ranking are committed as JSON before any run, and the verdict is computed mechanically as pass, fail or incomplete.
proof_purpose: that a measurement verdict (adopt an injected rule, accept a host fact) follows a rule fixed and hashed before any outcome was seen
note: Store each measurement spec (arms, fixtures, primary and guard criteria on CI bounds, rank) as a hashed record in G1 state before running; compute pass/fail/incomplete mechanically, with any missing read yielding incomplete.

name: Spec validation: every criterion has computed evidence
statement: A registered spec is refused if a criterion or rank path names an unknown panel or metric, if a report-only panel is read by a criterion, or if a panel computes nothing.
proof_purpose: that every acceptance criterion of a task contract or measurement spec maps to at least one computed check (no zero row in the coverage matrix)
note: At contract or spec registration, require every criterion to reference an existing deterministic check id and forbid report-only checks from gating; refuse the contract otherwise (G1's zero-row rule).

name: Locked holdout read once, enforced in code
statement: Test partitions need an explicit flag, a locked read for a named candidate is refused a second time, and an interrupted read is completed only by an explicit, recorded request.
proof_purpose: that a confirmation result for a rule or injection variant comes from fixtures never used to select it
note: Keep a hash-pinned holdout fixture set; the measurement runner records each (candidate, holdout) read in the ledger, refuses a second read, and labels reads of gate-failing candidates as exploratory.

name: Retire unsound instruments; past verdicts stand
statement: A benchmark found unsound as a gate is deleted and listed with its reason, date and last round, every later read is refused, and verdicts already computed from it remain the record.
proof_purpose: that no current G1 measurement depends on a probe already shown to be noise or mislabelled
note: Maintain a retired-probe list in G1 state (probe id, reason, date, last measurement that used it); the runner refuses retired probes while historical receipts keep their results.

name: Size guards to resolution; audit reliability
statement: A guard is meaningful only if the suite can resolve its threshold, so small panels are pooled and an instrument whose scores show near-zero split-half correlation across many checkpoints is removed.
proof_purpose: that a host-contract re-test or A/B probe can actually distinguish the effect size it gates on
note: Before a probe gates anything, repeat it on unchanged G1 and agy versions, compute split-half agreement and interval width, and gate only on pooled probes whose width is below the registered margin.

name: McNemar paired sample-size planning
statement: The number of paired items needed to detect a given change at a target power is computed before generating data, and after a run the observed interval says whether more volume could ever make the effect significant.
proof_purpose: that a planned agy re-test batch is large enough to detect the registered change (for example a drop from the measured 3-of-8 false-completion rate)
note: Before each host-contract or A/B measurement, compute the paired session count from baseline discordance and the minimum effect; refuse underpowered batches and record the plan in the measurement spec.

name: Withheld-evidence twins scored on confident answers
statement: Records whose deciding evidence was removed are scored not on accuracy but on how often the model still answers with >=0.9 confidence, paired against intact control twins.
proof_purpose: the rate at which the agent claims completion when G1 withheld or blocked the verifying evidence, versus the intact twin task
note: Build twin fixtures (intact vs the same task with the verifying tool call denied by G1) and measure the share of DONE claims on the withheld twin with a paired interval; use it as the primary metric for Stop-hook and injection A/B tests.

name: Present/absent option pairs expose shortcuts
statement: The same question is asked with a 'none of these' option once with the true option present and once with it removed, so a model that ignores the evidence answers the same way in both.
proof_purpose: that an injected rule makes the agent report 'blocked / cannot verify' when, and only when, the completion path is actually missing
note: Pair fixtures where a completion path exists vs is removed (required file absent, tool denied); the expected outcome differs only by that fact; count paired errors in A/B tests.

name: Code-labelled minimal pairs with ablation checks
statement: Generated items are kept only if changing exactly one sentence flips a code-computed label, removing any evidence sentence makes the label undetermined, and removing any filler leaves it unchanged.
proof_purpose: that each G1 deterministic check reacts to exactly the fact it claims to prove (flips on the deciding fact, invariant to filler)
note: Generate workspace-state pairs differing in one fact (a failing test, a missing artifact, a stale tree hash) and assert in G1's own CI that the gate flips exactly on the deciding fact and ignores filler edits.

name: Certificate-carrying fixtures re-derived before use
statement: Each generated record carries its rule tree, atoms, facts and label, and a checker recomputes the label from the certificate and verifies that a pair changes exactly one fact.
proof_purpose: that every measurement fixture's expected outcome is reproducible from its own stored certificate, not from a human or model label
note: Store with each fixture a certificate (setup commands, expected check vector, deciding fact) and re-derive the expected vector before every run; refuse fixtures whose certificate does not reproduce.

name: Planted single-error items for mutation testing
statement: A proposed answer is either exactly right or carries one plausible planted error from a per-task catalogue, with the label computed by an exact solver.
proof_purpose: that G1's completion gate rejects any receipt or claim carrying a single planted defect (wrong digest, stale tree hash, missing artifact, wrong test count)
note: Mutation-test the authority path: from a valid receipt generate one-defect variants from a named defect catalogue and require the completion gate to reject every variant while accepting the original.

name: Held-out templates and canonical structures
statement: Generalisation is measured on surface templates and rule structures never used in training, with structures deduplicated under commutativity and De Morgan normalisation.
proof_purpose: that an injected rule's measured benefit holds on task wordings and structures not used while writing it
note: Split A/B fixtures by template and task structure; author injected rules against development templates only and report effects on held-out templates.

name: Execution fingerprint recorded with every read
statement: Every report records package versions, device, dtype and the kernel implementations the outputs depend on, and reads are paired bit-for-bit only within one fingerprint.
proof_purpose: which agy version, model id, hook-file hashes and device produced a measured host fact, so two re-tests are compared only when comparable
note: Each host-contract re-test receipt carries agy version, model id, both hooks.json hashes, PRoot and Android build; comparisons across fingerprints are reported as drift, never as treatment effects.

name: Factorial drift attribution: code versus dependencies
statement: When repeated reads disagree, old and new code are each run under old and new dependency kernels on the same inputs, separating code drift, dependency drift and nondeterminism.
proof_purpose: whether a change in measured agy behaviour comes from G1's code, the agy/model version, or run-to-run variance
note: On any host-contract drift, rerun the probe as a 2x2 (previous/current G1 commit x previous/current agy where installable) plus a same-configuration repeat, and record the attribution in the measurement ledger.

name: Refuse results if evaluator code changed
statement: A trial hashes all source files at start and refuses to rank its result if they changed during the run, and a resumed evaluation is refused if any evaluator file differs.
proof_purpose: that a measurement result was produced by one fixed version of G1's hook and check code
note: Hash G1's hook scripts, both hooks.json layers and the fixtures before and after each measurement batch (the agent can rewrite hooks.json for the next session) and discard the batch on any change.
novelty: duplicate-of:T1 completion gate binding the current source and tree

name: No partial scores; count every rejection
statement: A read is valid only if every requested record and question was evaluated, and any rejected or failed record is counted and listed rather than silently dropped.
proof_purpose: that a measurement's denominator equals the registered fixture set (timed-out and crashed sessions are counted, not dropped)
note: Measurement receipts carry requested, completed and failed session counts; a batch with any unaccounted session is incomplete and cannot pass a criterion.

name: Refuse over-length input instead of truncating
statement: An input longer than the context is refused with its exact size and the limit, and truncation happens only when explicitly enabled and is then reported on every response.
proof_purpose: that G1's injected fact blocks and the evidence its checks read are complete, or that truncation is explicit
note: Cap SessionStart/PreInvocation injectSteps by bytes; if the canonical fact block would exceed the cap, inject an explicit 'N of M facts shown, full list at <path>' marker rather than cutting silently, and never feed truncated evidence to a gate.

name: Untrusted text cannot forge control delimiters
statement: Caller text is rewritten so it can never produce the special tokens that mark state, question, option and decision boundaries.
proof_purpose: that text quoted from tool output or files inside a G1 injection cannot imitate G1's trusted fact markers
note: Wrap G1 facts in a per-session nonce marker and escape any occurrence of the marker grammar inside quoted untrusted text before injecting.

name: Child-process probes with marker-line stdout
statement: Risky capability checks run in a fresh child process with a timeout and suppressed core dumps, and only a prefixed marker line from its stdout counts as the result.
proof_purpose: that a hook's stdout carries exactly G1's decision JSON (empty means no decision, {} means deny) even when helper tools print banners or crash
note: Hook scripts run verification helpers as children with captured stdout and timeouts, parse only a nonce-prefixed result line, and themselves print a single JSON object or nothing.

name: Worst-case admission bound; stop when unmeasurable
statement: Before any launch the worst-case cost of everything running plus the new job is compared with the authorization, and the session stops if current spend cannot be read.
proof_purpose: that a measurement batch of agy sessions cannot exceed its registered call or time budget
note: The measurement runner computes max sessions x max turns x timeout before starting and refuses when the bound exceeds the registered budget or when usage cannot be read.

name: Autonomous session proposes, never confirms
statement: An unattended research session may launch registered work and compute read-outs, but confirmation reads are printed as commands for a deliberate step and never executed by the session.
proof_purpose: that no completion or confirmation is issued by the agent itself
note: Already G1's model: the agent only produces candidate work; completion is issued solely by G1's own verifier run and receipt.
novelty: duplicate-of:T1 verification that the harness runs itself

name: Leases with staleness derived from measurements
statement: Each long attempt is written to a ledger before it starts and holds a heartbeat lease, and the stale threshold is derived arithmetically from the longest measured blocking operations.
proof_purpose: that G1's timeouts (hook budget, Stop wait, lease staleness) are justified by measured worst cases rather than guesses
note: Derive every G1 timeout from recorded maxima of measured agy and hook durations plus explicit margins, and store the derivation next to the constant.
novelty: duplicate-of:T1 single active task with pending journal

name: Scripted probes re-measure platform semantics
statement: When a platform behaves unexpectedly, a seconds-long probe reproduces the behaviour and the resulting constant cites it.
proof_purpose: that each measured agy hook fact (fail-closed PreToolUse, {} means deny, at most 10 Stop continues, layer order) still holds for the installed agy version
note: Keep one scripted probe per host fact; rerun the probe suite when the agy version or hook hashes change, and stop relying on any fact whose probe fails.

name: Published numbers must trace to reports
statement: Every number printed in the README and model cards is listed with the report file and key path it comes from, and CI fails when the printed digits differ from the source value.
proof_purpose: that any figure the agent reports at completion (tests passed, files changed) equals the corresponding field of G1's receipt
note: At Stop, extract numeric claims next to known keys from the final message and compare them with the bound receipt; a mismatch or a claim with no receipt returns continue with the exact discrepancy. Bind by key, not by mere presence.

name: Single canonical home lint per rule
statement: A CI test lists rules that may be implemented in exactly one file and fails on any regex match elsewhere.
proof_purpose: that each G1 fact (receipt hash, ledger append, deny decision, tree hash) is produced by exactly one implementation
note: Add a lint table to G1's tests: only the ledger module appends, only the gate module prints PreToolUse decisions, only one module computes the tree hash.

name: Differential parity replay against previous version
statement: A refactor is accepted only when the old code (from a worktree) and the new code produce bit-identical outputs on the same inputs.
proof_purpose: that a change to G1's hook code changes no decision on the recorded corpus of hook inputs unless the change is declared
note: Record every hook stdin G1 receives (redacted), replay the corpus through the previous and new hook versions in a scrubbed environment, and require identical stdout decisions except registered differences.

name: Pin third-party agent instructions by hash
statement: Skills installed from other repositories are recorded with source, path and a computed content hash in a lockfile.
proof_purpose: that rule or skill files G1 injects are byte-identical to the versions G1 approved
note: Keep the sha256 of every rule file G1 may inject in the global root-of-trust; refuse to inject a file whose hash differs and record the mismatch.

name: Hash-pinned exclusions applied to both arms
statement: Items can be excluded from a comparison only through a registered list whose sha256 is checked, and the same rows leave both sides.
proof_purpose: that an A/B result was not shaped by dropping inconvenient sessions after seeing outcomes
note: Measurement specs may name an exclusion file only by hash, registered before the run; the runner removes those fixtures from both arms and reports the count.

name: Freeze thresholds on fresh data
statement: A decision threshold for an error budget is selected on a separate calibration set and applied unchanged to the final test, with the empirical envelope stated as no guarantee.
proof_purpose: that G1's control thresholds (the displacement or oscillation cut-off that ends Stop continuations) are validated on sessions not used to choose them
note: Choose control thresholds on development fixtures, freeze them with their hash in the spec, and report their behaviour on a fresh holdout before deployment.

name: Matched placebo and re-read baseline controls
statement: A candidate must beat a matched control that received the same extra training without the intervention and the unchanged parent re-evaluated now, not an old report.
proof_purpose: that an injected rule's effect comes from its content, not from extra tokens or a newer host or model run
note: Every A/B of injected content includes a length- and position-matched placebo injection arm and a same-day no-injection baseline, all on identical fixtures.

name: Ensembles admitted only on paired evidence
statement: Averaging over option rotations reduced order flips, while averaging two training seeds gave no separated gain, so ensembles are kept as options with paired intervals rather than assumed to help.
proof_purpose: whether repeating a host-contract probe or an agent run k times narrows the measured interval enough to justify its cost
note: Treat repeated agy runs as an ensemble only in measurement: aggregate per-fixture outcomes across repeats, keep the repeat count only if paired evidence shows a narrower estimate, and permute injected-rule order across repeats to measure order sensitivity.

name: Fixed canary probe detects isolation leaks
statement: A fixed sibling question containing a secret code is placed next to real questions, and any movement of their answers beyond 0.001 fails the mechanism gate.
proof_purpose: that content G1 injects in one session (ephemeralMessage) or one hook layer does not leak into later sessions, transcripts or memory
note: In host-contract re-tests, inject a per-run nonce canary via SessionStart or PreInvocation and search the next fresh session's transcript and memory files for it; any hit invalidates the ephemerality assumption.

name: Validated envelope via non-inferiority buckets
statement: A capability is claimed only up to the largest length bucket whose paired difference from the reference bucket has a lower bound within a pre-set margin, with every record answered.
proof_purpose: up to which session length or transcript size a G1 control (Stop continuation, injection) is shown not to degrade
note: Bucket A/B fixtures by turn count or transcript bytes; publish the largest bucket whose paired lower bound stays within the margin as G1's validated envelope and flag sessions beyond it.

name: Held-out temperature fit with leakage refusal
statement: One temperature is fitted by minimum NLL on held-out datasets, reported with an out-of-fold group-disjoint estimate and bootstrap interval, and fits on data sharing sources with training are refused unless the override is recorded.
proof_purpose: none currently; relevant only if a probabilistic signal enters G1's measurement layer
note: If a probabilistic signal is ever introduced, fit its calibration only on task families disjoint from those used to design it, and store fit-set hashes and any override reason with the parameter.

name: Inject computed facts, not computation requests
statement: Arithmetic the model does badly (day counts between dates) is computed deterministically and appended to the input as plain sentences, which raised deadline-policy accuracy.
proof_purpose: none new; it is supporting evidence for injecting G1-computed facts (pass/fail vector, Hamming distance to goal) instead of asking the agent to derive them
note: PreInvocation injects the current acceptance pass/fail vector and distance to goal as computed facts, never as instructions to compute them.

name: Repeat target name for irreversible publish
statement: Publishing to a public repository requires naming it twice, private is the default, and an existing public repository is refused for private uploads.
proof_purpose: none
note: n/a: G1's existing deny/force_ask risk gate covers irreversible commands; repetition defends against human slips, not an adversarial agent.

name: Transcript-derived knowledge graph as memory
statement: Earlier agent sessions are distilled nightly into a private notes repository that agents search before re-deriving history.
proof_purpose: none
note: n/a: G1 continues from its own facts only; at most such notes could be an untrusted hint that is never read as state.

name: Resident local decision server with cache
statement: One process holds the checkpoint, batches queued requests on a single model thread, and caches the state prefix so repeated documents pay only for question rows.
proof_purpose: none
note: n/a: G1 hooks stay short-lived processes; if a judge were ever run for offline measurement it would need a key, no CORS and its own process lifecycle.

name: Disclose every arm tried and negatives
statement: Every round reports all arms with their failed criteria, selects one candidate per size, and logs negative findings with evidence so they are not repeated.
proof_purpose: how many injected-rule variants were tried before one was adopted (multiple-comparison context for its measured gain)
note: The measurement ledger records every variant evaluated, its verdict and failed criteria; adoption receipts cite the number of variants tried.

name: N-gram contamination screen against fixtures
