statement: The Gemini prompt demands intent classification before any tool call and forbids implementation without an explicit request, and criteria written after implementation are an anti-pattern, but both rely on the model obeying.
proof_purpose: Every workspace mutation happened under an already-registered contract hash, so criteria could not be written after the work.
note: While no active G1 contract exists, PreToolUse denies mutating tools (file writes, run_command outside an allowlisted read-only set) with a reason explaining how to register a contract; read and search tools get empty output (native behavior).

name: Adversarial class taxonomy for harness E2E
statement: Nine trigger-mapped adversarial classes (malformed input, prompt injection, cancel/resume, stale state, dirty worktree, hung commands, flaky tests, misleading success output, repeated interruptions) must be probed or marked not applicable with a reason.
proof_purpose: G1's host-contract E2E suite covers each failure class that can fake or lose completion, especially misleading success output and repeated interruptions.
note: Use the taxonomy as a checklist for G1's own E2E and host re-tests (false DONE after a blocked call, interrupt mid-verification, stale receipts after a tree change), measured with the ensemble/CI lane.

name: Transcript-mtime activity clock, report-only
statement: A running node's liveness is the mtime of its child's transcript log, surfaced as 'quiet for N minutes' after 10 minutes but never used to cancel or fail anything.
proof_purpose: none in the authority path; a measurement-lane liveness signal for deciding whether a Stop continuation is worth spending
note: Read agy's transcript_full.jsonl mtime and size at Stop as a measurement input (stall vs progress) alongside the receipt vector; never fail or complete a contract from it.
novelty: duplicate-of:T1 stagnation and oscillation detection (as a measurement input)

name: Steer or revive a node's live child
statement: send steers a running child in place or revives a finished resident child with its context, moving a failed node back to running, but is refused for completed or cancelled runs and for one-shot agents.
proof_purpose: none
note: (c) REJECT: G1 builds no steering verb; a steered or revived lane simply produces new work that needs new G1 receipts; only the rule that a completed contract cannot be revived is kept (OMO-07).

name: Executed evidence grants; model review only withholds
statement: Final approval is computed in exactly one function, which returns false unless Stage-1 executed checks ran and all passed; every model stage (semantic, consensus, reward-hacking) can only withhold approval.
proof_purpose: Completion cannot result from any model output: a task is complete only if every check G1 executed passed and no veto fired.
note: The Stop gate computes complete = (all contract checks executed by G1 passed and bound to a receipt) AND (veto set empty). Judge outputs are typed as veto-only inputs, and no schema field or code path lets them contribute an approval. Port the exhaustive 'no combination of model verdicts approves without executed evidence' test as a G1 conformance test.

name: Tri-state acceptance; skipped check is not evidence
statement: Each Stage-1 result is classified once as EXECUTED_PASS, EXECUTED_FAIL or NO_EVIDENCE. A skipped or never-run check is never evidence, so outcomes are APPROVED, REJECTED or UNVERIFIED.
proof_purpose: In every receipt, absence of executed verification is distinguishable from a pass.
note: Receipts carry an executed flag per check. Any check that has executed=false or is missing output leaves the task UNVERIFIED (still open), never complete. 'Skipped' must never render as pass in projections either.

name: Aggregate verdict recomputed from literal per-check results
statement: A stored aggregate 'passed' flag is never trusted: it is reconciled, failing closed, to the conjunction of every check's literal True, and an empty checklist never counts as all-passed.
proof_purpose: A receipt's summary verdict can be derived from its per-check results and cannot contradict them.
note: When G1 reads or replays a receipt, it recomputes the summary from the per-check tuples (exit code, expected output digest). A receipt whose stored summary differs is rejected, and an empty check vector is never 'all pass'.

name: Judge-reported reward-hacking risk as veto
statement: The Stage-2 semantic LLM is told to look for hardcoded outputs, test-only branches and placeholder logic and to report a reward_hacking_risk; a value of 0.7 or more withholds approval, but an omitted field defaults to 0.0.
proof_purpose: none (it can only add a veto; it proves no fact)
note: If G1 keeps a judge, it should be veto-only and fail closed: a missing or unparseable verdict counts as a veto, bounded by the Stop continuation budget. Worker artifacts go to the judge as nonce-delimited quoted data, and a judge pass never counts toward completion.
novelty: duplicate-of:vesperchant 3-tier hooks Stop audit with a fast judge model

name: Advisory multi-model consensus and deliberative jury
statement: Stage 3 runs a 2/3 vote across models, or one model with three role prompts when no OpenRouter key is set, plus a deliberative advocate/devil/judge mode that nothing in production calls; the vote can only withhold, and reviewer independence is a vendor label that gates nothing.
proof_purpose: none
note: Not in the authority path. Ensembles may appear only in G1's measurement harness.

name: Agent-writable check config, interpreter and PATH
statement: Stage-1 commands come from .ouroboros/mechanical.toml inside the evaluated tree; if the file is absent an LLM writes it, and it is never re-detected. The commands run with the checkout's .venv/bin first on PATH, so the agent under evaluation can redefine or shim its own grader, and any executed 'python -c pass' counts as evidence.
proof_purpose: none
note: Lesson: check definitions, interpreters and runner config live in G1's root-of-trust store outside workspacePaths and are pinned by hash. PreToolUse denies writes to the contract's protected paths, and G1 never resolves executables through the workspace PATH or venv.

name: Allowlist and operator filter for check commands
statement: Commands loaded from config must use an allowlisted executable and contain no shell operators or absolute/home paths, and python may run only as -m on stdlib or declared modules.
proof_purpose: A contract check command is a single argv with no shell composition.
note: At contract admission, reject any check command that is not a plain argv (no shell operators, no workspace-relative interpreter) and record the resolved binary hash (see OUR-22).

name: Grader command never reaches the worker
statement: Each AC's verify_command and output_assertion are withheld from every worker prompt, retry and host-dispatch payload; the worker sees only its expected_artifacts and a note that the harness verifies independently.
proof_purpose: The agent could not tailor its output to the check text, because that text never entered its context or any file it can read.
note: Check definitions live only in G1's root-of-trust directory outside workspacePaths and are never sent through injectSteps. PreToolUse denies any tool call whose arguments reference that directory or the G1 ledger. Injected context names only AC ids and required artifacts.

name: Sanitized retry hints instead of raw grader output
statement: Retry guidance is built from missing artifacts, sanitized verifier output and trace facts, with every encoding variant of hidden values removed longest-first; output tails and the names of failing claims still reach the worker.
proof_purpose: Stop-continuation reasons cannot leak the hidden check.
note: Build Stop 'continue' reasons only from structured fields G1 owns: failing AC ids, the pass/fail vector, Hamming distance and artifact names. Never echo raw check stdout/stderr, so no redaction list is needed.

name: Process-local opaque Seed handle vault
statement: For plugin dispatch, the raw Seed stays in an in-memory vault keyed by an opaque handle that is bound to one session and consumed once; a server restart invalidates the handle and evaluation then fails closed.
proof_purpose: none
note: Use a root-of-trust file store outside the workspace instead (OUR-08).

name: Held-out oracle cases frozen before work
statement: Before the worker starts, a read-only constructor model writes per-criterion oracles with visible and held-out cases. Held-out values are never written to disk or shown to the worker, the per-attempt gate uses visible cases only, and held-out cases run once at terminal verification. A package PASS from these model-authored oracles accepts a criterion even over a legacy rejection.
proof_purpose: The work satisfies inputs the agent never saw.
note: G1 may keep user- or G1-authored hidden cases in the root-of-trust store and run them at Stop. Model-generated hidden cases may only veto; they are never the sole passing evidence for an AC row.

name: Checks must fail on base, pass after
statement: A reproduction check is admitted only if it fails, with its own structured failure signature, on a fresh copy of the base checkout. A check that already passes on base, or whose held-out cases all pass on base, is excluded as non-discriminating, and a preservation check must pass on base.
proof_purpose: The check discriminates: it fails on the pre-task tree and passes on the delivered tree, so the work caused the pass.
note: When a task contract is registered, G1 snapshots the base tree and runs each AC check on a copy. A check is admitted only if it fails with its declared signature (reproduction) or passes (preservation). An AC row with no admitted discriminating check is a zero row, and the contract is rejected.

name: Canary proves the check exercises its target
statement: A test command is trusted only if it exits 0 on two base copies and fails after its target file is replaced with bytes that no language parses.
proof_purpose: The check is not vacuous: its result depends on the file it claims to test.
note: For each AC check that names target files, G1 runs a one-time canary at admission: it corrupts the target in a scratch copy and requires the check to fail. The canary result is recorded in the admission receipt.

name: Pre-existing tests rerun from base bytes
statement: Base tests that pair with or import changed modules run twice on the base and once on a copy of the candidate, in which those tests and their conftests are restored to base bytes and the worker's pytest config is neutralized. A test that passes stably on base but fails twice on the candidate is a veto.
proof_purpose: Pre-existing tests, in their original bytes, still pass against the new code, so deleting or editing tests cannot hide a regression.
note: At Stop, G1 verification also runs the pre-task test files, restored from the base snapshot, against a copy of the candidate tree. A test that passed stably on base and now fails is a veto. Errors in this check block completion, and no candidate-written exemptions are accepted.

name: Per-check exclusion with coverage recomputation
statement: A role violation or indeterminate result excludes only that check. Coverage is then recomputed, so a criterion keeps authority only while some admitted check still covers it, and one replacement model call targets the uncovered criteria.
proof_purpose: After exclusions, every acceptance-criterion row of the coverage matrix still has at least one admitted deterministic check.
note: Build G1's coverage matrix exactly this way (AC x admitted checks, recomputed after exclusions), but reject the contract on any zero row instead of falling back. A replacement check is a new contract version, not a silent patch.

name: No evidence becomes unverified success
statement: When transcript verification is unavailable, when the verify gate times out or cannot start, or when neither the check package nor the legacy verifier has evidence, the AC or criterion is kept successful and labelled unverified, and a worker can trigger the timeout path.
proof_purpose: none
note: Keep the 'preserve work' intent by recording the work in the ledger as UNVERIFIED and leaving the task open. For completion, timeouts, missing transcripts and unavailable verifiers count as FAIL, and they consume Stop budget.

name: Typed claims checked against tool-call transcript
statement: The worker must emit a fenced JSON evidence record (files_touched, commands_run, tests_passed). The terminal self-report is excluded by identity, and each claim must be backed by structured tool calls; otherwise the verdict is FABRICATION_SUSPECTED, unless every gap is a recognized EVIDENCE_FORM_MISMATCH.
proof_purpose: Every claimed command corresponds to a host-recorded tool call that succeeded.
note: G1 does not ask the agent for claims. It records its own PostToolUse facts (tool, args digest, exit status, call id). If the agent's final message claims tests or commands, G1 cross-checks the claim against those facts only to label FABRICATION vs FORM_MISMATCH in the continuation reason.

name: Narration and stdout accepted as evidence
statement: Several support tiers accept text the model controls: assistant narration or echoed stdout can back files_touched, regexes over worker-produced output can back tests_passed, and a 'functional tier' accepts any workspace script that exits 0, even on prose ACs.
proof_purpose: none
note: Lesson: G1 evidence is limited to host-recorded tool events and checks G1 ran itself. Assistant prose and the content of tool stdout are never evidence of completion.

name: Harness replays commands in isolated copies
statement: The harness re-runs up to three allowlisted transcript commands in a fresh copy of the workspace, with an environment built from scratch and under the sandbox. A replay counts only if it exits 0 without timing out, its exit matches the transcript's, and no pre-existing file's SHA-256 changed.
proof_purpose: The check G1 ran passed on an isolated copy of the exact tree without changing any pre-existing file.
note: Reuse this runner shape for G1's own contract checks at Stop: copy the tree, use a scratch environment and the sandbox where available, take SHA-256 of pre-existing files before and after, and judge by exit code only. Record the tree digest, argv, binary hash, exit code and output digests in the receipt.

name: Narrowing options and environment disqualify evidence
statement: Any option or environment assignment that selects, excludes or reconfigures tests disables claim linkage, for example pytest -k/--deselect/-p/-c, PYTHONPATH, JEST_* or go test -run. Configuration carried inside the workspace, such as pytest.ini addopts or conftest.py, is explicitly not detected.
proof_purpose: The check ran the full declared test set, not a narrowed subset.
note: G1 runs contract checks with a fixed argv and isolated runner configuration, using an explicit config file from the root of trust. Runner-config files in the workspace (pytest.ini, conftest.py, jest.config.*) are either part of the protected contract scope or restored from base when pre-existing tests run.

name: Probed write and network sandbox, fail-closed
statement: Commands the controller runs on its own authority are confined: Landlock ABI 3 or later plus seccomp and a network namespace on Linux, sandbox-exec on macOS, AppContainer on Windows. A per-process mutation-matrix probe runs first, and nothing runs if confinement or network isolation is unavailable; however, the sandbox can be switched off and that state is not recorded in receipts.
proof_purpose: A verification run could not write outside its copy or reach the network.
note: Probe once per host. If confinement is available, confine G1's check runs. Either way, record the sandbox backend and state in the receipt so a receipt from an unconfined run can be told apart, and never display confinement that was not applied.

name: Hash-pinned check executables, allowlisted environment
statement: Check interpreters are pinned by realpath plus SHA-256 and re-hashed from an O_NOFOLLOW descriptor right before exec (fexecve on Linux). The verify shell is sealed by realpath, SHA-256 and a capability probe, and replay and check environments are built from an allowlist rather than copied.
proof_purpose: The check ran with exactly the executable bytes recorded at admission, in an environment G1 constructed.
note: Contract admission records the SHA-256 of each check executable. At Stop, G1 re-hashes before exec (fexecve or O_NOFOLLOW where possible), builds the environment from an allowlist, and writes the binary hash and environment digest into the receipt. It never prepends a workspace venv or bin directory to PATH.
novelty: duplicate-of:T1 verification that the harness runs itself in a scrubbed environment (adds binary-hash pinning at exec time)

name: Tree digest brackets every write-capable step
statement: The workspace content digest is taken before and after any model step with write authority, such as the level coordinator. The model's own 'fixed it' summary is explicitly not proof, any change forces re-verification of work already accepted, and an unreadable digest fails closed.
proof_purpose: The tree that was verified is the tree delivered; nothing changed between verification and completion.
note: Each verification receipt records a tree digest, and G1 recomputes it at completion; any PostToolUse write after the receipt invalidates it. The digest scope comes from the contract in the root of trust, never from an agent-editable .gitignore.
novelty: duplicate-of:T1 completion gate binding the current source and tree (adds before/after bracketing of each actor)

name: One-to-one call-id correlation, fail-closed
statement: A tool event counts only when its start is correlated by call id with its own successful completion: duplicate starts cannot share one completion, a malformed error bit cannot be laundered by a 'completed' status, and correlation conflicts fail closed. The IOJournal that records these pairs swallows append failures.
proof_purpose: Each recorded tool result belongs to exactly one tool call that G1 saw being requested.
note: PreToolUse logs (conversationId, stepIdx, tool, args digest), and PostToolUse must match exactly one open entry; unmatched or duplicated results are not evidence. An append failure makes that step non-evidence for completion while staying fail-open for the agent.

name: Content-addressed evidence handles and set membership
statement: Evidence journal entries get content-addressed handles: a SHA-256 over kind, payload and source event ids. The deliver gate accepts a claim only if every cited (fact, chunk) pair belongs to the harness's set and the claim's terms appear in the cited text, but in production it only observes.
proof_purpose: A receipt cites its evidence by hash, so any edited evidence no longer matches its handle.
note: Keep only the handle scheme: every observation G1 stores in the ledger gets sha256(kind, payload, source ids), and completion receipts list the handles they rely on.

name: Every criterion needs a deterministic check
statement: Before a run, every acceptance criterion must declare either a verify_command or an explicit per-AC verify_exemption_reason, but the default mode only warns, and an unreadable config also falls back to warn.
proof_purpose: Every acceptance-criterion row of the contract has at least one deterministic check.
note: G1's contract check only blocks and fails closed: a zero row (no admitted check) rejects the contract. An exemption removes that AC from what completion may claim, and the receipt lists it.

name: Content-derived per-AC keys, random seed id
statement: Each AC gets a semantic key: SHA-256 of its description, verify_command, artifacts and assertion, truncated to 16 hex characters. The Seed id, however, is a random uuid, and Seed YAML on disk is trusted on load and on resume.
proof_purpose: An AC and its check are the same ones that were admitted; any edit produces a new AC identity.
note: Keep T1's contract hash and add per-AC keys = sha256(AC text, check argv, expected artifacts) so receipts bind each row's identity. Never accept an identity from a mutable file without re-hashing.
novelty: duplicate-of:T1 immutable task contracts with a contract hash

name: Recorded decision valid only for exact Seed
statement: Formal evaluation reuses a recorded check-package decision only if its package was frozen for the exact Seed digest and the decision names the Seed's criteria in Seed order; anything else is no evidence, never a pass.
proof_purpose: A verification result is applied only to the exact contract it was produced for.
note: T1 already does this. Keep the rule 'a mismatch is no evidence, never a pass' explicit in G1's receipt check.
novelty: duplicate-of:T1 completion gate binding the receipt sequence and hash

name: Spec-controlled and fail-off verification switches
statement: A Seed can opt out of verify-by-default with execution_mode: legacy, which accepts every root AC on self-report. Plugin dispatch silently downgrades verify-by-default, and the check-package switch treats unparsable environment values and unreadable config as 'off'.
proof_purpose: none
note: Lesson: verification policy comes only from G1's root of trust and is immutable per task. No contract field can weaken it, and unparsable or unreadable safety settings resolve to the strict mode.

name: Workspace-sourced config cannot change execution
statement: A project-local .env, which travels with a cloned repo, may not set executable paths, runtime selectors, permission modes, preload hooks, package-manager or module-resolution variables, git process controls, the sandbox switch or the verify shell; only home and global sources are trusted.
proof_purpose: Every policy value in force came from the global root-of-trust file, not from files the agent can write in the workspace.
note: Treat .agents/hooks.json and any G1 config in the workspace as untrusted. The global ~/.gemini/config/hooks.json is the root of trust, and workspace hooks may only add denies. At SessionStart, G1 verifies its policy digest against the global anchor.

name: LLM-scored ambiguity gate with bypasses
statement: Interview completion and Seed generation are gated on ambiguity = 1 - sum(weight x LLM clarity) <= 0.2. Deterministic code only clamps and applies floors, and several paths skip the gate: a force flag, a plugin path that accepts a caller-supplied score, a magic answer prefix that closes the interview unscored, and a typed-evidence alternative that is never wired in.
proof_purpose: none
note: Not adopted. At most it is a measurement signal in G1's A/B harness.

name: Answer provenance from forgeable text prefixes
statement: Answer provenance is decided by bracketed prefixes in the answer text: [from-code], [from-repo], [from-research] and [from-data] count as observations, and everything else, including [from-auto] machine answers, carries user-confirmed authority.
proof_purpose: none
note: Lesson: G1 derives provenance only from the hook channel (event type, conversationId, stepIdx), never from tags inside model or tool text.
novelty: duplicate-of:vesperchant 00-instinct trusted channel versus data channel

name: LLM answers its own interview questions
statement: In ooo auto, an answer-refiner LLM ('You answer Socratic interview questions on the user's behalf') replaces canned answers. It runs on the same backend that scores ambiguity, and lateral 'stagnation concretization' text is pushed into the transcript to lower the score.
proof_purpose: none
note: Not adopted.

name: Regex A-grade rubric with self-laundering repair
statement: The deterministic A-grade gate treats an AC as observable if it has a verify_command or its prose matches keyword/regex hints, and the bounded repairer rewrites failing ACs into a boilerplate sentence that the same regex accepts.
proof_purpose: none
note: Lesson: G1's contract check counts only admitted executable checks per AC (OUR-12, OUR-26), never text patterns.

name: Auto marks COMPLETE at dispatch
statement: ooo auto reaches COMPLETE as soon as the run starter returns a handle, and a passing static LLM Seed-QA verdict alone sets complete_verified.
proof_purpose: none
note: Lesson: in G1, 'complete' exists only as the output of the Stop gate with a bound receipt. Dispatch or a judge pass is never completion.

name: Generational spec rewriting by Wonder and Reflect
statement: 'Gets smarter on its own' concretely means that each generation one LLM (Wonder) asks what is still unknown and another (Reflect) patches the goal, constraints, AC wording and ontology, while the executor rewrites workspace code; the harness never rewrites its own prompts, skills, agents or code and keeps no cross-run lesson memory.
proof_purpose: none
note: Not adopted. G1 treats any change to the spec as a new task contract.

name: QA judge pass ends loop as completed
statement: The Ralph loop checks 'qa passed' (an LLM score >= 0.80) before the evolve step's action, so a judge pass ends the loop as completed even when the deterministic convergence gate returned 'continue'; when QA is skipped, reaching max generations can also report completed.
proof_purpose: none
note: Lesson for G1's Stop controller: a judge score may only add a 'continue' reason (a veto), never end the continuation chain as success. The only success exit is the deterministic gate.

name: Convergence needs full verdict coverage
statement: The evolution outcome gate converges only with full Seed-AC verdict coverage, final approval, a passing run verdict, no regression and a validator receipt. Ontology similarity >= 0.95 alone yields the non-success ONTOLOGY_STABLE, and per-AC rows may veto approval but never mint it.
proof_purpose: Stopping because nothing changes is distinguishable from completion; completion needs a verdict for every AC row.
note: G1's Stop controller has distinct terminal reasons: complete, stagnant, oscillating, budget-exhausted. Only 'complete' requires the full AC pass vector, from a fresh G1 run on the final tree, with no carried-forward verdicts.

name: Period-2 oscillation, plateau and repetition detection
statement: Stop detectors include period-2 oscillation (N~=N-2 and N-1~=N-3), a score plateau (|delta| < 0.01 over 3 generations), >= 70% repeated questions, a SHA-256 over structured QA findings that repeats across a window, and strictly decreasing QA grades. The 4-pattern StagnationDetector library is not wired into production.
proof_purpose: The continuation loop has returned to an earlier pass/fail state, so further continues are not making progress.
note: Apply the period-2 rule and the findings-hash idea to G1's own pass/fail vector (Hamming distance and exact revisits of a vector), never to similarity of model text.

name: Loop budget and policy snapshotted durably
statement: The automatic Ralph generation budget is clamped to 1..10 and is snapshotted, together with the auto-evolve decision, when evaluation is enqueued, then durably bound to the lineage so later config changes cannot rewrite replay; explicit Ralph requests outside 1..10 are rejected.
proof_purpose: The continuation budget in force for a task is the one recorded when the task was admitted.
note: Bind the maximum number of Stop continuations (at most agy's 10) and the policy digest into the task contract at admission. Stop reads the budget from the ledger, not from live config, and out-of-range values are rejected, not clamped.
novelty: duplicate-of:T1 bounded loops (adds a durable budget snapshot at admission)

name: Cooperative cancellation, zero-disables caps, uncounted failures
statement: Watchdogs cancel cooperatively; the generation safety timeout and the MCP tool timeout default to 0 (off); failed generations reuse their number and never count toward the 30-generation cap; rewind resets the cap; and hard token/dollar caps are explicitly rejected.
proof_purpose: none
note: Lesson: every G1 bound is hard and counted (failed turns consume budget), cancellation reaps process trees, and 0 never means unlimited.

name: Day-old model findings reused without revalidation
statement: Interview advisory lanes reuse findings that other sessions published within a rolling 1-day window (up to 20 per lane), explicitly without re-establishing that a finding still holds.
proof_purpose: none
note: Not adopted.

name: Model-built checks and verdicts that certify
statement: Outside the veto-only pipeline, models build or deliver the checks that certify. The evolve spec verifier passes an AC when LLM-extracted regex assertions match the source and the agent claims a pass. A decomposition-attestation LLM certifies that children cover their parent, so the parent succeeds when all children do. Plugin-mode evaluation returns a host subagent's free-text verdict as final.
proof_purpose: none
note: Lesson: G1 may let a model propose a check, but a proposed check gains authority only after deterministic admission (OUR-12, OUR-13), and a model-authored check may only veto.

name: Retry-driven model, effort and harness escalation
statement: On retries the orchestrator escalates model tiers (frugal, standard, frontier) and effort, walks Routing D one candidate route per classified failure (at most 128), and may redispatch a failing AC once to a different runtime; 'downgrade after 5 successes' and the N-version tournament are not wired.
proof_purpose: none
note: Not adopted.

name: One-winner guard tables for terminal events
statement: Session start, session terminal and per-(generation, root) final acceptance are each appended in a single BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction together with a guard-table insert. The acceptance row is keyed by a SHA-256 of the full payload, so a different digest raises an error instead of overwriting.
proof_purpose: A task completes at most once, and with exactly one receipt digest.
note: The ledger's completion record is unique per task id. A second completion with a different receipt digest is a hard conflict surfaced to the next session, not an overwrite.
novelty: duplicate-of:T1 completion gate binding the receipt sequence and hash (adds an exactly-once guard)

name: Journal reducer re-derives decisions, never more favourable
statement: The check-package journal accepts only closed record schemas allowed by a phase-transition table, runs the same reducer on write and on replay, and re-derives each recorded status from the recorded observations, refusing any decision more favourable than those observations support.
proof_purpose: Every stored verdict can be reproduced from stored G1 observations, and none is more favourable than they support.
note: On replay (at SessionStart and Stop), G1 folds ledger records through a closed-schema transition table and recomputes each completion verdict from the observation records it references. A mismatch marks the task UNDECIDABLE, which blocks completion, rather than trusting the stored verdict.

name: Unchained event log with wall-clock order
statement: The SQLite events table is append-only only by convention: there are no triggers, hash chain or MAC. Replay orders by (timestamp, random UUID) while cursors use rowid, malformed rows are skipped on replay, and one UPDATE exists. Checkpoints silently start fresh if every level is corrupt, and deleting every boundary record makes the run read as 'off'.
proof_purpose: none
note: Keep T1's hash chain plus a head anchor outside the workspace so that 'no ledger' and 'deleted ledger' can be told apart. Order by append sequence, not wall clock.
novelty: duplicate-of:T1 hash-chained append-only ledger with head anchor (this is a weaker form)

name: Database-clock lease with self-fencing single writer
statement: Generation ownership uses a 300 s lease acquired under BEGIN IMMEDIATE and measured on the database clock. The owner fences itself at half the lease, expired leases are reclaimed in two phases, and every owned write checks the fencing token and inserts the event in one transaction.
proof_purpose: At most one writer appended to the task ledger at a time, so receipts are never interleaved.
note: If G1's global and workspace hook layers can append concurrently, guard ledger appends with a flock or SQLite BEGIN IMMEDIATE lease and check a fencing token inside the append transaction. An expired owner is never taken over implicitly.

name: Boot-id process identity and flock leases
statement: A session owner's liveness is proven by a held flock plus a persisted (boot_id, pid, start_ticks) identity that rejects PID reuse and processes from a prior boot; sessions idle for an hour without a live lease are cancelled at server start.
proof_purpose: A recorded process owner is the same process, not a recycled PID.
note: Record (boot_id, pid, start_ticks) for every process G1 spawns or tracks, and check that triple before reaping a process or declaring an owner dead.
novelty: duplicate-of:T1 process-tree reaping (adds an identity that is safe against PID reuse)

name: Resume authority is process-local
statement: A fresh process can rebuild a session's status from the event store but cannot resume the work: execution authority belongs to the process that started it, a new process gets 'process-local resume unavailable', and status reconstruction ignores failures reading related events by default.
proof_purpose: none
note: Lesson: every piece of G1 authority (task, budget, receipts) can be reconstructed from the ledger alone.

name: Policy sealed per run, drift refused
statement: Each run seals its verification policy (run_verify_commands, exec_sandbox_enabled, verify timeout, verify-shell identity, retries, decomposition) into a versioned execution-semantics contract that resume validates exactly, and the executor re-checks the code identity of the verifier, dispatcher and coordinator before each effect.
proof_purpose: The receipt was produced under exactly the verification policy the task was admitted with.
note: At admission, G1 hashes its active policy (hooks.json files, check-runner version, sandbox state, budgets) into the task contract and into every receipt. A policy-digest mismatch at Stop blocks completion until a new task contract is admitted.

name: Extension trust keyed to tree digest
statement: A UserLevel plugin is trusted by (source, identity, canonical tree hash), and the firewall recomputes the tree hash before every invocation, failing closed with trust_subject_changed if it differs; the verify shell's identity is captured the same way.
proof_purpose: The hook scripts and check runner executing now are byte-identical to the ones the root of trust approved.
note: The global root-of-trust file records the SHA-256 of every G1 hook script and of the workspace hooks.json. Each hook invocation, or at least SessionStart, recomputes them. On a mismatch, PreToolUse denies mutating tools and the Stop gate refuses completion, because the agent can rewrite hooks.json for the next session.

name: Advisory fail-open hooks, no PreToolUse/Stop
statement: Ouroboros' host hooks are SessionStart (PyPI update notice), UserPromptSubmit (keyword-to-skill injection via additionalContext) and PostToolUse on Write|Edit (an mtime-based 'drift' notice). All of them exit 0 on failure, none is a PreToolUse or Stop gate, and the repo-local hook commands fall back to $PWD for the script root.
proof_purpose: none
note: Lesson: G1 hook commands use absolute paths under the root of trust, never $PWD or a workspace-relative script root. Injection hooks stay fail-open; gates stay fail-closed.

name: Veto hooks fail closed, observe hooks fail open
statement: The plugin tool-call hook contract separates an intercept scope, which may veto and fails closed by default, from an observe scope, which may only watch and fails open; the firewall treats a nonzero intercept result as a block.
proof_purpose: A crashed or timed-out gate never lets a tool call through, and a crashed observer never blocks one.
note: T1 already has this rule. Map it onto agy: PreToolUse gates print deny or nothing (never allow, and {} counts as deny), and injection hooks are fail-open.
novelty: duplicate-of:T1 fail-closed gates and fail-open projection

name: agy driven headless with full skip-permissions
statement: When Ouroboros drives Antigravity, it runs `agy -p <prompt> --dangerously-skip-permissions [--model]` with the prompt in argv and reads plain-text stdout that has no structured tool events. It translates tool restrictions into prompt prose, forces bypass on every orchestrated runtime, parses stdout JSON-first (so the model can forge events), skips binary-identity checks, and the check-package constructor refuses agy.
proof_purpose: none (host facts for G1's agy adapter)
note: Facts for G1's agy adapter: tool restrictions stated in the prompt are not enforcement, so G1 must deny in PreToolUse. G1 takes tool evidence from hook stdin and transcriptPath, never from agy stdout. Re-test these claims against agy 1.1.27 before relying on them.

name: Host text quarantined from failure classifiers
statement: In host-dispatch mode, a failure reported by the host is kept as data and the terminal message content is replaced with a fixed string, so host text such as 'usage limit reached' cannot steer the engine's recovery classifiers; empty or non-substantive submissions are rejected.
proof_purpose: No control decision (pause, retry, budget) was triggered by text the model wrote.
note: G1 classifies outcomes only from hook event fields and the exit codes of checks G1 ran. Model and tool text goes into the ledger as quoted data and is never pattern-matched to choose a control action.
novelty: duplicate-of:vesperchant 00-instinct trusted channel versus data channel

name: Paired counterbalanced A/B experiment harness
statement: A manual canonical harness runs paired arms in x/y, y/x, x/y order from a frozen ledger, with preflight hashes of the source tree, expected.yaml and model config. A deterministic smoke oracle grades each arm, the decision is a vote count with no statistics, and the only committed run is inconclusive because all pairs were invalid.
proof_purpose: none in the authority path; in measurement it would show whether an injected rule changes outcomes
note: Reuse the shape for G1's A/B tests of injected content: paired counterbalanced arms, preflight hashes that include the grader file, and a deterministic oracle. Add exact sign or McNemar tests with confidence intervals and pre-registered sample sizes, and count pipeline failures as outcomes.

name: Anti-skip assertions, positive controls and audit canaries
statement: The tests guard against vacuous passes: CI fails if named native tests were skipped, a test asserts that Landlock really exists on the Linux CI runner, a real outbound connection serves as a positive control before network denial is asserted, a CPython audit hook with planted canary files (and a negative control) proves the controller reads only declared inputs, and real LLM spawning is blocked in tests.
proof_purpose: A passing G1 conformance suite actually exercised each mechanism (no vacuous skip), and a positive control showed the check could fail.
note: Every G1 host-contract re-test and conformance test includes a positive control (the bad action succeeds without G1), a negative control (G1 blocks it), and an assertion that the environment supports the mechanism, so an unsupported environment fails the test rather than skipping it.

name: Bot review approval satisfies required review
statement: The repository's one required approving review can be satisfied by the ouroboros-agent bot, and agent handoff docs say to merge only after the bot approves, so a model's verdict is part of the merge path.
proof_purpose: none
note: Not adopted.

name: SKILL.md on-demand prompt modules
statement: Each of the 28 patterns ships as a self-contained Markdown skill whose frontmatter description is the model-facing trigger and whose body has Goal, Workflow, Rules and a self-run Verification section.
proof_purpose: none
note: REJECT as a G1 mechanism: skills stay the host's native capability (P2). Anything G1 must guarantee goes through hooks, and any habit G1 wants delivered goes through measured PreInvocation injection.

name: Reach-bias: hide action-biasing reflexes
statement: Skills whose mere presence would bias the agent toward an action (commit, publish, demolition, chronic self-doubt) are user-invoked only, so the model cannot reach them and no skill can chain one user-invoked skill into another.
proof_purpose: none for authority; measurement fact that injected text without action-inviting reflexes does not raise the false-completion rate
note: INJECT-content rule: G1's injected text never contains action-inviting reflexes such as 'commit when done' or 'reply DONE'; variants are A/B-tested on the false-completion rate in the measurement layer, never treated as a guarantee.

name: Unpinned global install with auto-updating symlinks
statement: Installation is one npx skills@latest command for every agent, run from an elevated shell when needed so skills are symlinked and auto-update, and users are invited to paste it into an agent and say 'set this up for me'.
proof_purpose: none
note: REJECT: G1 installs only vendored, hash-pinned hook files through its own one-time bootstrap and never lets upstream text flow into agent context. The 'enumerate each name, never --all' habit is kept in the bootstrap (PTH-19).

name: Claude Code plugin manifest and shadow installs
statement: A .claude-plugin/plugin.json registers all 28 skill paths so a clone can load as a Claude Code plugin, which the skills CLI cannot see and re0-upgrade must detect as a 'shadow install'.
proof_purpose: none
note: REJECT: G1 has no plugin surface; its only delivery is the two agy hooks.json layers.

name: Bare-text CLAUDE.md pointer to AGENTS.md
statement: AGENTS.md is the one canonical instruction file for agents and contributors (README is human-only), and Claude Code is pointed at it by a CLAUDE.md whose entire content is the text 'AGENTS.md'.
proof_purpose: none
note: REJECT: G1 delivers its contract text through SessionStart/PreInvocation injection computed from its own state; any instruction-file copy is an optional mirror that G1 never relies on.

name: Fail-open SessionStart notice hook
statement: A SessionStart command hook injects a discovery notice into the model's context, exits 0 with valid JSON on every path, stays silent when it cannot tell, and throttles itself to once per 24 hours with a stamp file.
proof_purpose: none (projection only; never part of the authority path)
note: INJECT: G1's SessionStart projection is wrapped so every path prints a valid injectSteps object or nothing, and it recomputes its text from the ledger each session instead of throttling by clock; agy already treats SessionStart as fail-open.
novelty: duplicate-of:T1 fail-closed gates and fail-open projection

name: Relay-cue phrasing with explicit do-not-act clause
statement: The injected notice is phrased as a cue for the model to relay to the human, plus an explicit prohibition on acting ('do NOT run /re0-upgrade or install anything yourself'), chosen because a relay test reportedly surfaced it on about two thirds of first turns.
proof_purpose: none for authority; measurement fact 'injected variant A yields rate p (with CI) against variant B'
note: MEASURE: treat the wording of injected text as an A/B variable in G1's measurement layer (ensembles with confidence intervals), for example a declarative ledger fact plus an explicit 'do not claim completion; G1 decides' clause versus the bare fact, scored on the false-completion rate.

name: Compaction-safe idempotent prompt injection
statement: The OpenCode adapter injects the notice at most once per session and skips injection when a rebuilt, post-compaction system prompt already contains the notice marker.
proof_purpose: none (projection hygiene: at most one copy of G1's projection in model context)
note: RESEARCH: measure whether agy ephemeralMessage steps persist or accumulate across PreInvocation calls and context compaction; only if they do, tag the projection with the ledger head hash and skip re-injection when that head is already present.

name: Shared core with thin host adapters
statement: Roster and notice logic live in one shared module that a command-hook adapter (Claude Code, Codex) and a JS plugin adapter (OpenCode) both import, so host differences stay inside the adapters.
proof_purpose: none (structural: keeps agy output shapes and decision semantics out of core semantics, P7)
note: STRUCTURE: G1 core (ledger, contract, gate decisions as pure functions) returns host-neutral verdicts; one agy adapter maps them to agy JSON (empty stdout for no decision, never {} or allow, deny/ask/force_ask, injectSteps, Stop continue) and holds the measured agy facts.

name: State path defined once; retired names tombstoned
statement: The runtime state directory is defined in exactly one module and imported everywhere, and a CI guard fails if the retired home name reappears in shipped runtime or installer prose, with no legacy fallback or migrator by design.
proof_purpose: every G1 component reads and writes the same canonical state root, and no retired or P8-rejected mechanism identifier is present in shipped G1 core
note: ENFORCE in G1's test suite: one constants module owns the state root and ledger paths; a tombstone list of deleted mechanisms is grepped across shipped core and must return zero hits; the ledger carries a schema version and G1 fails closed on an unknown version instead of migrating silently.

name: Guarded copies: exact equality enforced
statement: When a fact must physically exist in several places (units ship alone and there is no build step), the copies are kept and a deterministic CI guard fails on any divergence; where a pointer suffices, copies are replaced by a pointer to one canonical home.
proof_purpose: two copies of one fact are exactly equal; in G1, the G1 entries registered in the global and workspace hooks.json files (and the hook script hashes) equal the set recorded at bootstrap
note: ENFORCE: wherever G1 must duplicate a fact it checks exact equality, never similarity. The global (root-of-trust) PreToolUse hook compares the G1 entries in .agents/hooks.json and the G1 script hashes with the bootstrap record and denies mutating tools on mismatch, which catches an agent that rewrote hooks.json for the next session; facts are kept out of comments, which no guard covers.

name: Strict dual-parser frontmatter gate
statement: Every skill's YAML frontmatter must parse strictly, with unique keys, under both YAML 1.1 and 1.2, because the two hosts that load skills use those parsers and silently drop a skill that one of them misreads.
proof_purpose: each canonical G1 record (ledger entry, contract, receipt, hooks.json) has exactly one interpretation, so the hash that binds it binds one meaning
note: ENFORCE in the ledger library: parse canonical JSON strictly and reject duplicate keys (stock JSON.parse and Python json.loads silently keep the last one), invalid UTF-8 and trailing data before hashing; serialize canonically; validate hooks.json the way agy reads it (camelCase keys); keep a regression test that a duplicate-key record is rejected.

name: Catalog lint: structure, links, orphans, typos
statement: CI checks that every skill has the required sections, a name equal to its directory, registration in plugin.json and README, no deep ../ references, resolvable relative links, reachability from README, and no near-miss skill-name typos.
proof_purpose: none beyond facts G1 already proves
note: REJECT as separate mechanisms; keep only the habit of collecting every violation before failing in G1's own test runner.
novelty: duplicate-of:T1 completion gate that binds artifacts and output digests

name: Gates need negative controls
statement: The guards document that a piped while-read loop runs in a subshell and silently swallows failures (a green gate that cannot fail), yet only one of the six guards ships a test proving it can fail.
proof_purpose: each G1 gate is non-vacuous: a known-bad fixture makes it deny, so a pass from that gate carries information
note: ENFORCE in G1 self-test: every gate (PreToolUse write locks, completion hash and subset checks, ledger chain verification, Stop continuation) ships a negative-control fixture that must produce deny or fail; a gate whose negative control passes is marked untrusted, and the self-test receipt records each gate's hash with its negative-control outcome.

name: Tag-triggered release with exact version gate
statement: A pushed signed tag triggers CI that validates the catalog, requires package.json's version to equal the tag exactly, publishes with npm provenance only if the version is not already published, and creates or edits the GitHub Release idempotently; CI never signs or creates commits or tags.
proof_purpose: a completion is recorded at most once per (task, receipt hash), and only when the receipt-bound identity equals the current identity exactly
note: ENFORCE: G1's completion append is idempotent, so re-running completion for the same task and receipt hash is a no-op rather than a second entry, and the exact check (receipt-bound tree hash equals current tree hash) runs immediately before the append, as version-equals-tag runs before publish.
novelty: duplicate-of:T1 completion gate binding receipt sequence/hash and the current source and tree

name: Never hand-run a harness-owned step
statement: Steps the release workflow owns are never run by hand, not even to rescue a failed run, because a hand-run step drops what the workflow adds (provenance attestation, title convention) while still looking like a good release.
proof_purpose: every receipt and ledger entry was written by G1's own process, not by the agent
note: ENFORCE: PreToolUse denies agent file writes and shell commands that target G1's state directory, receipts, hooks.json files or verifier entry points (exact path match on tool arguments, best-effort for shell strings), and the ledger accepts only hash-chained entries appended by G1, so an agent-authored 'receipt' fails even if a write slips through.
novelty: duplicate-of:T1 verification that the harness runs itself in a scrubbed environment

name: Re-cut a broken tag at the same version
statement: A tag whose message, signature or target the author got wrong is deleted and re-cut at the same version instead of rolling forward, so one version name can denote different tag objects over time.
proof_purpose: none
note: REJECT: G1 identifies receipts, contracts and hook scripts by content hash only; names (tags, versions, task labels) never serve as the binding identity, and a correction is a new ledger entry, never a re-cut under the same identifier.

name: Signed commits and tags as trust boundary
statement: Signed tags and signed, cleaned commits are the human's trust boundary, checked with git tag -v and %G? = G before pushing.
proof_purpose: a ledger head anchor was produced with G1's key and not by the agent, but only if the key is outside the agent's reach
note: RESEARCH: signing the ledger head adds trust only if the key lives outside the agent's OS user (separate user, hardware token, or a keyring that requires presence); otherwise G1 relies on hash chaining plus a head anchor stored where agent tools are denied.

name: Idempotent non-clobbering hook installer
statement: re0-upgrade converges an install by classifying names as stale, missing, present or unknown against a rename table and the catalog, printing a plan, running only the planned commands, retrying a failed item once, and wiring a SessionStart hook only if none already runs the script by any path, after a config backup and without touching foreign hooks.
proof_purpose: after bootstrap each hooks.json layer holds exactly one G1 entry per event with the expected command and script hash, and every foreign entry is byte-identical to before
note: ENFORCE in G1's one-time bootstrap: parse both hooks.json layers, classify entries as g1-current, g1-stale or foreign, rewrite only G1 entries (identified by script hash, not path), back up with the backup hash recorded in the ledger, verify the post-state by exact set equality, and make re-running a no-op; the recorded set feeds the live check in PTH-11.

name: Remote tag-pinned fetch of hook code
statement: The upgrade skill downloads executable hook scripts from raw.githubusercontent.com at the installed version's tag into ~/.re0/ and registers them as SessionStart commands in Claude Code and Codex configs.
proof_purpose: none
note: REJECT: G1 hook scripts are vendored in the G1 repository and pinned by sha256 recorded at bootstrap; G1 never fetches executable hook code at install or run time.

name: Static host matrix versus measured host contract
statement: Hook wiring supports only Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode and skips Copilot CLI, Grok Build and Antigravity CLI, asserting that Antigravity has no session-start event, while README claims the suite runs on any agent including Antigravity.
proof_purpose: the running agy version equals a version whose hook contract G1 has measured, so G1's fail-open and fail-closed assumptions hold for this session
note: ENFORCE: the agy adapter stores the measured hook contract keyed by agy version (events, fail-open/closed behavior, empty-stdout and {} semantics, the 10-continue cap); SessionStart records the observed agy version in the ledger, and the completion gate refuses receipts from a session whose host version has not passed the contract re-test suite.

name: Consent-gated promotional repository star
statement: After a successful upgrade the skill asks once, through the host's structured question tool, whether to star the repository with the user's authenticated gh account, and only an explicitly submitted 'Star repository' choice authorizes the API call.
proof_purpose: none
note: REJECT. Its consent rule (authorization is never inferred from silence, preselection or an adjacent approval) is already implied by G1 deciding each call separately and never printing allow.

name: Gitignored local provenance casebooks
statement: Iteration casebooks and release notes live in a gitignored .re0/ directory described as history and scratch, never shipped and never canonical, yet the repository's design rationales and proofs point into it.
proof_purpose: none
note: REJECT as state: G1's only canonical record is its ledger, and agent-written notes are never read as facts.
novelty: duplicate-of:vesperchant .harness records (history, plans, walkthroughs, handoffs, audits, metrics)

name: Trust the artifact, not the author
statement: A skill must either re-derive the work from what is true now or import outside eyes to test it, because the maker's in-session mind is the worst judge of whether the work is clear and correct.
proof_purpose: none (doctrine)
note: Already G1 doctrine in a stricter form: the artifact is judged by G1's deterministic verification and hashes, never by another model reading it.
novelty: duplicate-of:vesperchant 00-instinct (confirm against a primary source; trusted versus data channel)

name: Restraint: an empty pass changes nothing
statement: A pass that finds nothing to genuinely improve changes nothing, an empty findings list is a valid result, and drift or disagreement must never be invented to justify work.
proof_purpose: a Stop continuation is issued only when the deterministic failing set is non-empty
note: ENFORCE in Stop control: emit continue only when the pass/fail vector contains at least one failing acceptance check; an all-pass vector ends the loop without inventing work, and an unrunnable check is UNKNOWN, never pass. This is implied by G1's Hamming-distance control and costs one explicit test.

name: Edit-safety: assert target, report MISS
statement: Every mutating skill must assert that each edit target exists and report a MISS rather than a silent no-op, edit unicode-safe, replace per occurrence rather than by blanket sweep, and script large structural moves.
proof_purpose: every G1 state mutation was applied against the expected prior state, with no lost update and no silent no-op
note: ENFORCE in G1's own writes: every ledger append names the expected head hash and fails loudly on mismatch (a compare-and-swap precondition complementing T1's head anchor), and a G1 operation that matches nothing returns an explicit MISS that every gate treats as not done.

name: Negatives-as-corpus: archive, never delete
statement: 'Cut' means move to an archive, never delete: failed paths, descoped items, retired cycles and declined contributions are kept as data so later cycles can prove an anti-pattern is gone.
proof_purpose: failed receipts, rejected completions and superseded contracts remain in the hash chain, so no later claim can erase an earlier failure
note: ENFORCE in the ledger: failing receipts, rejected completions and superseded contracts are appended and never rewritten, and re-verification appends a new receipt instead of replacing history.

name: git log as the cross-environment handoff
statement: re0-git rewrites a finished commit's message to a durable-facts-only standard (commit-economy) so a fresh session can continue from git log alone, keeping the tree byte-identical and re-signing the commit.
proof_purpose: none
note: REJECT as a handoff channel; G1 continuity comes from its ledger. The 'tree stays byte-identical' check survives inside the declared-scope invariant (PTH-29).

name: Declared-scope invariant checked by exact diff
statement: Several mutating patterns declare what may change and check it mechanically afterwards: a message-only rewrite must leave the tree byte-identical, a reorder must keep every item and change only positions, a compression must keep every load-bearing claim, and an upgrade may run only the commands its plan named.
proof_purpose: every change made during the task lies inside the contract's declared write scope (the changed-path set is a subset of the allowed set)
note: ENFORCE: the immutable contract declares an allowed path set and G1 snapshots a tree manifest at contract time; PreToolUse denies file-tool writes outside the set (best-effort for shell strings) and PostToolUse journals each mutating call; at Stop the completion gate diffs the tree against the snapshot and requires exact subset membership, otherwise deny.

name: Unknown is not empty: tri-state results
statement: When a probe cannot tell (no skills visible, an unparseable list, an unreachable source, a missing skill), the result is reported as unknown or skipped, never as empty, missing or clean, and an orchestrator states what it skipped and why.
proof_purpose: no gate decision treats an unrunnable, timed-out or unparseable check as pass
note: ENFORCE: every G1 check returns PASS, FAIL or UNKNOWN; in the authority path UNKNOWN denies completion exactly like FAIL, the projection shows it as unknown, and every skipped check is named in the receipt.
novelty: duplicate-of:T1 fail-closed gates and fail-open projection

name: Two independent enumerations must agree
statement: Before acting on an enumeration, re-enumerate by a different method and confirm it surfaces nothing the first missed, and cross-check a tool's report against the on-disk footprint before concluding something is absent.
proof_purpose: the changed-file set used by the scope and tree checks is complete, because two independent enumerators agree exactly
note: ENFORCE: at completion G1 derives the changed set twice, from git status including untracked and ignored files and from a content-hash walk against the contract-time manifest; any disagreement yields UNKNOWN and denies completion.

name: Author never self-assesses
statement: Judgment on clarity, a decision or a validation must come from a separate context-free sub-session that receives only the artifact or an abstract item, never the author's intent, reasoning or negotiation.
proof_purpose: the party that judged completion is not the party that did the work
note: Already G1 doctrine: G1 itself verifies at Stop; model-based fresh-context review is allowed only in the measurement layer (PTH-43).
novelty: duplicate-of:T1 verification that the harness runs itself in a scrubbed environment

name: A deny is never re-litigated in-session
statement: When a user disputes a bright-line exclusion, the pressured session does not re-decide it: the abstract item goes to a fresh context, the appeal and outcome are logged, repeated appeals are surfaced as a signal, and excluded asks are never posed just to see whether they pass.
proof_purpose: a gate decision is a pure function of G1 state and tool arguments, so agent prose cannot change it, and exact repeats of denied calls are counted
note: ENFORCE: PreToolUse decisions read only the ledger and the tool arguments, never the agent's explanation; G1 stores a hash of each denied call and counts exact repeats as revisits that feed the oscillation detector and Stop control.

name: macrothink: convergence is reassurance, never proof
statement: macrothink strips the session's framing, fans out 2-5 same-model fresh reads, reports divergence first, and forbids majority vote, averaging, and calling same-model convergence verified or proved; prism applies the same never-average rule.
proof_purpose: no completion was ever granted on the basis of model agreement
note: Keep only the rule as an authority-path invariant: no count of agreeing model outputs, a judge model included, can satisfy a G1 gate; model ensembles appear only in the measurement layer with confidence intervals. Reject the fan-out.

name: re0-memo: failures become hard gates
statement: re0-memo turns a finished or failed cycle into class-level lessons, anti-patterns and next-cycle gates, prefers hard gates over advice, and checks that a from-scratch agent could avoid the failure from the docs alone.
proof_purpose: every observed G1 failure class has a deterministic regression fixture that fails on the original failure
note: GOVERNANCE: each observed G1 failure (for example the measured 3-of-8 'DONE' replies after a blocked call) becomes a named failure class with a deterministic regression fixture in G1's suite, never just a new injected sentence.

name: re0-merge: default-deny admission of additions
statement: re0-merge declines additive contributions by default, admits new tooling only if it mechanizes a rule already enforced by hand, verifies fixes with a throwaway regression case, keeps contributor authorship, and approves before landing.
proof_purpose: none at runtime; governance: each admitted G1 mechanism names the existing proof obligation it mechanizes
note: GOVERNANCE for P8: a proposed G1 mechanism is declined unless it mechanizes a proof obligation G1 already has and ships with its negative control (PTH-14); the burden is on the addition to show G1 is weaker without it.

name: re0-release: irreversible publication staked separately
statement: re0-release treats the local commit and the public tag-and-push as two separately confirmed moments, stops on any checklist gap instead of guessing past it, and watches the triggered workflow to completion ('confirmed, not assumed').
proof_purpose: no public, irreversible command (push, tag push, publish, release) ran without a native user confirmation
note: ENFORCE: PreToolUse classifies irreversible public commands (git push, tag pushes, npm publish, gh release) and returns force_ask; how force_ask behaves in agy print mode is unmeasured and must be tested first, and completion still rests on G1 observing the outcome itself.

name: re0-plan: never-empty casebook, evidence traces to design
statement: re0-plan creates an iteration folder and its first real file in the same step, so it is never empty, and requires every EVIDENCE gate to trace back to a DESIGN line, so no proof surface exists that the design never asked for.
proof_purpose: the contract's coverage matrix has no zero row (criterion without a check) and no zero column (check that covers no criterion)
note: ENFORCE at contract acceptance: extend G1's coverage-matrix check (acceptance criteria x deterministic checks) to reject zero columns as well as zero rows, and write the contract and its first ledger entry in one journaled step so no task exists without its contract.

name: nba: one next action with done-when
statement: nba reads live cycle state and returns exactly one next action, the cheapest move that clears the binding constraint, framed as where you are, the action, why now and an observable done-when, without executing it.
proof_purpose: none (guidance; the Stop gate, not the reason text, is the enforcement)
note: INJECT through the Stop continue reason: G1 names exactly one failing acceptance check from its pass/fail vector (deterministic tie-break such as contract order) and gives that check's exact command as the done-when, instead of a list or a model-written plan.

name: catchup: state-grounded re-entry briefing
statement: catchup rebuilds a returning human's context from live state rather than conversation memory, anchored at their last touch and ordered as needs-you, changed and new words, with every claim traceable to a file, commit or artifact and 'done' meaning verified done.
proof_purpose: none (projection supporting TW(b) reconstruction)
note: INJECT: G1's SessionStart projection lists the active task, its contract hash, the latest receipt and the delta since that receipt, each line citing ledger sequence and hash, and shows 'complete' only for receipt-bound completions.
novelty: duplicate-of:T1 fail-closed gates and fail-open projection

name: mandela: verifier must not be the designer
statement: mandela audits any validation against eight leakage patterns, including shared hallucination, tautology (a scorer grading buckets it drew) and verifier = designer, and asks whether external ground truth enters independently.
proof_purpose: the checks that produced the receipt are byte-identical to the checks fixed in the contract before work began, so the agent did not author or weaken its own verifier during the task
note: ENFORCE: at contract time G1 hashes every file its checks depend on (tests, fixtures, verifier scripts) as declared in the contract; PreToolUse denies writes to them during the task, and the completion gate at Stop requires their hashes to equal the contract-time hashes, else deny. This makes patterns 4 and 5 mechanical; T1's tree binding alone would bind tests the agent had already weakened.

name: sip: post-change self-check orchestrator
statement: sip is a model-invoked skill that, right after any create or change, runs shower, factchk or mandela, an ssotize audit, detool and re0 on the result, on the stated premise that 'remember to verify' never fires in a fresh session.
proof_purpose: none
note: REJECT the skill. Its own premise, that prompt reminders do not fire, is the case for G1's Stop hook running G1's deterministic verification whenever the agent tries to stop.
novelty: duplicate-of:vesperchant 3-tier hooks (Stop audit with a fast judge model)

name: shower: zero-context cold read
statement: shower hands a fresh, context-free sub-session only the artifact's contents, never a repo path or the author's intent, compares its blind reading with a privately noted intent, treats every mismatch as a defect, and warns that one read is one draw.
proof_purpose: measurement fact: a fresh agy session given only G1's projection reconstructs the active task and next failing check at rate p (with CI)
note: MEASURE TW(b): run N fresh agy sessions that receive only G1's SessionStart projection, score whether each names the right task, contract hash and next failing check, and report the rate with a confidence interval; a regression blocks a G1 release, never agent work.

name: detool: no incidental host nouns in portable text
statement: detool classifies text by role and replaces incidental vendor, model, CLI, path or harness nouns in durable content with the mechanism they mean, while keeping provenance, runbooks and tool-subject claims concrete; durable docs also use generic examples rather than real instances and never model-brand a name.
proof_purpose: G1 core files contain no host identifiers outside the agy adapter
note: ENFORCE in G1's test suite: a deterministic grep over G1 core, excluding the adapter directory, for a host-noun list (agy, antigravity, gemini, agy event and file names) must return zero hits; role judgments stay with human reviewers.

name: re0: rewrite a drifted artifact as v0
